cards.mean: in a complete mess; all over the place
cards.lit: messy sevens and rotten eights: things scattered every which way

use.how: An adjective: predicate, complement after 得 (弄得乱七八糟) or before 的. Said of rooms, writing, things or one's thoughts being in disorder.

near.diff: 一塌糊涂 stresses how bad a result or situation is (考得一塌糊涂); 乱七八糟 stresses disorder and lack of arrangement.

cards.cue: You come home to find your teenager's clothes on the floor, books on the bed and dirty dishes on the desk. How do you describe the room?

ctx.s: 你的房间怎么{乱七八糟}的？快收拾一下。
ctx.en: Why is your room such a mess? Tidy it up.

ctx.s: 孩子们走了以后，客厅被弄得{乱七八糟}。
ctx.en: After the children left, the living room was a total mess.

ctx.s: 他的字写得{乱七八糟}，老师根本看不懂。
ctx.en: His handwriting is all over the place; the teacher can't read it at all.

ctx.s: 抽屉里塞满了{乱七八糟}的东西，找把剪刀都难。
ctx.en: The drawer is stuffed with all sorts of junk; even finding a pair of scissors is hard.

ctx.s: 这份报告的数据{乱七八糟}，你得重新整理一遍。
ctx.en: The data in this report are a mess; you need to reorganise them.

ctx.s: 最近事情太多，我心里{乱七八糟}的，什么都想不清楚。
ctx.en: So much has been going on lately; my head is in a muddle and I can't think straight.

bad.s: 弟弟昨天{乱七八糟}了我的房间。
bad.en: (meant: my brother messed up my room yesterday)
bad.why: It is an adjective, not a verb; you need a pattern like 'made my room messy' (ba ... nong de ...).

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜种类很多，{乱七八糟}，我很喜欢。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant has a wide variety of dishes, which I like)
bad.why: It means a disorderly mess and is a complaint; it cannot praise a wide choice of dishes.

cards.mean: exactly alike, identical
cards.lit: one mould, one shape: as if cast from the same mould

use.how: Predicate or attribute, usually in A跟B一模一样. Said of looks, objects, voices or events that cannot be told apart.

near.diff: 如出一辙 is bookish and compares methods or events, often critically; 一模一样 is everyday and mostly about how things look or sound.

cards.cue: Twin sisters turn up at a party in the same dress with the same haircut, and nobody can tell which is which.

ctx.s: 这对双胞胎长得{一模一样}，我总是认错。
ctx.en: The twins look exactly alike; I always mix them up.

ctx.s: 你的手机跟我的{一模一样}，连颜色都相同。
ctx.en: Your phone is identical to mine, even the colour.

ctx.s: 他画的这只猫和照片上的{一模一样}。
ctx.en: The cat he drew looks exactly like the one in the photo.

ctx.s: “你看，这道题跟昨天考的{一模一样}吧？”
ctx.en: "Look, this question is exactly the same as the one in yesterday's exam, isn't it?"

ctx.s: 二十年过去了，这条老街跟我小时候{一模一样}，一点儿没变。
ctx.en: Twenty years on, this old street is exactly as it was when I was a child; it hasn't changed a bit.

ctx.s: 他说话的语气跟他父亲{一模一样}。
ctx.en: The way he talks is exactly like his father.

bad.s: 这两件衣服有点儿{一模一样}。
bad.en: (meant: these two pieces of clothing are a bit alike)
bad.why: It means completely identical, so it cannot be softened with 'a bit' (you dian er); for partial likeness say 'look a bit alike'.

bad.s: 他{一模一样}他爸爸。
bad.en: (meant: he looks just like his dad)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; the pattern is 'A gen B (zhang de) yi mu yi yang'.

cards.mean: baffling; making no sense at all
cards.lit: no one can name its mystery: nobody can say what is behind it

use.how: Predicate (我觉得莫名其妙), adverbial with 地 (莫名其妙地关机了) or an exclamation. Said of behaviour, events or words with no apparent reason.

near.diff: 不知所措 is not knowing what to do; 莫名其妙 is not understanding why something happened or what it means.

cards.cue: Your friend suddenly gets angry at you over lunch and walks out without a word, and you have no idea why.

ctx.s: 他突然生气了，我觉得{莫名其妙}。
ctx.en: He suddenly got angry, and I was completely baffled.

ctx.s: 你这话说得{莫名其妙}，我听不懂。
ctx.en: What you just said makes no sense; I don't follow.

ctx.s: 手机{莫名其妙}地关机了，怎么也打不开。
ctx.en: My phone switched itself off for no reason and won't turn back on.

ctx.s: 大家都在笑，只有他一脸{莫名其妙}。
ctx.en: Everyone was laughing; only he looked completely lost.

ctx.s: 这条规定真是{莫名其妙}，谁也说不出它有什么用。
ctx.en: This rule is absurd; nobody can say what it's for.

ctx.s: “你干吗瞪我？”“{莫名其妙}，我什么时候瞪你了？”
ctx.en: "Why are you glaring at me?" "What are you on about? When did I glare at you?"

bad.s: 这本小说写得太好了，真是{莫名其妙}！
bad.en: (meant: this novel is so well written, it's simply wonderful)
bad.why: The 'miao' here is not 'wonderful': the idiom means baffling and cannot praise anything.

bad.s: 我{莫名其妙}这件事。
bad.en: (meant: I don't understand this matter)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; say instead that the matter leaves you baffled.

cards.mean: have a good trip (wish to someone setting off)
cards.lit: a following wind all the way

use.how: A farewell wish, alone or after 祝你, said to someone about to leave on a journey.

near.diff: Both are farewells; 一路平安 wishes a safe journey, 一路顺风 a smooth one.

cards.cue: Your friend is leaving tomorrow on a long train journey home. What do you say as you see them off at the station?

ctx.s: 明天你就要出发了，祝你{一路顺风}！
ctx.en: You're setting off tomorrow. Have a good trip!

ctx.s: “我走了，到了给你打电话。”“好，{一路顺风}！”
ctx.en: "I'm off, I'll call you when I get there." "OK, have a good trip!"

ctx.s: 同事们在火车站跟他告别，祝他{一路顺风}。
ctx.en: His colleagues said goodbye to him at the station and wished him a good journey.

ctx.s: 客人们上了大巴，酒店经理在门口挥手说：“祝各位{一路顺风}！”
ctx.en: The guests got on the coach, and the hotel manager waved from the door: "Have a good journey, everyone!"

ctx.s: 妈妈把他送到车站，嘱咐了半天，最后说了句“{一路顺风}”。
ctx.en: His mother saw him to the station, gave him advice for ages, and finally said "have a good trip".

ctx.s: 你们开车回老家，路上慢点儿，{一路顺风}。
ctx.en: You're driving back to your hometown, so take it easy on the road. Have a good journey.

bad.s: 欢迎回来！{一路顺风}！
bad.en: (meant: welcome back, I hope your trip went well)
bad.why: It is said to someone leaving, not arriving; to someone who has just arrived you acknowledge the tiring journey.

bad.s: 祝你生日快乐，{一路顺风}！
bad.en: (meant: happy birthday, all the best)
bad.why: It wishes a good journey only; it is not a general good-luck wish for a birthday.

cards.mean: to talk to oneself
cards.lit: self speaks, self talks: speaking with no one else to hear

use.how: An intransitive verb phrase or adverbial before 道 or a quote. Describes someone speaking aloud with no listener.

near.diff: 喃喃自语 is literary and stresses a low, murmuring voice; 自言自语 is everyday and only says there is no listener.

cards.cue: Alone in the kitchen, your grandmother keeps saying aloud "now where did I put the salt?" though no one is there to answer.

ctx.s: 他一边做饭一边{自言自语}。
ctx.en: He talks to himself while he cooks.

ctx.s: 你一个人在那儿{自言自语}，没事吧？
ctx.en: You're over there talking to yourself. Are you all right?

ctx.s: 老人坐在窗前{自言自语}，好像在跟老朋友聊天。
ctx.en: The old man sat by the window talking to himself, as if chatting with an old friend.

ctx.s: 她{自言自语}道：“明天一定会更好。”
ctx.en: "Tomorrow will be better," she said to herself.

ctx.s: 小孩子玩玩具时经常{自言自语}，这很正常。
ctx.en: Young children often talk to themselves while playing with toys; that's perfectly normal.

ctx.s: 有人觉得{自言自语}是压力大的表现，其实不一定。
ctx.en: Some people think talking to yourself is a sign of stress, but that's not necessarily so.

bad.s: 面试开始了，请你先{自言自语}一下。
bad.en: (meant: the interview is starting, please introduce yourself first)
bad.why: It means talking with no listener, not talking about oneself; an interview calls for a self-introduction.

bad.s: 我们俩在咖啡馆{自言自语}了一下午。
bad.en: (meant: the two of us chatted in the café all afternoon)
bad.why: Two people talking to each other are chatting, not talking to themselves.

cards.mean: to talk utter nonsense
cards.lit: wild talk and eight kinds of rambling

use.how: Verb phrase or predicate (别胡说八道, 完全是胡说八道). A blunt rebuttal of what someone says; too rude for polite or formal settings.

near.diff: 胡言乱语 is incoherent raving, as in a fever or when drunk; 胡说八道 denies that what someone claims is true.

cards.cue: A coworker loudly claims you broke the printer, though you were on holiday all that week. You snap back at him.

ctx.s: 别{胡说八道}了，我根本没说过那种话！
ctx.en: Stop talking rubbish, I never said anything of the sort!

ctx.s: 他明明什么都不懂，还在那儿{胡说八道}。
ctx.en: He clearly knows nothing about it, yet there he is spouting nonsense.

ctx.s: 网上那些{胡说八道}的消息，你千万别信。
ctx.en: Don't believe any of that nonsense going around online.

ctx.s: “听说你要辞职了？”“谁在{胡说八道}？没有的事。”
ctx.en: "I hear you're quitting?" "Who's spreading that rubbish? It's not true."

ctx.s: 这篇文章完全是{胡说八道}，一点儿根据都没有。
ctx.en: This article is pure nonsense, without a shred of evidence.

ctx.s: 小孩子{胡说八道}，您别往心里去。
ctx.en: The child is just talking nonsense; please don't take it to heart.

bad.s: 王教授在会上{胡说八道}了一个很有意思的观点。
bad.en: (meant: Professor Wang put forward an interesting view at the meeting)
bad.why: It is a blunt insult, never neutral 'say'; it cannot describe putting forward a good idea, and is rude about a professor.

bad.s: 他在背后{胡说八道}我。
bad.en: (meant: he spread lies about me behind my back)
bad.why: It takes no object; you cannot use it to mean spreading lies about a person.

cards.mean: to achieve two aims with one action
cards.lit: one move, two gains

story.text: Bian Zhuangzi wanted to kill a tiger, but a servant boy stopped him: two tigers were about to eat an ox, they would fight over it, the smaller would be killed and the larger wounded. If he waited and then killed the wounded one, one action would win him the fame of killing two tigers. He waited, and it happened just so.
story.source: 《史记·张仪列传》（陈轸讲给秦惠王的故事）

use.how: Predicate, often after 真是 or 可谓, or before 的. Approves of one plan or action that brings two benefits at once.

near.diff: 一箭双雕 often describes a calculated move that hits two targets, sometimes against people; 一举两得 is plain approval of a practical choice.

cards.cue: By walking the dog every morning, she gets her own exercise and keeps the dog happy at the same time.

ctx.s: 骑自行车上班，既能锻炼身体，又能省钱，真是{一举两得}。
ctx.en: Cycling to work keeps you fit and saves money: two birds with one stone.

ctx.s: 你帮我练英语，我帮你练中文，这不是{一举两得}吗？
ctx.en: You help me with my English and I help you with your Chinese. Doesn't that work for both of us?

ctx.s: 周末去做志愿者，既帮了别人，又学到了东西，{一举两得}。
ctx.en: Volunteering at weekends helps others and teaches you things too: a double gain.

ctx.s: 把旧仓库改成咖啡馆，既省了拆除费，又多了收入，可谓{一举两得}。
ctx.en: Turning the old warehouse into a café saves the cost of demolition and brings in income: a move that pays off twice.

ctx.s: 听说出差时能顺便看望父母，她觉得{一举两得}，马上答应了。
ctx.en: When she heard the business trip would let her visit her parents too, she thought it was ideal and agreed at once.

ctx.s: 有没有{一举两得}的办法，既不加班，又能按时完成？
ctx.en: Is there a way to kill two birds with one stone: no overtime, and still finish on time?

bad.s: 他先学了英语，后来又学了法语，真是{一举两得}。
bad.en: (meant: he learned English and then French, so he gained two languages)
bad.why: Two separate efforts are not one action with two results; the idiom needs a single act that brings both gains.

bad.s: 我想{一举两得}这个问题。
bad.en: (meant: I want to solve this problem in one go)
bad.why: It takes no object and does not mean 'solve'; it describes a plan or method, not what you do to a problem.

cards.mean: to give up halfway
cards.lit: to stop halfway along the road

story.text: Yue Yangzi left home to study with a teacher but came back after a year because he missed home. His wife took a knife to the cloth on her loom and said that it had been woven thread by thread, and cutting it now would waste it all; stopping his studies halfway was the same. He went back and studied for seven years without returning. The phrase itself is older, from the Doctrine of the Mean.
story.source: 《后汉书·列女传·乐羊子妻》；词语见《礼记·中庸》

use.how: Intransitive predicate, never with an object; the subject is the quitter or the undertaking (他总是半途而废, 项目半途而废). Said of studies, plans and projects.

near.diff: 前功尽弃 stresses that all earlier effort is wasted; 半途而废 stresses quitting before the end.

cards.cue: He trained hard for a marathon for a month, then quit with the race still eight weeks away.

ctx.s: 学外语最怕{半途而废}，每天坚持一点儿就好。
ctx.en: The worst thing in learning a language is giving up halfway; just keep at it a little every day.

ctx.s: 你已经练了三个月了，现在放弃不就{半途而废}了吗？
ctx.en: You've practised for three months. If you give up now, won't you have quit halfway?

ctx.s: 由于资金不足，这个项目不得不{半途而废}。
ctx.en: For lack of funds, the project had to be abandoned halfway.

ctx.s: “我不想学钢琴了。”“做事不能{半途而废}，至少把这首曲子学完。”
ctx.en: "I don't want to learn piano any more." "You can't give up halfway. At least finish learning this piece."

ctx.s: 他减肥总是{半途而废}，坚持不到一个星期。
ctx.en: His diets always fizzle out; he never lasts a week.

ctx.s: 老师在毕业典礼上提醒我们：无论做什么，都不要{半途而废}。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony our teacher reminded us: whatever you do, don't give up halfway.

bad.s: 我们走到{半途而废}的地方，休息了一下。
bad.en: (meant: we stopped for a rest at the halfway point)
bad.why: It means abandoning an undertaking, not the midpoint of a route; for that just say 'halfway' (yi ban).

bad.s: 他去年{半途而废}了大学学业。
bad.en: (meant: last year he dropped out of university)
bad.why: It takes no object; say instead that he gave up his studies halfway, with the studies or the person as subject.

cards.mean: without realising it; unawares
cards.lit: not knowing, not feeling

use.how: Adverbial, often 不知不觉中 or 不知不觉就. Said of time passing or a change happening without one noticing.

near.diff: 潜移默化 is a gradual influence on someone's thinking or character; 不知不觉 is anything happening unnoticed, most often time passing.

cards.cue: You sit down to check your phone for a minute, and when you look up it is dark outside.

ctx.s: 我们聊得很开心，{不知不觉}天就黑了。
ctx.en: We were having such a good chat that it got dark before we knew it.

ctx.s: 他躺在床上看书，{不知不觉}睡着了。
ctx.en: He was reading in bed and drifted off to sleep without realising.

ctx.s: {不知不觉}中，我来中国已经三年了。
ctx.en: Before I knew it, I had been in China for three years.

ctx.s: 跟中国朋友在一起久了，我的口音也{不知不觉}地变了。
ctx.en: After spending so long with Chinese friends, my accent has changed without my noticing.

ctx.s: 你有没有发现，孩子们{不知不觉}就长大了？
ctx.en: Have you noticed how the children have grown up before we realised it?

ctx.s: 逛街的时候，钱{不知不觉}就花光了。
ctx.en: When you go shopping, the money is gone before you know it.

bad.s: 我{不知不觉}这个消息。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't know about this news)
bad.why: It is an adverbial about not noticing, not a verb meaning 'not know'; here you simply need 'did not know'.

bad.s: 她是一个{不知不觉}的人，从来不关心别人。
bad.en: (meant: she is an oblivious person who never cares about others)
bad.why: It describes how something happens, not a person's character; it cannot label someone as oblivious.

cards.mean: wholeheartedly, with undivided devotion
cards.lit: one heart, one mind

use.how: Adverbial (一心一意地做…) or predicate after 对… (对他一心一意). Said of sustained devotion to one task, goal or person.

near.diff: 全心全意 is more formal and often about serving people or a cause; 一心一意 is everyday and also used of loyalty to one partner.
专心致志 is full concentration on the task in front of you; 一心一意 is devotion to one aim, kept up over time.

cards.cue: After years of juggling three jobs, she quits two of them to put all her energy into the one bakery she loves.

ctx.s: 他现在{一心一意}准备考试，别的事都不管。
ctx.en: He is now devoting himself entirely to preparing for the exam and ignoring everything else.

ctx.s: 她对丈夫{一心一意}，几十年从没变过。
ctx.en: She has been completely devoted to her husband, unchanged for decades.

ctx.s: 只要你{一心一意}地做好一件事，就一定会有收获。
ctx.en: As long as you put your whole heart into doing one thing well, you will get something out of it.

ctx.s: 退休以后，爷爷{一心一意}地照顾他的花园。
ctx.en: Since retiring, Grandpa has devoted himself wholeheartedly to his garden.

ctx.s: “你真的想好了吗？”“想好了，我就想{一心一意}地画画。”
ctx.en: "Have you really thought it through?" "I have. I just want to give myself completely to painting."

ctx.s: 这家小店的老板{一心一意}做面条，十年只卖这一样。
ctx.en: The owner of this little shop has devoted himself to noodles, selling nothing else for ten years.

bad.s: 我对这份工作很{一心一意}。
bad.en: (meant: I am very devoted to this job)
bad.why: It cannot be modified by 'very' (hen); use it bare, as a predicate or as an adverbial before the verb.

bad.s: 他{一心一意}地看了一眼手表。
bad.en: (meant: he glanced attentively at his watch)
bad.why: It describes devotion kept up over time, not one brief glance; for close attention use 'carefully' (ren zhen).

cards.mean: may everything go as you wish (a greeting)
cards.lit: ten thousand things, all as you wish

use.how: A set wish, said alone or after 祝你/祝您: 祝您新年快乐，万事如意！ Used at New Year, birthdays and in cards; also in 人生哪能万事如意.

near.diff: 一路顺风 wishes someone a safe journey only; 万事如意 wishes that everything in life goes well.
一帆风顺 is smooth progress in one undertaking or career; 万事如意 is the all-round greeting for every part of life.

cards.cue: You are writing a New Year card to your old teacher and want to wish them well in every part of life. How do you end it?

ctx.s: 新年快乐，祝您身体健康，{万事如意}！
ctx.en: Happy New Year! Wishing you good health and that everything goes your way!

ctx.s: 奶奶过生日，我们一起举杯，祝她老人家{万事如意}。
ctx.en: At Grandma's birthday we all raised our glasses and wished her every happiness.

ctx.s: 贺卡最后，他写了一句：“祝阿姨{万事如意}，天天开心！”
ctx.en: At the end of the card he wrote: "Wishing you all the best, Auntie, and happiness every day!"

ctx.s: 春节拜年的时候，大家见面总要说一句“{万事如意}”。
ctx.en: When people pay New Year visits at Spring Festival, they always greet each other with "may all go well".

ctx.s: 婚礼上，主持人祝新郎新娘白头偕老、{万事如意}。
ctx.en: At the wedding the host wished the bride and groom a long life together and every happiness.

ctx.s: “祝你工作顺利，家庭幸福，{万事如意}！”“谢谢，也祝你全家都好！”
ctx.en: "Wishing you success at work, a happy family and all the best in everything!" "Thanks, and all the best to your whole family too!"

bad.s: 他这次考试{万事如意}，得了满分。
bad.en: (meant: his exam went smoothly and he got full marks)
bad.why: The first half means everything in life; it is a broad wish, not a report that one event went well. Say the exam went smoothly instead.

bad.s: 祝你{万事如意}地通过考试。
bad.en: (meant: I hope you pass the exam smoothly)
bad.why: It is a complete wish on its own, not an adverb for a verb. Wish someone a smooth pass in plain words, or use the idiom by itself.

cards.mean: fully willing, gladly accepting it of one's own accord
cards.lit: the heart content and the feelings willing

use.how: Adverbial (心甘情愿地做) or predicate (我是心甘情愿的). Stresses that a cost, hardship or sacrifice is accepted freely, without being forced.

near.diff: 一厢情愿 is one side's wishful thinking that ignores the other side; 心甘情愿 is freely accepting a cost yourself.

cards.cue: A friend pities you for spending every weekend caring for your sick father. You say nobody forced you: you choose to do it.

ctx.s: 为了孩子，妈妈{心甘情愿}地吃苦。
ctx.en: For her children's sake, the mother willingly puts up with hardship.

ctx.s: 这份工作工资不高，但他做得{心甘情愿}。
ctx.en: The job doesn't pay much, but he does it gladly.

ctx.s: “你周末还去医院照顾爸爸，不累吗？”“累，但我是{心甘情愿}的。”
ctx.en: "You go to the hospital to look after your dad even at weekends. Aren't you tired?" "I am, but I do it willingly."

ctx.s: 没有人逼他，他是{心甘情愿}捐出这笔钱的。
ctx.en: Nobody pressured him; he donated the money entirely of his own accord.

ctx.s: 这是我自己选的路，再苦再累我也{心甘情愿}。
ctx.en: This is the path I chose myself; however hard and tiring it gets, I accept it gladly.

ctx.s: 合同的条件很苛刻，可她为了这个机会，还是{心甘情愿}地签了字。
ctx.en: The terms of the contract were harsh, but for the sake of the opportunity she signed it willingly.

bad.s: 她{心甘情愿}他明天来。
bad.en: (meant: she is happy for him to come tomorrow)
bad.why: It describes one's own readiness to do or bear something; it cannot take another person's action as its object, the way 'hope' can.

bad.s: 他{心甘情愿}地以为她也喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: he fondly imagined that she liked him too)
bad.why: Believing what you wish were true is wishful thinking, a different idiom. This one means freely accepting a cost yourself.

cards.mean: huge crowds of people everywhere
cards.lit: mountains of people, seas of people

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的, describing a place packed with people: 广场上人山人海。 It paints a scene; it does not count things.

near.diff: 成千上万 gives a large number of anything (people, letters, birds); 人山人海 pictures one place packed with a crowd.

cards.cue: On the first day of the national holiday you reach a famous scenic spot and can barely move for the crowds. How do you describe it?

ctx.s: 国庆节的时候，长城上{人山人海}。
ctx.en: During the National Day holiday the Great Wall is packed with people.

ctx.s: 演唱会门口{人山人海}，我们根本挤不进去。
ctx.en: There was a sea of people at the concert entrance; we couldn't squeeze in at all.

ctx.s: “周末去公园吗？”“算了吧，肯定{人山人海}。”
ctx.en: "Shall we go to the park this weekend?" "Forget it, it'll be heaving with people."

ctx.s: 春运期间，火车站里{人山人海}，到处都是拿着行李的旅客。
ctx.en: During the Spring Festival travel rush the station is a sea of people, with travellers and luggage everywhere.

ctx.s: 早知道商场打折时{人山人海}，我就不来了。
ctx.en: If I'd known the mall would be this packed during the sale, I wouldn't have come.

ctx.s: 记者站在{人山人海}的广场上，报道新年倒计时的盛况。
ctx.en: Standing in the packed square, the reporter described the grand New Year countdown.

bad.s: 我们班有{人山人海}的学生。
bad.en: (meant: our class has a great many students)
bad.why: It pictures a crowd packed into one place, not the number of members in a group. Simply say the class has many students.

bad.s: 我家的书{人山人海}，书架都放不下了。
bad.en: (meant: we have so many books the shelves can't hold them)
bad.why: It is only about crowds of people. For a great many things, use an ordinary 'very many' or a different image.

cards.mean: to fall in love at first sight
cards.lit: at one look, the feelings gather on someone

use.how: Predicate, often 对某人一见钟情, or attributive (一见钟情的爱情). Mainly about romantic love; playfully also about an object you love at once.

near.diff: 青梅竹马 is a bond that grew from childhood together; 一见钟情 is love that strikes at the very first meeting.

cards.cue: Your friend met someone at a wedding, talked for five minutes, and has thought of nobody else since. How did it start?

ctx.s: 他在图书馆遇见了她，就{一见钟情}了。
ctx.en: He met her in the library and fell for her at first sight.

ctx.s: 你相信{一见钟情}吗？
ctx.en: Do you believe in love at first sight?

ctx.s: 我父母是在火车上认识的，爸爸对妈妈{一见钟情}。
ctx.en: My parents met on a train; my dad fell in love with my mum the moment he saw her.

ctx.s: 这部电影讲的是两个陌生人在雨中{一见钟情}的故事。
ctx.en: The film is about two strangers who fall in love at first sight in the rain.

ctx.s: 这套房子我一走进去就{一见钟情}，当天就交了定金。
ctx.en: I fell in love with this flat the moment I walked in and paid the deposit that same day.

ctx.s: 与其说是{一见钟情}，不如说是日久生情，他们做了三年同事才在一起。
ctx.en: It wasn't so much love at first sight as love that grew over time: they were colleagues for three years before getting together.

bad.s: 我和他认识十年了，慢慢地{一见钟情}。
bad.en: (meant: over ten years I gradually fell in love with him)
bad.why: It means love at the very first meeting, so it cannot happen slowly over ten years. For love that grows over time, use another phrase.

bad.s: 我第一次见到新老板就{一见钟情}，觉得他很能干。
bad.en: (meant: my first impression of the new boss was that he is very capable)
bad.why: It means falling in love, not forming a good opinion of someone. For a good first impression of a boss, say that plainly.

cards.mean: to be greatly surprised
cards.lit: to 'eat' one big shock: the word for 'be startled' split open by 'big' and 'one'

use.how: Predicate (他大吃一惊) or after 让/令 (这个消息让我大吃一惊). A sudden strong surprise at unexpected news or a sight, good or bad; takes no object.

near.diff: 目瞪口呆 shows the frozen, speechless look of someone stunned; 大吃一惊 simply names the strong surprise.
喜出望外 is delight at unexpected good news; 大吃一惊 is strong surprise at anything, good or bad.

cards.cue: You check the restaurant bill and find it is three times what you expected. What is your reaction?

ctx.s: 听到这个消息，我{大吃一惊}。
ctx.en: I was astonished when I heard the news.

ctx.s: 他打开门，看见满屋子的朋友，{大吃一惊}。
ctx.en: He opened the door, saw a room full of friends and got the shock of his life.

ctx.s: 成绩一向很差的小明这次考了第一名，让老师{大吃一惊}。
ctx.en: Xiaoming, whose marks had always been poor, came first this time, which greatly surprised the teacher.

ctx.s: 医生看了检查结果，{大吃一惊}，马上让他住院。
ctx.en: The doctor was alarmed by the test results and had him admitted to hospital at once.

ctx.s: 结账时一看账单，我们都{大吃一惊}：一顿饭竟然花了这么多钱。
ctx.en: When we saw the bill we were all stunned: one meal had cost that much.

ctx.s: 这家小公司的产品卖到了全世界，令同行{大吃一惊}。
ctx.en: This small company's products are now sold worldwide, much to the astonishment of its rivals.

bad.s: 他从小就{大吃一惊}，什么都怕。
bad.en: (meant: he has been timid since childhood and is afraid of everything)
bad.why: It is one moment of shock at something unexpected, not a lasting timid character. Say he has always been easily scared.

bad.s: 我{大吃一惊}了这个消息。
bad.en: (meant: I was shocked by this news)
bad.why: It takes no object. Put the news first as the cause (on hearing the news, I was...) or make the news the subject with 'made me'.

cards.mean: by every possible means
cards.lit: a thousand methods and a hundred schemes

use.how: Adverbial before the verb it serves: 千方百计地想办法, 千方百计逃避责任. Stresses trying method after method, for good aims or bad ones.

near.diff: 全力以赴 is throwing all one's strength into one task; 千方百计 is trying one method after another to reach a goal.

cards.cue: A boy wants a puppy: he begs, writes letters, offers to do chores and even gets his grandparents to ask. How does he go about it?

ctx.s: 孩子生病了，父母{千方百计}地给他找好医生。
ctx.en: When their child fell ill, the parents tried everything to find him a good doctor.

ctx.s: 为了让我答应，他{千方百计}地讨好我。
ctx.en: To get me to say yes, he tried every way he could think of to please me.

ctx.s: 那只猫{千方百计}想从笼子里跑出来。
ctx.en: The cat tried every trick it could to get out of the cage.

ctx.s: 他{千方百计}逃避责任，最后还是被发现了。
ctx.en: He tried every possible way to dodge responsibility, but in the end he was found out.

ctx.s: 公司正在{千方百计}降低成本，连办公室的灯都少开了。
ctx.en: The company is cutting costs by every means it can; even the office lights are switched on less.

ctx.s: “你们是怎么找到这本旧书的？”“我们{千方百计}地打听，问遍了全城的旧书店。”
ctx.en: "How did you find this old book?" "We asked around every way we could and tried every second-hand bookshop in the city."

bad.s: 这个问题很简单，我{千方百计}就解决了。
bad.en: (meant: the problem was simple and I solved it right away)
bad.why: It implies great trouble and many attempts, so it cannot describe something easy that was done at once.

bad.s: 明天就是决赛了，大家一定要{千方百计}！
bad.en: (meant: the final is tomorrow, everyone must give it their all!)
bad.why: It needs the action it serves after it (by every means, win the match). As a standalone rallying call to give everything, use the 'go all out' idiom.

cards.mean: to go all out, putting everything into it
cards.lit: to set off toward it with all one's strength

use.how: Predicate, often after 要/会/一定: 我们会全力以赴。 Said of a serious task, match or emergency; a pledge of total effort. Takes no object.

near.diff: 尽力而为 is a modest 'I'll do what I can' that leaves room for failure; 全力以赴 pledges everything.
千方百计 is trying many different methods, even to dodge something; 全力以赴 is wholehearted effort on one worthy task.

cards.cue: Before the final, the coach asks whether the team is ready. The captain promises they will hold nothing back.

ctx.s: 明天的比赛，我们一定{全力以赴}。
ctx.en: In tomorrow's match we'll give it everything we've got.

ctx.s: 地震发生后，救援人员{全力以赴}抢救伤员。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, rescuers went all out to save the injured.

ctx.s: 经理问：“这个项目下周能完成吗？”小王说：“我们会{全力以赴}的。”
ctx.en: The manager asked, "Can this project be finished next week?" Xiao Wang said, "We'll put everything into it."

ctx.s: 离高考只剩一个月了，她正在{全力以赴}地复习。
ctx.en: With only a month left before the university entrance exam, she is revising flat out.

ctx.s: 既然决定参加，就要{全力以赴}，不能马马虎虎。
ctx.en: Now that you've decided to take part, you have to go all out, not do it half-heartedly.

ctx.s: 虽然最后输了，但队员们都{全力以赴}了，观众还是给他们鼓掌。
ctx.en: Although they lost in the end, the players had given everything, and the crowd still applauded them.

bad.s: 你放心，这件事我{全力以赴}你。
bad.en: (meant: don't worry, I'll do my utmost to help you with this)
bad.why: It takes no object. Say you will go all out, or that you will go all out to help.

bad.s: 他为了不交作业，{全力以赴}地找借口。
bad.en: (meant: he tried every trick to get out of handing in his homework)
bad.why: It means wholehearted effort on a worthy task. For scheming in many ways, especially to avoid something, use the 'by every possible means' idiom.

cards.mean: it's a deal; that's settled then
cards.lit: one word and it is fixed

use.how: Said on its own or after 那就/咱们 to seal an agreement between people: 好，一言为定！ The other side often answers with 一言为定 too.

cards.cue: Your friend agrees to lend you their bike next weekend if you fix its brakes first. You shake hands on it. What do you say?

ctx.s: “明天早上八点见。”“好，{一言为定}！”
ctx.en: "See you at eight tomorrow morning." "Right, it's a deal!"

ctx.s: 那就这么说好了，下周你请我吃饭，{一言为定}。
ctx.en: So that's agreed: next week you treat me to dinner. Deal.

ctx.s: 爸爸说：“你考到九十分，我就带你去海边。”儿子马上说：“{一言为定}！”
ctx.en: Dad said, "Score ninety and I'll take you to the seaside." His son said at once, "It's a deal!"

ctx.s: 咱们{一言为定}，谁也不许反悔。
ctx.en: Let's settle it here and now, and nobody is allowed to back out.

ctx.s: 两个老板握了握手，说了声“{一言为定}”，合作就这样谈成了。
ctx.en: The two bosses shook hands, said "Agreed," and the partnership was settled just like that.

ctx.s: 上次我们不是说好了“{一言为定}”吗？你怎么又变卦了？
ctx.en: Didn't we say last time it was a deal? Why have you changed your mind again?

bad.s: 这件事我还要考虑一下，{一言为定}。
bad.en: (meant: I need to think about it a bit more, then I'll decide)
bad.why: It seals an agreement right now, so it contradicts still needing time to think. Say you will reply once you have thought it over.

bad.s: 老师在课上{一言为定}地讲了语法。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher explained the grammar decisively)
bad.why: It is not an adverb for firm or clear speaking; it is only a spoken formula for sealing a deal between people.

cards.mean: in high spirits, elated
cards.lit: spirits high and vigour blazing

story.text: In his book of literary criticism, Liu Xie surveyed the styles of earlier writers. Of the poet Xi Kang (Xi Shuye) he said that, being bold and gallant, his writing had lofty inspiration and blazing brilliance. The phrase first described the vigour of a writer's style and later came to mean being in high spirits.

use.how: Adverbial (兴高采烈地跑回家) or predicate (孩子们兴高采烈). Describes lively, visible joy, often of a group, at an outing, event or good news.

near.diff: 得意洋洋 is smug pride in one's own success and often criticises; 兴高采烈 is open, innocent cheerfulness.
喜出望外 is delight at unexpected good news; 兴高采烈 describes the lively, excited mood people show.

cards.cue: On the last day of term, the children pour out of school laughing and shouting, off on their holidays. How do they look?

ctx.s: 放假了，孩子们{兴高采烈}地跑出校门。
ctx.en: School was out, and the children ran out of the gates in high spirits.

ctx.s: 他{兴高采烈}地告诉我，他找到工作了。
ctx.en: He excitedly told me he had found a job.

ctx.s: 球赛赢了，球迷们{兴高采烈}地在街上唱歌。
ctx.en: Their team had won, and the fans sang jubilantly in the streets.

ctx.s: 看大家{兴高采烈}的样子，今天一定有什么好事吧？
ctx.en: Everyone looks so cheerful; something good must have happened today?

ctx.s: 一家人{兴高采烈}地去郊游，没想到半路下起了大雨。
ctx.en: The family set off happily on an outing, but it started pouring halfway there.

ctx.s: 晚会上，同学们{兴高采烈}，又唱又跳，一直玩到深夜。
ctx.en: At the party the classmates were in great spirits, singing and dancing late into the night.

bad.s: 他安静地坐在窗前，{兴高采烈}地看书。
bad.en: (meant: he sat quietly by the window, happily reading)
bad.why: It describes lively, visible excitement, which clashes with sitting quietly. For relish in reading, use the 'with keen interest' idiom.

bad.s: 他考了第一名，就{兴高采烈}地看不起别人。
bad.en: (meant: after coming first he proudly looked down on others)
bad.why: Looking down on others is smug self-satisfaction, a different idiom. This one is innocent cheerfulness with no contempt in it.

cards.mean: with great relish or keen interest
cards.lit: savoury and full of flavour

use.how: After 得 or before a verb with 地, with 吃, 看, 听, 讲: 吃得津津有味, 津津有味地看. Describes a person relishing food or absorbed in a story or book.

near.diff: 狼吞虎咽 is eating fast and greedily; 津津有味 is eating slowly enough to savour and enjoy it.
全神贯注 is total concentration, even on dull work; 津津有味 says the person is enjoying it.

cards.cue: Your grandfather spends the whole afternoon with an old adventure novel, chuckling and savouring every page. How is he reading?

ctx.s: 弟弟{津津有味}地吃着妈妈做的饺子。
ctx.en: My little brother is tucking into the dumplings Mum made, enjoying every bite.

ctx.s: 这本小说我看得{津津有味}，一个晚上就看完了。
ctx.en: I enjoyed this novel so much that I finished it in one evening.

ctx.s: 爷爷讲起年轻时的故事，孩子们听得{津津有味}。
ctx.en: When Grandpa told stories from his youth, the children listened, enthralled.

ctx.s: 这道菜看起来很普通，他却吃得{津津有味}，连说好吃。
ctx.en: The dish looked ordinary, but he ate it with relish, saying again and again how good it was.

ctx.s: 你在看什么，看得这么{津津有味}？
ctx.en: What are you reading that's got you so absorbed?

ctx.s: 别人觉得历史课很无聊，她却学得{津津有味}。
ctx.en: Others find history lessons boring, but she studies the subject with real relish.

bad.s: 我饿坏了，{津津有味}地三分钟就吃完了一大碗面。
bad.en: (meant: I was starving and wolfed down a big bowl of noodles in three minutes)
bad.why: Eating fast out of hunger is wolfing food down, a different idiom. This one means savouring the food with pleasure.

bad.s: 这个苹果很{津津有味}。
bad.en: (meant: this apple tastes very good)
bad.why: It describes how a person eats, reads or listens, not how the food tastes, and it does not take 'very'. Just say the apple is delicious.

cards.mean: brightly multicoloured
cards.lit: five colours and six hues

use.how: Describes things you can see that have many bright colours, as an attribute or predicate: 五颜六色的气球 / 花园里五颜六色的。

near.diff: 五花八门 is about many different kinds or varieties; 五颜六色 is only about many visible colours.

cards.cue: A children's party table is covered with red, yellow, green and blue balloons and sweets. How do you describe it?

ctx.s: 孩子们手里拿着{五颜六色}的气球。
ctx.en: The children are holding balloons of every colour.

ctx.s: 秋天到了，山上的树叶变得{五颜六色}，特别好看。
ctx.en: Autumn has come, and the leaves on the hills have turned all sorts of colours; it's beautiful.

ctx.s: 这幅画{五颜六色}的，是你女儿画的吗？
ctx.en: This picture is so colourful. Did your daughter paint it?

ctx.s: 市场里摆满了{五颜六色}的水果和蔬菜。
ctx.en: The market is full of brightly coloured fruit and vegetables.

ctx.s: 她用{五颜六色}的便利贴把学习计划贴满了一面墙。
ctx.en: She covered a whole wall with her study plan on sticky notes of every colour.

ctx.s: 节日的晚上，{五颜六色}的烟花照亮了整个城市。
ctx.en: On the night of the festival, multicoloured fireworks lit up the whole city.

bad.s: 这家书店的书{五颜六色}，什么类型都有。
bad.en: (meant: the bookshop has books of every kind)
bad.why: It describes colours you can see, not a variety of types. For many kinds of things, use the idiom for a dazzling variety (wu hua ba men).

bad.s: 今天的天空{五颜六色}，蓝得发亮。
bad.en: (meant: the sky is a brilliant blue today)
bad.why: It means many different colours at once; a sky of one brilliant blue is not multicoloured.

cards.mean: not knowing whether to laugh or cry
cards.lit: unable to cry and unable to laugh

use.how: Said about something absurd that is annoying and funny at once, often 让人哭笑不得 or 我听了哭笑不得。

near.diff: 莫名其妙 means baffling, with no understandable reason; 哭笑不得 is your reaction to something absurd that is both funny and exasperating.

cards.cue: You asked your little son to wash the car. He washed it with your expensive shampoo and now proudly wants praise.

ctx.s: 他在作文里写“我的爸爸是一只猫”，老师看了{哭笑不得}。
ctx.en: He wrote 'My dad is a cat' in his essay, and the teacher didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

ctx.s: 我让儿子帮我买盐，他买回来一袋糖，真让人{哭笑不得}。
ctx.en: I asked my son to buy salt and he came back with a bag of sugar. I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

ctx.s: 导航把我们带进了一条死胡同，还说“您已到达目的地”，车里的人都{哭笑不得}。
ctx.en: The satnav led us into a dead end and announced 'You have arrived at your destination'; everyone in the car didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

ctx.s: “狗把你的作业吃了？”“是啊，老师听了这个理由也{哭笑不得}。”
ctx.en: "The dog ate your homework?" "Yes, and when the teacher heard that excuse she didn't know whether to laugh or cry either."

ctx.s: 翻译软件把菜名翻得乱七八糟，外国客人看着菜单{哭笑不得}。
ctx.en: The translation app made a mess of the dish names, and the foreign guests looked at the menu half amused, half exasperated.

ctx.s: 公司为了省电，规定晚上加班不许开空调，员工们对这条规定{哭笑不得}。
ctx.en: To save electricity the company banned air conditioning during evening overtime; the staff didn't know whether to laugh or cry at the rule.

bad.s: 听说奶奶去世了，他{哭笑不得}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing his grandmother had died, he was overwhelmed)
bad.why: It reacts to something absurd and a little funny; using it for real grief sounds flippant and wrong.

bad.s: 收到录取通知书，她高兴得{哭笑不得}。
bad.en: (meant: she was so happy she laughed and cried at once)
bad.why: It implies exasperation at something ridiculous, not pure joy. Tears of happiness call for a different expression.

cards.mean: completely, leaving nothing behind (forgot, ate)
cards.lit: wiped dry and clean: not a trace left

use.how: A complement after verb + 得: 忘得一干二净, 吃得一干二净, 推得一干二净. Stresses that nothing at all is left.

near.diff: 一清二楚 means knowing or seeing something very clearly; 一干二净 means nothing is left, so 忘得一干二净 is the opposite of 记得一清二楚.

cards.cue: You studied a list of words last night, and this morning you can't recall a single one. How thoroughly did you forget them?

ctx.s: 一盘饺子被孩子们吃得{一干二净}。
ctx.en: The children ate the whole plate of dumplings; not one was left.

ctx.s: 昨天学的单词，我今天就忘得{一干二净}了。
ctx.en: The words I learned yesterday, I've completely forgotten today.

ctx.s: 你怎么把我们的约会忘得{一干二净}？
ctx.en: How could you completely forget our date?

ctx.s: 出了问题以后，他把责任推得{一干二净}。
ctx.en: When things went wrong, he pushed off every bit of the responsibility.

ctx.s: 小偷把店里值钱的东西偷得{一干二净}。
ctx.en: The thief took every last valuable thing in the shop.

ctx.s: 搬走之前，她把旧房子打扫得{一干二净}才交了钥匙。
ctx.en: Before moving out, she cleaned the old flat spotless and only then handed back the keys.

bad.s: 他对这件事知道得{一干二净}。
bad.en: (meant: he knows all about this matter)
bad.why: It means nothing is left, so it cannot express thorough knowledge. Use 'know very clearly' (yi qing er chu) instead.

bad.s: 他是一个{一干二净}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is a neat, tidy person)
bad.why: It is a degree complement after a verb (swept spotlessly clean), not a description of a person's tidiness.

cards.mean: to think one is always right
cards.lit: to take oneself to be right

story.text: In the Mencius, Mencius explains why Confucius despised the 'village worthy': a man whom everyone in his village likes, who seems loyal and honest but simply goes along with the world. Everyone is pleased with him and he thinks himself right, yet he cannot enter the Way of the sage kings Yao and Shun. That is why Confucius called such people thieves of virtue.

use.how: A predicate or attribute criticising someone who will not listen to others: 他太自以为是了 / 自以为是的人; also adverbial 自以为是地。

near.diff: 不懂装懂 is pretending to know what you don't; 自以为是 is sincerely believing you are right and ignoring others.

cards.cue: Your teammate brushes off every suggestion, insists his plan is the only correct one, and is surprised when it fails.

ctx.s: 他太{自以为是}了，从来不听别人的建议。
ctx.en: He is far too sure he's right; he never listens to anyone's advice.

ctx.s: 别那么{自以为是}，你也可能会错。
ctx.en: Don't be so sure of yourself; you could be wrong too.

ctx.s: 新来的经理很{自以为是}，开会时总是打断大家。
ctx.en: The new manager thinks he's always right and keeps interrupting everyone in meetings.

ctx.s: 他总是{自以为是}地替别人做决定，结果谁都不满意。
ctx.en: He always decides things for other people, sure he knows best, and in the end nobody is happy.

ctx.s: 年轻时我有点{自以为是}，后来吃了亏才明白要多听别人的。
ctx.en: When I was young I was rather sure I was always right; only after paying for it did I learn to listen to others.

ctx.s: 这篇评论写得很{自以为是}，好像只有作者的看法才是对的。
ctx.en: This review is written very self-righteously, as if only the author's view could be correct.

bad.s: 她很{自以为是}，所以面试表现得很好。
bad.en: (meant: she is self-confident, so her interview went well)
bad.why: It criticises arrogance and refusal to listen; it is never praise for healthy self-confidence.

bad.s: 我{自以为是}你的看法。
bad.en: (meant: I think your view is right)
bad.why: It is about oneself thinking one is right and takes no object; to agree with someone else's view, say you think their view is right.

cards.mean: absent-minded, with one's mind elsewhere
cards.lit: the heart is not here

story.text: The phrase comes from the Great Learning, which argues that cultivating oneself depends on setting the mind right: when the mind is not present, one looks but does not see, listens but does not hear, and eats without knowing the taste of the food.

use.how: A predicate or adverbial (心不在焉地) about someone whose attention is elsewhere at the moment, often mildly critical: 上课心不在焉。

near.diff: 粗心大意 is a careless habit that causes mistakes; 心不在焉 is a passing state of having your mind on something else.

cards.cue: Your friend keeps stirring her coffee and staring out of the window, answering you with 'mm' without hearing a word.

ctx.s: 上课的时候，他一直{心不在焉}，老师叫了他两次都没听见。
ctx.en: All through the lesson his mind was somewhere else; the teacher called his name twice and he didn't hear.

ctx.s: 你今天怎么{心不在焉}的？有什么心事吗？
ctx.en: Why are you so distracted today? Is something on your mind?

ctx.s: 她{心不在焉}地搅着咖啡，眼睛一直看着窗外。
ctx.en: She absent-mindedly stirred her coffee, her eyes fixed on the window.

ctx.s: 开会时小王{心不在焉}，老板问他问题，他连问的是什么都不知道。
ctx.en: Xiao Wang's mind was elsewhere in the meeting; when the boss asked him something, he didn't even know what the question was.

ctx.s: 我跟他说了半天，他只是{心不在焉}地“嗯”了几声。
ctx.en: I talked to him for ages, and he just went 'mm' a few times without really listening.

ctx.s: 比赛前一天晚上，他看书看得{心不在焉}，满脑子都是明天的比赛。
ctx.en: The night before the match he read without taking anything in; all he could think of was the game.

bad.s: 我给他打电话，他{心不在焉}，家里没人。
bad.en: (meant: I phoned him but he wasn't at home)
bad.why: It means the mind is elsewhere while the person is present; it says nothing about being physically absent.

bad.s: 度假的时候，我{心不在焉}，什么烦恼都没有。
bad.en: (meant: on holiday I was carefree)
bad.why: It means distracted and inattentive, not relaxed. For being carefree, use a different idiom (wu you wu lv).

cards.mean: half-hearted; unable to commit to one thing
cards.lit: three hearts and two minds

use.how: A predicate or adverbial criticising someone who keeps switching and won't commit: 做事三心二意 / 别三心二意了。Also used of fickleness in love.

near.diff: 一心一意 is its opposite: wholehearted devotion to one thing.

cards.cue: A student practises piano for ten minutes, switches to drawing, then picks up the guitar, and finishes none of them.

ctx.s: 学习的时候不能{三心二意}。
ctx.en: When you study, you can't keep half your mind on other things.

ctx.s: 他做作业总是{三心二意}，一会儿看手机，一会儿吃零食。
ctx.en: He never sticks to his homework: one minute he's on his phone, the next he's snacking.

ctx.s: 你一会儿想学吉他，一会儿想学画画，再这样{三心二意}，什么都学不好。
ctx.en: One minute you want to learn guitar, the next painting; if you keep chopping and changing like this, you'll never master anything.

ctx.s: 她一年换了好几个专业，父母说她太{三心二意}了。
ctx.en: She changed her major several times in one year, and her parents said she couldn't commit to anything.

ctx.s: 对感情{三心二意}的人，很难得到别人的信任。
ctx.en: People who are fickle in love find it hard to win others' trust.

ctx.s: “我还是想学画画……”“别{三心二意}了，选一个就坚持下去。”
ctx.en: "Actually I'd rather learn painting..." "Stop flitting about. Pick one and stick with it."

bad.s: 他{三心二意}，一次能做三件事。
bad.en: (meant: he is good at multitasking)
bad.why: It criticises a lack of commitment; it is never praise for doing several things at once.

bad.s: 做这个决定之前，我{三心二意}地考虑了很久。
bad.en: (meant: I thought it over carefully from every angle)
bad.why: It means half-hearted and fickle, not careful thought. For careful deliberation use 'think deeply' (shen si shu lv).

cards.mean: anxious and unsettled inside
cards.lit: seven going up and eight going down

use.how: Almost always about the heart: 心里七上八下(的). Describes nervous unease while waiting for an uncertain outcome.

near.diff: 提心吊胆 is fearing danger over a period of time; 七上八下 is the jumpy, unsettled feeling while you wait to find out how something turned out.

cards.cue: You sat the most important exam of your life last week, and the results come out tomorrow morning. How does your heart feel tonight?

ctx.s: 等考试成绩的时候，我心里{七上八下}的。
ctx.en: While I was waiting for my exam results, my stomach was in knots.

ctx.s: 第一次上台演讲，他心里{七上八下}，手都在发抖。
ctx.en: Giving his first speech on stage, he was so jittery that his hands shook.

ctx.s: 儿子去参加篮球队的选拔，妈妈在家等消息，心里{七上八下}的。
ctx.en: Her son had gone to the basketball team trials, and his mother waited at home for news, her heart all of a flutter.

ctx.s: 面试结束后，她心里一直{七上八下}的，不知道能不能被录取。
ctx.en: After the interview she was on edge the whole time, not knowing whether she'd be hired.

ctx.s: “医生怎么还不出来？”“别急，我心里也{七上八下}的。”
ctx.en: "Why hasn't the doctor come out yet?" "Hang on, I'm on edge too."

ctx.s: 公司要裁员，名单明天公布，办公室里每个人心里都{七上八下}。
ctx.en: The company is cutting jobs and the list comes out tomorrow; everyone in the office feels uneasy.

bad.s: 我们爬山爬得{七上八下}，累死了。
bad.en: (meant: we climbed up and down the hills all day)
bad.why: It describes an anxious state of mind, not physical movement up and down.

bad.s: 收到礼物，她心里{七上八下}，开心极了。
bad.en: (meant: she was thrilled to get the present)
bad.why: It is anxiety and unease, not happy excitement.

cards.mean: in a frantic, flustered rush
cards.lit: hands busy and feet in a muddle

use.how: A predicate or adverbial (手忙脚乱地) for clumsy, disorganised hurry when caught unprepared: 客人一来，她就手忙脚乱。

near.diff: 不可开交 stresses having too much to do to get away; 手忙脚乱 stresses flustered, clumsy disorder.
惊慌失措 is panic from fear or shock; 手忙脚乱 is a disorganised rush, often with no fear at all.

cards.cue: Guests ring the doorbell early; you are still dropping dishes and pulling on mismatched socks as you tidy up.

ctx.s: 客人突然来了，妈妈{手忙脚乱}地收拾房间。
ctx.en: Guests turned up unexpectedly, and Mum rushed around tidying the room in a fluster.

ctx.s: 第一次给宝宝换尿布，爸爸{手忙脚乱}的。
ctx.en: Changing the baby's nappy for the first time, Dad was all fingers and thumbs.

ctx.s: 闹钟没响，我早上{手忙脚乱}，连袜子都穿反了。
ctx.en: My alarm didn't go off, and in the morning rush I even put my socks on inside out.

ctx.s: 餐厅一下子来了很多客人，新来的服务员{手忙脚乱}，把菜送错了桌。
ctx.en: A crowd of customers arrived at once; the new waiter got flustered and took dishes to the wrong table.

ctx.s: “快点，车要开了！”“别催我，越催我越{手忙脚乱}。”
ctx.en: "Hurry up, the bus is leaving!" "Stop rushing me, the more you rush me the more flustered I get."

ctx.s: 只要提前准备好材料，到时候就不会{手忙脚乱}了。
ctx.en: As long as you get the materials ready in advance, you won't be scrambling when the time comes.

bad.s: 他工作很{手忙脚乱}，但每件事都安排得井井有条。
bad.en: (meant: he is very busy but well organised)
bad.why: It means flustered and disorganised, so it contradicts 'well organised'. To say simply busy, just say 'very busy'.

bad.s: 他摔倒以后{手忙脚乱}，腿疼得走不了路。
bad.en: (meant: after falling, his arms and legs hurt)
bad.why: It describes a frantic rush, not injured hands and feet.

cards.mean: too impatient to wait
cards.lit: so pressed that one cannot wait

use.how: Usually an adverbial before the action someone is eager to do: 迫不及待地打开 / 迫不及待想看; can also stand as a predicate: 我已经迫不及待了。

near.diff: 争分夺秒 is racing against the clock to finish in time; 迫不及待 is eagerness to start something right now.

cards.cue: A parcel you have waited a month for finally arrives, and you tear it open right there at the front door.

ctx.s: 一放学，孩子们就{迫不及待}地跑出了教室。
ctx.en: As soon as school was out, the children dashed out of the classroom.

ctx.s: 收到快递，她{迫不及待}地打开了盒子。
ctx.en: When the parcel arrived, she couldn't wait to open the box.

ctx.s: 新手机一上市，他就{迫不及待}地买了一部。
ctx.en: The moment the new phone came out, he rushed to buy one.

ctx.s: “电影什么时候上映？”“下个月，我已经{迫不及待}了！”
ctx.en: "When does the film come out?" "Next month. I can't wait!"

ctx.s: 他还没听完问题，就{迫不及待}地开始回答。
ctx.en: He started answering before he'd even heard the whole question.

ctx.s: 天气刚暖和一点，公园里的花就{迫不及待}地开了。
ctx.en: The weather had barely warmed up when the flowers in the park eagerly burst into bloom.

bad.s: 时间{迫不及待}，我们必须马上出发。
bad.en: (meant: time is pressing, we must leave now)
bad.why: It describes a person's eagerness, not urgent time. To say time is pressing, say that time is tight.

bad.s: 一听说要打针，孩子就{迫不及待}地哭了起来。
bad.en: (meant: as soon as he heard about the injection, the child burst into tears)
bad.why: It means eager to do something you want to do; it cannot describe an instant reaction of fear or dread.

cards.mean: calm and unhurried
cards.lit: neither flustered nor hurried

use.how: Usually an adverbial (不慌不忙地 + verb) or predicate, for someone who acts calmly when others would rush: 他不慌不忙地回答。

near.diff: 心平气和 is calm in temper, not angry; 不慌不忙 is calm in pace, not rushing under pressure.

cards.cue: The fire alarm goes off and everyone runs, but one teacher calmly lines up the children and walks them out.

ctx.s: 他{不慌不忙}地喝完茶才出门。
ctx.en: He took his time finishing his tea before he left.

ctx.s: 警报响了，老师{不慌不忙}地带着学生走出教学楼。
ctx.en: The alarm went off, and the teacher calmly led the students out of the building.

ctx.s: 面对记者的问题，她{不慌不忙}，一个一个地回答。
ctx.en: Faced with the reporters' questions, she kept her composure and answered them one by one.

ctx.s: 大家都急得团团转，只有他{不慌不忙}的，把东西一件件装进箱子。
ctx.en: Everyone was rushing around in a panic; only he stayed unhurried, packing things into the box one by one.

ctx.s: “车快开了，你怎么还{不慌不忙}的？”“别担心，还有十分钟呢。”
ctx.en: "The train's about to leave, why are you still dawdling?" "Relax, there are still ten minutes."

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后一分钟，他仍然{不慌不忙}地运球，找准机会投进了一球。
ctx.en: With one minute left in the game, he kept dribbling calmly, picked his moment and scored.

bad.s: 这家公司这几年发展得{不慌不忙}，越来越好。
bad.en: (meant: the company has grown steadily in recent years)
bad.why: It describes how a person acts under time pressure, not the steady growth of a company. Say it grew steadily.

bad.s: 他脾气特别好，跟家人从来{不慌不忙}，没吵过一次架。
bad.en: (meant: he is very good-tempered and has never once quarrelled with his family)
bad.why: It is about pace and composure, not temper. For someone who never gets angry, use 'calm and even-tempered'.

cards.mean: very cautiously, taking great care
cards.lit: small heart, reverent and respectful: acting with a careful, watchful heart

story.text: The phrase comes from the Book of Songs, in an ode praising King Wen of Zhou, who is described as xiaoxin yiyi: careful and reverent. There it described his respectful conduct in serving Heaven. Over time the sense shifted, and today it simply means doing something with great caution.

use.how: Usually an adverbial with 地 before a verb (小心翼翼地走) or a predicate. Describes how a person handles something fragile, risky or sensitive.

near.diff: 一丝不苟 praises meticulous attention to standards and detail; 小心翼翼 is caution for fear of breaking, falling or offending.

cards.cue: Carrying a full bowl of hot soup across a crowded room, step by step, eyes fixed on it. How does she walk?

ctx.s: 妈妈{小心翼翼}地把蛋糕从盒子里拿了出来。
ctx.en: Mum took the cake out of the box very carefully.

ctx.s: 地上结了冰，大家都{小心翼翼}地往前走。
ctx.en: The ground was icy, so everyone moved forward very cautiously.

ctx.s: 他第一次抱刚出生的女儿，动作{小心翼翼}的。
ctx.en: Holding his newborn daughter for the first time, he moved with great care.

ctx.s: “你说话怎么这么{小心翼翼}？”“我怕说错话惹老板生气。”
ctx.en: "Why are you choosing your words so carefully?" "I'm afraid of saying something that will annoy the boss."

ctx.s: 自从上次被骗以后，她跟陌生人打交道总是{小心翼翼}。
ctx.en: Since she was cheated last time, she has always been very wary in dealing with strangers.

ctx.s: 谈判的时候，双方都{小心翼翼}地避开了价格问题。
ctx.en: During the negotiation, both sides carefully steered clear of the question of price.

bad.s: {小心翼翼}！后面有车开过来了！
bad.en: (meant: Look out! There's a car coming up behind you!)
bad.why: It describes the careful manner in which someone does something; it cannot be shouted as a warning. To warn someone, say xiaoxin (look out).

bad.s: 这个计划写得很{小心翼翼}。
bad.en: (meant: this plan was written thoroughly)
bad.why: It describes a person's cautious manner, not the quality of a document. A thorough plan is zhoumi (well thought out) or xiangxi (detailed).

cards.mean: careless, not paying attention
cards.lit: a coarse heart and a big, loose mind

use.how: A predicate or attributive (太粗心大意了，粗心大意的人). Criticises carelessness that causes a mistake, often in work, exams or driving.

near.diff: 丢三落四 is the habit of forgetting or losing belongings; 粗心大意 is carelessness in doing a task, which leads to errors.
心不在焉 is having one's mind elsewhere at the moment; 粗心大意 is not taking enough care, whatever the reason.

cards.cue: A student knew every answer but lost marks for copying a number wrong and skipping the last page. What went wrong?

ctx.s: 考试的时候千万别{粗心大意}，写完要检查一遍。
ctx.en: Whatever you do, don't be careless in the exam; check everything once you've finished.

ctx.s: 他太{粗心大意}了，把“己”字写成了“已”字。
ctx.en: He was so careless that he wrote the character ji (self) as yi (already).

ctx.s: 这次事故是司机一时{粗心大意}造成的。
ctx.en: This accident was caused by a moment's carelessness on the driver's part.

ctx.s: “又算错了？”“对不起，我太{粗心大意}了。”
ctx.en: "Wrong again?" "Sorry, I was too careless."

ctx.s: 做实验可不能{粗心大意}，一个数据错了，结果就全错了。
ctx.en: You can't be careless in an experiment: one wrong figure and the whole result is wrong.

ctx.s: 合同里有一个数字写错了，都怪他{粗心大意}。
ctx.en: A figure in the contract was written wrongly, all because of his carelessness.

bad.s: 作业很简单，我{粗心大意}地做完了，得了满分。
bad.en: (meant: I finished the easy homework without effort and got full marks)
bad.why: It means careless and blames someone for errors; it cannot mean relaxed or effortless, and clashes with a perfect result.

bad.s: 这道题很{粗心大意}。
bad.en: (meant: this question is tricky and easy to get wrong)
bad.why: Only a person can be careless. For a tricky question, say it is easy to get wrong (rongyi chucuo).

cards.mean: always forgetting or losing things
cards.lit: to lose three and leave four behind

use.how: A predicate or attributive about a person's habit (他总是丢三落四的). It takes no object: you cannot 丢三落四 a particular thing.

near.diff: 粗心大意 is carelessness that causes mistakes in a task; 丢三落四 is specifically forgetting or losing one's things, again and again.

cards.cue: Your brother leaves his keys at home, his umbrella on the bus and his homework on the kitchen table, every single week. What is he like?

ctx.s: 我弟弟总是{丢三落四}的，今天又把作业忘在家里了。
ctx.en: My little brother is always forgetting things; today he left his homework at home again.

ctx.s: 你怎么这么{丢三落四}？雨伞都丢了三把了！
ctx.en: How can you be so forgetful? You've already lost three umbrellas!

ctx.s: 年纪大了，我也开始{丢三落四}，出门老是忘带手机。
ctx.en: Now that I'm older, I've started forgetting things too; I'm always going out without my phone.

ctx.s: 出发前列一张清单，就不会{丢三落四}了。
ctx.en: Make a list before you set off and you won't leave things behind.

ctx.s: 她以前很{丢三落四}，现在出门前都要把包检查一遍。
ctx.en: She used to lose things all the time; now she checks her bag before she goes out.

ctx.s: 像他这样{丢三落四}的人，最好别让他保管护照。
ctx.en: Someone as forgetful as him had better not be put in charge of the passports.

bad.s: 我今天把钥匙{丢三落四}了。
bad.en: (meant: I lost my keys today)
bad.why: It describes a habit and takes no object. To say you lost your keys, use the plain verb diu (to lose).

bad.s: 搬家前他{丢三落四}，扔了很多旧东西。
bad.en: (meant: before moving he got rid of lots of old things)
bad.why: It is about forgetting or losing things by accident, not deliberately throwing them away.

cards.mean: half believing, half doubting
cards.lit: half belief, half doubt

use.how: A predicate or adverbial with 地, often 对…半信半疑. The subject is the person who hears something and is unsure whether it is true.

near.diff: 犹豫不决 is being unable to decide what to do; 半信半疑 is being unsure whether what one hears is true.

cards.cue: A friend tells you the shop is giving away free phones today. It sounds too good to be true, but maybe it is real. How do you take the news?

ctx.s: 听说明天放假，同学们都{半信半疑}。
ctx.en: When they heard tomorrow was a day off, the students weren't sure whether to believe it.

ctx.s: 他说自己中了大奖，我听了{半信半疑}。
ctx.en: He said he'd won a big prize; I only half believed him.

ctx.s: 她{半信半疑}地打开那封邮件，没想到真的是录取通知。
ctx.en: Half doubting, she opened the email, and to her surprise it really was an offer of admission.

ctx.s: “这种药真的有用吗？”奶奶{半信半疑}地问医生。
ctx.en: "Does this medicine really work?" Grandma asked the doctor doubtfully.

ctx.s: 一开始大家对这个新方法{半信半疑}，用了一个月才发现效果不错。
ctx.en: At first everyone was sceptical about the new method; only after a month did they find it worked well.

ctx.s: 对网上各种减肥广告，我一直抱着{半信半疑}的态度。
ctx.en: I've always taken all those online weight-loss ads with a pinch of salt.

bad.s: 我{半信半疑}地做了一半作业就去睡觉了。
bad.en: (meant: I did half my homework and went to bed)
bad.why: Here 'half' belongs to belief and doubt; it says nothing about doing half of a task.

bad.s: 这个消息很{半信半疑}。
bad.en: (meant: this news is doubtful)
bad.why: The person who hears the news is half doubting, not the news itself. Say you half believe the news, or that it is not very credible.

cards.mean: having only a superficial understanding
cards.lit: to know one bit and understand half

story.text: Dictionaries trace the phrase to Canglang Remarks on Poetry by the Song-dynasty critic Yan Yu. Grading poets by how deeply they had grasped the art, he distinguished a thorough understanding from one that reaches only 'one bit of knowledge and half an understanding'.

use.how: A predicate (对…一知半解) or attributive (一知半解的知识). Criticises shallow knowledge, or modestly describes one's own.

near.diff: 一窍不通 is knowing nothing at all; 一知半解 is knowing a little, superficially, often while thinking one knows more.
不懂装懂 is pretending to understand; 一知半解 describes how much one actually understands.

cards.cue: After reading two articles online, your neighbour lectures everyone about investing, but gets the basics wrong. How much does he really understand?

ctx.s: 我对电脑只是{一知半解}，这个问题我修不了。
ctx.en: I only know a little about computers; I can't fix this problem.

ctx.s: 别看他说得头头是道，其实他对这一行{一知半解}。
ctx.en: He may sound convincing, but actually his knowledge of this trade is shallow.

ctx.s: 学东西最怕{一知半解}，以为自己懂了，其实没懂。
ctx.en: The worst thing in learning is half-understanding: thinking you've got it when you haven't.

ctx.s: “你能给我讲讲这个法律问题吗？”“我也{一知半解}，你最好去问律师。”
ctx.en: "Can you explain this legal question to me?" "I only half understand it myself; you'd better ask a lawyer."

ctx.s: 凭着{一知半解}的知识就给别人看病，太危险了。
ctx.en: Treating people's illnesses on the strength of half-baked knowledge is far too dangerous.

ctx.s: 说明书我读了两遍，懂了一部分，可还是{一知半解}。
ctx.en: I've read the instructions twice and got some of it, but I still only half understand them.

bad.s: 我对日语{一知半解}，一个字也看不懂。
bad.en: (meant: I know nothing about Japanese and can't read a word)
bad.why: It means knowing a little, not nothing. For knowing nothing at all, the idiom is yi qiao bu tong.

bad.s: 他特别聪明，老师讲一点，他就{一知半解}了。
bad.en: (meant: he's so bright he grasps the whole thing from a hint)
bad.why: It criticises shallow understanding; it is not praise for quick learning. For grasping a lot from a hint, say ju yi fan san.

cards.mean: to know absolutely nothing about a subject
cards.lit: not even one opening is clear: in old thought the heart had openings for understanding

use.how: A predicate, usually 对…一窍不通, about a subject or skill. Often self-deprecating (我对音乐一窍不通), or critical of someone else.

near.diff: 一知半解 is knowing a little, superficially; 一窍不通 is knowing nothing whatsoever about the subject.

cards.cue: Someone asks you to fix their car engine. You have never opened a bonnet in your life and couldn't name a single part. What do you say?

ctx.s: 我对做饭{一窍不通}，连鸡蛋都不会煎。
ctx.en: I know nothing at all about cooking; I can't even fry an egg.

ctx.s: 他对音乐{一窍不通}，却非要当评委。
ctx.en: He knows absolutely nothing about music, yet he insists on being a judge.

ctx.s: “你懂车吗？”“我对汽车{一窍不通}，只会开。”
ctx.en: "Do you know about cars?" "I know nothing about them; I can only drive one."

ctx.s: 刚来公司的时候，我对财务{一窍不通}，全靠同事带我。
ctx.en: When I first joined the company I knew nothing about finance; I relied entirely on my colleagues to teach me.

ctx.s: 一个对法律{一窍不通}的人，怎么能当律师呢？
ctx.en: How can someone who knows nothing about law be a lawyer?

ctx.s: 爷爷原来对手机{一窍不通}，现在都会视频聊天了。
ctx.en: Grandpa used to know nothing about mobile phones; now he can even video chat.

bad.s: 前面在修路，这条路{一窍不通}。
bad.en: (meant: the road ahead is blocked by roadworks)
bad.why: It is only about knowing nothing of a subject; tong here is not 'passing through'. For a blocked road say the road is bu tong.

bad.s: 我跟新来的同事{一窍不通}，还没说过话。
bad.en: (meant: I don't know the new colleague at all)
bad.why: It is about a field of knowledge or a skill, not about knowing a person. To say you don't know someone well, say bu shu.

cards.mean: practice makes perfect
cards.lit: familiarity can give birth to skill

story.text: The saying is traditionally illustrated by the tale of the oil seller. Chen Yaozi was a famous archer who hit the target eight or nine times out of ten. An old oil seller watching him only nodded slightly. When Chen asked whether his shooting was not skilled, the old man said there was no secret, only a practised hand. He set a gourd on the ground, covered its mouth with a coin with a square hole, and poured oil through the hole without wetting the coin. The four-character phrase itself is later.

use.how: Stands alone as a saying or a clause, often to encourage (多练练，熟能生巧) or to explain someone's skill. Not used as an attributive.

cards.cue: Your nephew is frustrated that his first dumplings fall apart. You tell him that after a few hundred more, his hands will know what to do.

ctx.s: 别着急，多练几次，{熟能生巧}嘛。
ctx.en: Don't worry, practise a few more times; practice makes perfect.

ctx.s: 刚开始他包饺子很慢，后来{熟能生巧}，一分钟能包好几个。
ctx.en: At first he was slow at making dumplings, but with practice he got so good he could make several a minute.

ctx.s: 老师常说：写字没有捷径，只有{熟能生巧}。
ctx.en: The teacher often says there's no shortcut to good handwriting, only practice.

ctx.s: “你打字怎么这么快？”“天天打，{熟能生巧}呗。”
ctx.en: "How do you type so fast?" "I type every day; practice makes perfect, that's all."

ctx.s: 他做了二十年木匠，{熟能生巧}，不用尺子也能锯得很直。
ctx.en: After twenty years as a carpenter his skill is such that he can saw straight without a ruler.

ctx.s: 所谓{熟能生巧}，任何技能都要靠大量重复才能掌握。
ctx.en: As the saying goes, practice makes perfect: any skill takes a great deal of repetition to master.

bad.s: 他真是{熟能生巧}，第一次做饭就做得特别好吃。
bad.en: (meant: he's a natural; his very first meal was delicious)
bad.why: The saying credits skill to long practice, so it contradicts doing well the first time. For natural talent, say someone has tianfu (a gift).

bad.s: 我们俩认识十年了，所以{熟能生巧}。
bad.en: (meant: we've known each other ten years, so we get along well)
bad.why: Shu here means practised at a skill, not close to a person. For friends who get along, say they are hen shu or hen you moqi.

cards.mean: endless, going on and on
cards.lit: without finishing, without ending

use.how: A predicate, adverbial with 地, or complement after 得 (吵得没完没了). Complains that something tiresome won't stop: rain, noise, talk, arguments.

cards.cue: The upstairs neighbours have been drilling since eight this morning, and it is now evening. You complain to your flatmate.

ctx.s: 这雨下得{没完没了}，衣服都晾不干。
ctx.en: This rain just won't stop; the washing can't even dry.

ctx.s: 你别{没完没了}地问了，我已经回答过了！
ctx.en: Stop asking over and over; I've already answered!

ctx.s: 楼上在装修，电钻声{没完没了}，吵得我没法休息。
ctx.en: The flat upstairs is being renovated and the drilling goes on and on; I can't get any rest.

ctx.s: 一说起他的狗，他就{没完没了}。
ctx.en: Once he starts talking about his dog, there's no stopping him.

ctx.s: 会开了三个小时还{没完没了}，大家都不耐烦了。
ctx.en: The meeting had been going for three hours with no end in sight, and everyone was getting impatient.

ctx.s: 两个孩子为一个玩具吵得{没完没了}，最后妈妈把玩具收走了。
ctx.en: The two children squabbled endlessly over a toy, until Mum finally took it away.

bad.s: 这本小说太好看了，我希望它{没完没了}。
bad.en: (meant: this novel is so good I wish it would never end)
bad.why: It is a complaint about something tiresome; it cannot express a wish that something good would last.

bad.s: 他还{没完没了}作业，不能出去玩。
bad.en: (meant: he hasn't finished his homework, so he can't go out)
bad.why: It does not mean 'not yet finished' and takes no object. Say the homework is not done yet (hai mei zuowan).

cards.mean: truly living up to its name or reputation
cards.lit: the name matches the reality

use.how: A predicate or attributive, very often 是名副其实的… (a true…). Confirms that a name, title or reputation matches the facts.

cards.cue: A town calls itself the city of flowers, and when you visit, every street really is full of blossoms all year round.

ctx.s: 这里一年四季都开着花，真是{名副其实}的花城。
ctx.en: Flowers bloom here all year round; it truly deserves to be called the City of Flowers.

ctx.s: 他每天要看好几个小时的书，是个{名副其实}的书迷。
ctx.en: He reads for several hours every day; he's a bookworm in every sense of the word.

ctx.s: 都说这家店的烤鸭好吃，今天一尝，果然{名副其实}。
ctx.en: Everyone says this restaurant's roast duck is good; having tried it today, it really lives up to its reputation.

ctx.s: “这座山为什么叫雪山？”“山顶一年到头都是雪，{名副其实}嘛。”
ctx.en: "Why is this mountain called Snow Mountain?" "The peak is covered in snow all year; the name fits."

ctx.s: 这支球队连续三年拿了冠军，成了{名副其实}的强队。
ctx.en: Having won the championship three years running, the team has become a powerhouse in the true sense.

ctx.s: 大家都叫他“活字典”，什么难字他都认识，真是{名副其实}。
ctx.en: Everyone calls him a "walking dictionary", and he really does know every difficult character: the name truly fits.

bad.s: 他{名副其实}地叫王明，不是小名。
bad.en: (meant: his real name is Wang Ming, not a nickname)
bad.why: It is a judgement that a name or reputation fits the facts, not a way of saying 'real name' (zhenming).

bad.s: 她的名字很{名副其实}，听起来很美。
bad.en: (meant: her name is lovely)
bad.why: It does not mean a name sounds nice; it means the person or thing deserves its name. A nice-sounding name is hao ting.

cards.mean: a common, everyday occurrence
cards.lit: ordinary home cooking, a simple everyday meal

use.how: A noun, usually after 是 or 成了: 加班是家常便饭. Says something happens all the time, often something hard. Can still mean a simple home meal.

near.diff: 理所当然 says something is natural and to be expected; 家常便饭 says it happens so often it is routine.

cards.cue: A firefighter shrugs when asked about being woken at three in the morning: it happens several times a week.

ctx.s: 当医生的，加班是{家常便饭}。
ctx.en: For doctors, working overtime is an everyday thing.

ctx.s: 对他来说，出差就跟{家常便饭}一样。
ctx.en: For him, business trips are completely routine.

ctx.s: 在这个城市，堵车早就成了{家常便饭}。
ctx.en: In this city, traffic jams have long been part of daily life.

ctx.s: “你们公司经常开会开到很晚吗？”“那是{家常便饭}。”
ctx.en: "Does your company often have meetings that run late?" "That happens all the time."

ctx.s: 小时候家里穷，饿肚子是{家常便饭}。
ctx.en: Our family was poor when I was little; going hungry was a regular thing.

ctx.s: 有空来我家吃顿{家常便饭}吧，不用客气。
ctx.en: Come round for a simple home-cooked meal when you're free; no need to stand on ceremony.

bad.s: 他{家常便饭}地迟到，老板很生气。
bad.en: (meant: he is late all the time and the boss is angry)
bad.why: It is a noun, not an adverb. Say that being late is a daily thing for him, or simply that he is often late.

bad.s: 去年我第一次出国，真是{家常便饭}。
bad.en: (meant: going abroad for the first time last year was a big experience)
bad.why: It means something routine and frequent, so it cannot describe a first-time, special event.

cards.mean: it's a long story
cards.lit: when it comes to telling it, the words are long

use.how: Said before or instead of an explanation whose background takes long to tell: 这事说来话长。 Often a gentle way to put the story off.

near.diff: 一言难尽 says it can't be summed up briefly, often because it was hard or bitter; 说来话长 only says the story is long.

cards.cue: A friend asks why you moved to another city. The reason involves years of events, and you would rather tell it over dinner later.

ctx.s: “你们俩是怎么认识的？”“{说来话长}，我们是在火车上认识的。”
ctx.en: "How did you two meet?" "It's a long story. We met on a train."

ctx.s: 他叹了口气说：“这件事{说来话长}，等有空我再慢慢告诉你。”
ctx.en: He sighed: "It's a long story; I'll tell you properly when I have time."

ctx.s: 我为什么辞职？{说来话长}，咱们先点菜吧。
ctx.en: Why did I quit? It's a long story. Let's order first.

ctx.s: 这座老房子的来历{说来话长}，要从我爷爷那一代说起。
ctx.en: The history of this old house is a long story; it starts with my grandfather's generation.

ctx.s: 记者问她为什么回国，她只是笑着说：“{说来话长}。”
ctx.en: When the reporter asked why she had come back home, she just smiled and said, "It's a long story."

ctx.s: 说起这个品牌名字的由来，那可就{说来话长}了。
ctx.en: As for where this brand's name comes from, now that's a long story.

bad.s: 这部电影{说来话长}，我看了三个小时。
bad.en: (meant: this film is very long; I watched it for three hours)
bad.why: It is about a story that would take long to tell, not about something that is long in itself, such as a film or a meeting.

bad.s: 他每次开会都{说来话长}，大家都听烦了。
bad.en: (meant: he goes on and on at every meeting)
bad.why: It does not mean long-winded. It introduces a story that would take long to tell, not a person who talks too much.

cards.mean: to tell the plain truth, frankly
cards.lit: true words, truly spoken

use.how: Used intransitively as a predicate or as an opener before a frank, often unwelcome remark: 我就实话实说了。 跟你实话实说吧。

near.diff: 开门见山 is about getting to the point without preamble; 实话实说 is about saying the true thing even when it is unwelcome.

cards.cue: Your friend asks what you honestly think of her new haircut. You don't like it, and you decide to tell her so instead of being polite.

ctx.s: 你问我觉得怎么样，那我就{实话实说}了：这道菜太咸。
ctx.en: Since you ask what I think, I'll be honest: this dish is too salty.

ctx.s: 跟你{实话实说}吧，这个月我真的没钱了。
ctx.en: To tell you the truth, I'm really out of money this month.

ctx.s: 医生，请您{实话实说}，我的病到底严不严重？
ctx.en: Doctor, please be frank with me. How serious is my illness, really?

ctx.s: 面试时被问到缺点，她{实话实说}，承认自己不太会安排时间。
ctx.en: Asked about her weaknesses in the interview, she told the plain truth and admitted she is not good at managing her time.

ctx.s: 他因为{实话实说}得罪了领导，可同事们心里都佩服他。
ctx.en: He offended his boss by speaking frankly, but his colleagues privately admired him.

ctx.s: “你是不是不喜欢我送的礼物？”“{实话实说}，这个颜色我不太喜欢。”
ctx.en: "You don't like the present I gave you, do you?" "Honestly, I'm not keen on the colour."

bad.s: 这本书{实话实说}地记录了那段历史。
bad.en: (meant: this book faithfully records that period of history)
bad.why: It describes a person speaking frankly to someone, not a book or record being accurate.

bad.s: 他把这件事{实话实说}给了妈妈。
bad.en: (meant: he told his mother the truth about it)
bad.why: It takes no object and cannot be followed by gei. Put the listener before it instead: gen mama shihua shishuo.

cards.mean: everyone talking at once
cards.lit: seven mouths and eight tongues

use.how: Usually an adverbial before a speech verb: 大家七嘴八舌地讨论起来。 Needs a group of people, each saying something different.

near.diff: 议论纷纷 is many people commenting or gossiping about something; 七嘴八舌 stresses many voices talking over each other at the same moment.

cards.cue: The waiter asks a table of eight what they would like, and everyone starts calling out different orders at the same time.

ctx.s: 老师刚说完，同学们就{七嘴八舌}地讨论起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher finished, the students all started discussing it at once.

ctx.s: 你们别{七嘴八舌}的，一个一个说！
ctx.en: Don't all talk at once. One at a time!

ctx.s: 记者们围着球员，{七嘴八舌}地提问。
ctx.en: The reporters crowded round the player, all firing questions at once.

ctx.s: 家里人{七嘴八舌}地给我出主意，我反而更不知道怎么办了。
ctx.en: My whole family chimed in with advice all at once, and I ended up even less sure what to do.

ctx.s: 群里大家{七嘴八舌}，半天也没定下来去哪儿吃饭。
ctx.en: Everyone in the group chat had something to say, and after ages we still hadn't decided where to eat.

ctx.s: 会上大家{七嘴八舌}，主持人只好敲了敲桌子。
ctx.en: Everyone at the meeting was talking over each other, so the chair had to rap on the table.

bad.s: 我妹妹特别{七嘴八舌}，一个人能说一下午。
bad.en: (meant: my sister is very chatty; she can talk all afternoon)
bad.why: It needs a group of people talking at once. It cannot describe one talkative person.

bad.s: 全班同学{七嘴八舌}地回答：“明白了！”
bad.en: (meant: the whole class answered together, "Got it!")
bad.why: It means many different voices at once. A whole class saying the same words together needs yi kou tong sheng.

cards.mean: to come straight to the point
cards.lit: open the door and see the mountain

story.text: The phrase began as a term of literary criticism. The Southern Song critic Yan Yu wrote that Li Bai's opening lines were 'open the door and see the mountain': his poems show their subject from the very first line, with no lead-in. Later it came to describe any speech or writing that gets to the point at once.

use.how: Used as a predicate or adverbial about speaking or writing: 我就开门见山了。 他开门见山地问。 文章开门见山。

near.diff: 拐弯抹角 is the opposite: talking around the point instead of stating it.
直截了当 is directness in general, also in refusing or acting; 开门见山 is about raising the main point first.

cards.cue: You meet a busy client for the first time. With ten minutes before their flight, you skip the small talk and state your proposal in your first sentence.

ctx.s: 时间不多，我就{开门见山}了：这个项目需要再加两个人。
ctx.en: We don't have much time, so I'll get straight to it: this project needs two more people.

ctx.s: 他一坐下就{开门见山}地问：“你打算什么时候还钱？”
ctx.en: The moment he sat down he asked outright: "When are you going to pay me back?"

ctx.s: 这篇文章{开门见山}，第一句就提出了作者的观点。
ctx.en: This article gets straight to the point; the very first sentence states the author's view.

ctx.s: 写求职信最好{开门见山}，先说明你申请的是哪个职位。
ctx.en: In a cover letter it's best to be direct and say first which position you are applying for.

ctx.s: 王经理说话一向{开门见山}，从来不绕弯子。
ctx.en: Manager Wang always gets straight to the point and never beats about the bush.

ctx.s: 别铺垫那么多了，{开门见山}地说吧，你到底想让我帮什么忙？
ctx.en: Enough of the lead-up. Get to the point: what exactly do you want me to help with?

bad.s: 我一打开窗户就{开门见山}，风景真美。
bad.en: (meant: as soon as I opened the window I saw the mountains)
bad.why: It is only used figuratively, about speaking or writing; it never describes a real view.

bad.s: 他{开门见山}地把房子卖了。
bad.en: (meant: he sold the house without hesitating)
bad.why: It is about raising the main point in speech or writing, not about doing something decisively.

cards.mean: to beat around the bush
cards.lit: to turn the bends and skirt round the corners

use.how: Mostly an adverbial or predicate about roundabout talk: 别拐弯抹角了。 他拐弯抹角地问。 Can also describe a winding route.

near.diff: 开门见山 is the opposite: raising the main point at once.
吞吞吐吐 is halting, hesitant speech; 拐弯抹角 can be fluent but avoids the point.

cards.cue: Your roommate talks for ten minutes about rising prices and his tough job, and only at the very end hints that he'd like to borrow some money.

ctx.s: 有话直说，别{拐弯抹角}的。
ctx.en: Say what you mean. Stop beating around the bush.

ctx.s: 他{拐弯抹角}地问了半天，原来是想借我的车。
ctx.en: He hinted around for ages, and it turned out he wanted to borrow my car.

ctx.s: 她不好意思直接拒绝，就{拐弯抹角}地说自己最近太忙。
ctx.en: She was too embarrassed to refuse outright, so she said in a roundabout way that she'd been very busy lately.

ctx.s: 你{拐弯抹角}说了这么多，到底想要什么？
ctx.en: You've gone round in circles for so long. What is it you actually want?

ctx.s: 批评下属的时候，他总是{拐弯抹角}，结果对方根本没听懂。
ctx.en: When he criticises his staff he always talks around it, so the person never gets the message.

ctx.s: 出租车在老城的小巷里{拐弯抹角}，开了很久才到。
ctx.en: The taxi wound its way through the old town's alleys and took ages to get there.

bad.s: 这个问题很复杂，他{拐弯抹角}地解释得非常清楚。
bad.en: (meant: he explained this complex issue very clearly, from every angle)
bad.why: It criticises avoiding the point, so it cannot go with praise for a clear explanation.

bad.s: 他太{拐弯抹角}了，到现在还没决定。
bad.en: (meant: he is so indecisive that he still hasn't decided)
bad.why: It is about roundabout talk or a winding route, not about being unable to make up one's mind.

cards.mean: sweet talk, honeyed words
cards.lit: sweet words and honeyed speech

use.how: A noun phrase, usually an object: 说甜言蜜语, 被甜言蜜语骗了. Implies words meant to please or win someone over, often insincere; between lovers it can be light.

near.diff: 花言巧语 is clever, deceptive talk used to trick someone; 甜言蜜语 is flattering, affectionate talk that may or may not be sincere.

cards.cue: Every time your friend's boyfriend forgets something important, he makes up for it with a flood of compliments and promises he never keeps.

ctx.s: 他就会说{甜言蜜语}，真到需要帮忙的时候人就不见了。
ctx.en: All he's good at is sweet talk; when you actually need help, he's nowhere to be found.

ctx.s: 别被推销员的{甜言蜜语}骗了，先看看合同。
ctx.en: Don't be taken in by the salesman's sweet talk; read the contract first.

ctx.s: 刚谈恋爱的时候，他每天都对我说{甜言蜜语}。
ctx.en: When we first started dating, he said sweet things to me every day.

ctx.s: 妈妈提醒她：“光听{甜言蜜语}没用，要看他怎么做。”
ctx.en: Her mother warned her: "Sweet words mean nothing; watch what he does."

ctx.s: 这些{甜言蜜语}我早就听腻了，你还是说点实在的吧。
ctx.en: I'm sick of all this honeyed talk. Tell me something real.

ctx.s: 故事里的骗子靠着{甜言蜜语}，骗走了老人一辈子的积蓄。
ctx.en: In the story, the con man used sweet talk to cheat the old man out of his life savings.

bad.s: 老师的{甜言蜜语}让我很感动，我决定更加努力。
bad.en: (meant: my teacher's kind encouragement moved me, so I decided to work harder)
bad.why: It suggests flattery meant to win someone over, often insincere, so it cannot describe a teacher's sincere encouragement.

bad.s: 这家店的蛋糕真是{甜言蜜语}。
bad.en: (meant: this shop's cakes are really sweet)
bad.why: It is only about words, never about taste.

cards.mean: to say the same thing in unison
cards.lit: different mouths, the same voice

use.how: An adverbial before a speech verb: 大家异口同声地说。 Also used when everyone asked gives the same answer or opinion.

near.diff: 不约而同 is any action people happen to do together without arranging it; 异口同声 is only about saying the same thing.
七嘴八舌 is many people saying different things at once; 异口同声 is many saying the same thing.

cards.cue: You ask three children whether they want to go to the zoo, and all three shout "Yes!" at exactly the same moment.

ctx.s: 老师问：“作业写完了吗？”同学们{异口同声}地说：“写完了！”
ctx.en: The teacher asked, "Have you finished your homework?" and the class answered in chorus, "Yes!"

ctx.s: 我问两个孩子想吃什么，他们{异口同声}地喊：“冰淇淋！”
ctx.en: I asked the two kids what they wanted to eat, and they both shouted, "Ice cream!"

ctx.s: 双胞胎{异口同声}地叫了一声“爸爸”，把他逗笑了。
ctx.en: The twins said "Daddy!" in perfect unison, which made him laugh.

ctx.s: 问起这家餐厅，几位老顾客{异口同声}地说好。
ctx.en: When asked about this restaurant, the regulars all said the same thing: it's good.

ctx.s: 对于这个方案，评委们几乎{异口同声}地表示反对。
ctx.en: The judges objected to the plan almost with one voice.

ctx.s: 被问到谁最努力，队员们{异口同声}地喊出了队长的名字。
ctx.en: Asked who worked hardest, the players all called out the captain's name together.

bad.s: 我和朋友{异口同声}地穿了一样的衣服。
bad.en: (meant: my friend and I happened to wear the same clothes)
bad.why: It is only about speaking. Happening to wear the same clothes without arranging it is bu yue er tong.

bad.s: 大家{异口同声}地发表了不同的意见。
bad.en: (meant: everyone voiced different opinions at once)
bad.why: It means saying the same thing, so it contradicts different opinions. Many different voices at once is qi zui ba she.

cards.mean: to do the same thing without having agreed to
cards.lit: without arranging it, and yet the same

use.how: An adverbial before a verb, with two or more people as subject: 我们不约而同地笑了。 Stresses that the shared action was not planned.

near.diff: 异口同声 is only saying the same words; 不约而同 covers any action or reaction people happen to share.
不谋而合 is ideas or plans turning out to match; 不约而同 is mostly people doing the same thing at the same time.

cards.cue: Without texting each other, you and your sister both turn up at your parents' house on the same evening, each with a cake.

ctx.s: 听到这个消息，我们{不约而同}地笑了起来。
