ctx.en: When we heard the news, we all burst out laughing at the same time.

ctx.s: 聚会那天，我和她{不约而同}地穿了红裙子。
ctx.en: On the day of the party, she and I both happened to wear red dresses.

ctx.s: 你们俩是商量好的吗？怎么{不约而同}地选了同一个题目？
ctx.en: Did you two plan this? How did you both pick the same topic?

ctx.s: 两位作家{不约而同}地把故事放在了同一个小镇。
ctx.en: Independently of each other, the two writers set their stories in the same small town.

ctx.s: 停电以后，邻居们{不约而同}地走到楼下，互相打听情况。
ctx.en: After the power cut, the neighbours all came downstairs of their own accord to ask each other what was going on.

ctx.s: 那年春节，兄弟三人{不约而同}地回到了老家。
ctx.en: That Spring Festival, the three brothers all went back to their hometown without arranging it.

bad.s: 我们提前约好了，所以{不约而同}地在门口见面。
bad.en: (meant: we had arranged it, so we met at the door)
bad.why: It means without having arranged it, so it contradicts the first half: we had arranged it in advance.

bad.s: 他俩的性格{不约而同}，都很安静。
bad.en: (meant: their personalities are alike; both are quiet)
bad.why: It describes people happening to act alike at one moment, not a lasting likeness such as similar personalities.

cards.mean: from or in all directions
cards.lit: four sides and eight directions

use.how: Usually after 从, 向 or 来自, about people or things moving from or to every side: 从四面八方赶来, 向四面八方散去.

near.diff: 五湖四海 is about people coming from all over the country or world; 四面八方 is any movement from or to every direction, near or far.

cards.cue: A whistle blows in the park, and dogs come running back to their owners from every side.

ctx.s: 烟花一响，孩子们从{四面八方}跑了过来。
ctx.en: When the fireworks went off, children came running from every direction.

ctx.s: 鸽子被吓了一跳，向{四面八方}飞去。
ctx.en: Startled, the pigeons flew off in all directions.

ctx.s: 站在山顶往{四面八方}看，全是一片绿色。
ctx.en: From the top of the mountain, everything you see in every direction is green.

ctx.s: 地震发生后，救援人员从{四面八方}赶到灾区。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, rescuers rushed to the disaster area from all sides.

ctx.s: 我们班的同学来自{四面八方}，口音都不一样。
ctx.en: The students in our class come from all over, and they all have different accents.

ctx.s: 音乐节还没开始，从{四面八方}来的歌迷就挤满了公园。
ctx.en: Before the music festival had even started, fans from all around had packed the park.

bad.s: 这家超市的东西{四面八方}，什么都有。
bad.en: (meant: this supermarket has all kinds of things)
bad.why: It is about directions and places, not about a shop offering a wide variety of goods.

bad.s: 他{四面八方}地考虑了这个问题。
bad.en: (meant: he considered the problem from every angle)
bad.why: It means directions in space. It cannot describe thinking about a problem from every angle.

cards.mean: tens of thousands; vast numbers
cards.lit: reaching the thousands, climbing to the ten-thousands

use.how: A number phrase before a countable noun, with 的 or a measure word: 成千上万的游客, 成千上万只鸟. Used for people, animals and repeated events.

near.diff: 人山人海 paints a scene packed with people; 成千上万 states a huge number of any countable thing.

cards.cue: After one famous singer shared the charity's page, donations poured in from people beyond counting: not dozens, not hundreds, far more.

ctx.s: 每年春天，{成千上万}的游客来这里看樱花。
ctx.en: Every spring, tens of thousands of tourists come here to see the cherry blossoms.

ctx.s: 这个视频一发出去，就有{成千上万}的人点赞。
ctx.en: As soon as the video was posted, thousands upon thousands of people liked it.

ctx.s: 你知道吗？一个蜂巢里住着{成千上万}只蜜蜂。
ctx.en: Did you know a single hive is home to tens of thousands of bees?

ctx.s: 一到冬天，{成千上万}只候鸟飞到这片湖上过冬。
ctx.en: Every winter, vast numbers of migratory birds fly to this lake to spend the season.

ctx.s: 为了这个产品，工程师们做了{成千上万}次实验。
ctx.en: The engineers ran thousands upon thousands of tests for this product.

ctx.s: 这场洪水让{成千上万}的家庭失去了房子。
ctx.en: The flood left tens of thousands of families without homes.

bad.s: 我花了{成千上万}的时间学中文。
bad.en: (meant: I've spent a huge amount of time learning Chinese)
bad.why: It counts separate things such as people, animals or attempts. It cannot measure an amount of time.

bad.s: 广场上{成千上万}，挤得走不动。
bad.en: (meant: the square was so packed you couldn't move)
bad.why: It is a number phrase and needs a noun after it, such as people. A packed scene on its own is ren shan ren hai.

cards.mean: all kinds of; a bewildering variety
cards.lit: five flowers, eight gates: so many different kinds that you cannot keep track

use.how: Predicate or before 的, about a mixed assortment of things, ideas or methods: 说法五花八门. Often hints that the variety is confusing.

near.diff: 形形色色 is a calm 'of every sort', often about people; 五花八门 stresses that the mix is varied to the point of bewildering.
应有尽有 praises a complete supply of what you need; 五花八门 only says there are many different kinds.

cards.cue: Everyone in your group chat suggests a different cure for a cold: ginger, vinegar, sweating it out, hot cola. How do you describe the advice?

ctx.s: 超市里的饮料{五花八门}，我都不知道该买哪一种了。
ctx.en: There were so many kinds of drinks in the supermarket that I didn't know which one to buy.

ctx.s: 孩子们的回答{五花八门}，老师听了忍不住笑起来。
ctx.en: The children's answers were all over the place, and the teacher couldn't help laughing.

ctx.s: 他换过的工作{五花八门}：送过外卖，卖过保险，还当过导游。
ctx.en: He has done all sorts of jobs: delivering food, selling insurance, even working as a tour guide.

ctx.s: 网上关于减肥的说法{五花八门}，很多根本没有科学根据。
ctx.en: Online there are endless different claims about losing weight, and many have no scientific basis at all.

ctx.s: “你为什么不去那家培训班？”“他们的收费项目{五花八门}，我怕被骗。”
ctx.en: "Why didn't you sign up for that course?" "They charge for all kinds of different things; I was afraid of being cheated."

ctx.s: 近年来，{五花八门}的手机应用层出不穷，让不少老人无所适从。
ctx.en: In recent years a bewildering variety of phone apps has appeared, leaving many older people at a loss.

bad.s: 她今天穿的裙子很{五花八门}。
bad.en: (meant: her dress today is very colourful)
bad.why: It describes an assortment of many different kinds of things; a single dress cannot be that. For bright colours say sècǎi xiānyàn.

bad.s: 他是一个{五花八门}的人，什么都会。
bad.en: (meant: he is a versatile person who can do everything)
bad.why: It describes a mixed collection of things or ideas, not a person's talents. A versatile person is duō cái duō yì.

cards.mean: has everything one could want
cards.lit: whatever there should be, there is, all of it

use.how: Stands as a predicate after a list or a 从……到…… phrase, about shops, places or facilities: 吃的用的应有尽有. Takes no object.

near.diff: 一应俱全 is more formal and mostly about goods or facilities being complete; 应有尽有 is the everyday choice.
五花八门 only says there are many different kinds, often confusingly; 应有尽有 says everything you need is there.

cards.cue: A friend asks whether to pack towels, slippers and a hairdryer for the hotel. You tell them not to bother: the hotel provides every one of those.

ctx.s: 这家超市很大，吃的用的{应有尽有}。
ctx.en: This supermarket is huge; it has everything you could want to eat or use.

ctx.s: 新小区里幼儿园、医院、健身房{应有尽有}，生活非常方便。
ctx.en: The new estate has a kindergarten, a clinic, a gym, everything, so life there is very convenient.

ctx.s: “去露营要带什么？”“不用带，营地里帐篷、烧烤架{应有尽有}。”
ctx.en: "What do I need to bring camping?" "Nothing, the campsite has tents, barbecues, the lot."

ctx.s: 别看这个小店不起眼，修车用的零件却{应有尽有}。
ctx.en: The little shop doesn't look like much, but it stocks every car part you could need.

ctx.s: 酒店的早餐{应有尽有}，中餐西餐随便选。
ctx.en: The hotel breakfast has everything; you can choose Chinese or Western as you like.

ctx.s: 展会上，从传统手工艺品到最新的电子产品，{应有尽有}，吸引了大批游客。
ctx.en: The fair had everything from traditional handicrafts to the latest electronics, and drew large crowds.

bad.s: 这个问题的答案{应有尽有}，大家说法都不一样。
bad.en: (meant: the answers to this question vary widely)
bad.why: It praises a complete supply of what you need, not a confusing variety of opinions; that is wǔ huā bā mén.

bad.s: 我们公司{应有尽有}一台新打印机。
bad.en: (meant: our company has a new printer)
bad.why: It is a complete predicate and cannot take an object; it also means a full range, not one item. Just use the verb yǒu.

cards.mean: unique, one of a kind
cards.lit: only one, with no second

use.how: Predicate, usually 是……的, or before 的: 每个人的指纹都是独一无二的. Said of a thing, place or quality of which no other exists.

near.diff: 与众不同 means standing out from the rest; 独一无二 means there is literally only one of it.
绝无仅有 stresses that something almost never happens or exists at all; 独一无二 simply says there is no second one.

cards.cue: Your grandmother embroidered a quilt by hand just for you, and no copy of it exists anywhere in the world. How do you describe it?

ctx.s: 每个人的指纹都是{独一无二}的。
ctx.en: Everyone's fingerprints are unique.

ctx.s: 这条项链是奶奶留给我的，对我来说{独一无二}。
ctx.en: My grandmother left me this necklace; to me there is nothing else like it.

ctx.s: 这家店的杯子都是手工做的，每一个都{独一无二}。
ctx.en: This shop's cups are all handmade, so each one is one of a kind.

ctx.s: “这幅画能买到复制品吗？”“买不到，它是{独一无二}的。”
ctx.en: "Can I buy a copy of this painting?" "No, there is only one."

ctx.s: 他在这方面的经验，在全公司可以说是{独一无二}的。
ctx.en: His experience in this area is, you could say, unmatched in the whole company.

ctx.s: 这座古桥的结构在国内{独一无二}，具有很高的研究价值。
ctx.en: The structure of this old bridge is unique in the country and of great value for research.

bad.s: 她今天穿得很{独一无二}，大家都在看她。
bad.en: (meant: she is dressed very unusually today and everyone is looking)
bad.why: An outfit that stands out is yǔ zhòng bù tóng; this idiom means only one exists, not that a style is unusual.

bad.s: 我们班有两个{独一无二}的学生。
bad.en: (meant: our class has two exceptional students)
bad.why: It means there is only one of something, so 'two one-of-a-kind students' contradicts itself.

cards.mean: out of the ordinary, unlike everyone else
cards.lit: not the same as the crowd

use.how: Predicate or before 的, about a person, style or idea that stands out from most others: 他的想法与众不同. Takes no object: 众 is already what it is compared with.

near.diff: 独一无二 means only one exists; 与众不同 means unlike most others, though there may be more like it.
别具一格 is more written and praises a distinctive style in art or design; 与众不同 is everyday and wider.

cards.cue: In an office where everyone wears grey suits, the new colleague walks in wearing a bright orange jacket and a bow tie. How does he look?

ctx.s: 她的发型{与众不同}，在人群里一眼就能认出来。
ctx.en: Her hairstyle is so unusual that you can spot her in a crowd at a glance.

ctx.s: 这家餐厅的装修{与众不同}，看起来像一座小图书馆。
ctx.en: This restaurant is decorated unlike any other; it looks like a little library.

ctx.s: “你为什么喜欢他？”“他看问题的角度总是{与众不同}。”
ctx.en: "Why do you like him?" "He always looks at things from an angle nobody else does."

ctx.s: 想让产品卖得好，就得做出点{与众不同}的东西。
ctx.en: If you want a product to sell, you have to make something that stands out.

ctx.s: 他从小就显得{与众不同}，别的孩子玩游戏，他却在看地图。
ctx.en: Even as a child he seemed different: while other kids played games, he pored over maps.

ctx.s: 这位导演的作品风格{与众不同}，在业内很受关注。
ctx.en: This director's style is unlike anyone else's and draws a lot of attention in the industry.

bad.s: 我和哥哥{与众不同}，他爱运动，我爱看书。
bad.en: (meant: my brother and I are different from each other)
bad.why: It says someone stands out from most people, not that two people differ from each other. Say hěn bù yíyàng.

bad.s: 她的性格{与众不同}她妈妈。
bad.en: (meant: her personality is different from her mother's)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; the comparison is always with 'the crowd'. Say hé tā māma bù yíyàng.

cards.mean: largely the same with minor differences
cards.lit: alike in the large, different in the small

use.how: Predicate about two or more things being compared: 这几款手机大同小异. Often implies the choice hardly matters or nothing stands out.

near.diff: 一模一样 means exactly identical; 大同小异 admits small differences.
半斤八两 says two sides are equally bad, as a criticism; 大同小异 is a neutral comparison.

cards.cue: You compare three phone contracts and find they differ only by a few details in the small print. How do you sum them up?

ctx.s: 这几款手机{大同小异}，买哪个都行。
ctx.en: These phones are all much the same; any of them will do.

ctx.s: 我看了好几本语法书，内容都{大同小异}。
ctx.en: I've looked at several grammar books and their content is pretty much the same.

ctx.s: “这两家店的菜单有什么区别？”“{大同小异}，就是一家多了几道甜点。”
ctx.en: "What's the difference between the two restaurants' menus?" "They're much the same; one just has a few more desserts."

ctx.s: 两家公司的方案{大同小异}，只是价格差一点。
ctx.en: The two companies' proposals are basically the same, apart from a small difference in price.

ctx.s: 很多景点卖的纪念品都{大同小异}，没什么特色。
ctx.en: The souvenirs at many tourist sites are all much alike, with nothing special about them.

ctx.s: 各地的春节习俗{大同小异}，都寄托着人们对团圆的期盼。
ctx.en: Spring Festival customs vary only a little from place to place, and all express the hope of family reunion.

bad.s: 这两个城市{大同小异}，一个在北方很冷，一个在南方很热。
bad.en: (meant: these two cities are very different)
bad.why: It says the things are basically the same, so it cannot introduce big differences. Say wánquán bù tóng.

bad.s: 我和他{大同小异}地完成了作业。
bad.en: (meant: he and I did the homework in almost the same way)
bad.why: It is a predicate comparing things, not an adverb with de. Say that the two pieces of homework are dà tóng xiǎo yì.

cards.mean: perfect in every way
cards.lit: complete in ten parts, beautiful in ten parts

use.how: Predicate or before 的, very often negated or with 想/要求/做到: 世上没有十全十美的人. Often used to say that perfection is unrealistic.

near.diff: 完美无缺 is a direct 'flawless', mostly affirmative; 十全十美 is the usual word in sayings that nothing is perfect.
美中不足 names the one flaw in something good; 十全十美 says there is no flaw at all.

cards.cue: Your friend will only date someone rich, kind, handsome, funny and a great cook. You tell them nobody like that exists.

ctx.s: 世界上没有{十全十美}的人，你别对自己太苛刻。
ctx.en: Nobody in the world is perfect; don't be so hard on yourself.

ctx.s: 这个计划不可能{十全十美}，能解决主要问题就行。
ctx.en: This plan can't be perfect; it's enough if it solves the main problems.

ctx.s: “这房子怎么样？”“交通方便，价格合理，简直{十全十美}。”
ctx.en: "How's the flat?" "Good transport links, reasonable price, it's practically perfect."

ctx.s: 他做什么都想做到{十全十美}，所以常常很累。
ctx.en: He wants everything he does to be perfect, so he's often exhausted.

ctx.s: 找对象别要求{十全十美}，两个人合得来最重要。
ctx.en: Don't demand perfection in a partner; what matters most is that you get along.

ctx.s: 任何制度都难以做到{十全十美}，需要在实践中不断完善。
ctx.en: No system can be perfect; it has to be improved continually in practice.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜{十全十美}，就是太咸了。
bad.en: (meant: the food is great except that it is too salty)
bad.why: Perfect means no flaw, so it cannot be followed by a flaw. For a good thing with one drawback use měi zhōng bù zú.

bad.s: 他这次考试考了{十全十美}分。
bad.en: (meant: he got full marks in the exam)
bad.why: It is not a number and cannot go before fēn. Full marks is mǎnfēn.

cards.mean: a small flaw in something otherwise good
cards.lit: within the beauty, something falls short

use.how: Mostly as 美中不足的是…… after praising something, to name its one drawback: 环境很好，美中不足的是离地铁远.

near.diff: 十全十美 means flawless; 美中不足 points to the one flaw in something good.
白璧微瑕 'a tiny blemish on white jade' is literary; 美中不足 is the everyday way to say it.

cards.cue: You describe a holiday with great food, kind hosts and beautiful beaches, then add that it rained every single afternoon.

ctx.s: 这次旅行很开心，{美中不足}的是天天下雨。
ctx.en: The trip was great fun; the only pity was that it rained every day.

ctx.s: 这家酒店环境很好，{美中不足}的是离地铁有点远。
ctx.en: The hotel is lovely; the one drawback is that it's a bit far from the metro.

ctx.s: “新手机怎么样？”“拍照很清楚，就是电池不太耐用，有点{美中不足}。”
ctx.en: "How's the new phone?" "The camera is sharp, but the battery doesn't last; that's the one letdown."

ctx.s: 婚礼办得很热闹，唯一{美中不足}的是奶奶生病没能来。
ctx.en: The wedding was a lively affair; the one thing missing was Grandma, who was ill and couldn't come.

ctx.s: 这部电影故事精彩，演员出色，只是结尾仓促，算是{美中不足}。
ctx.en: The film has a great story and fine actors; only the rushed ending lets it down a little.

ctx.s: 该产品设计新颖，性能稳定，{美中不足}之处在于价格偏高。
ctx.en: The product is innovative in design and reliable in performance; its one shortcoming is the rather high price.

bad.s: 这家餐厅又脏又贵，{美中不足}的是服务员也很凶。
bad.en: (meant: the restaurant is dirty and expensive, and the staff are rude too)
bad.why: It needs something that is good overall; you cannot add one more flaw to a list of flaws with it.

bad.s: 我的钱{美中不足}，买不起这台电脑。
bad.en: (meant: I don't have enough money to buy this computer)
bad.why: The idiom is about a flaw in something good, not about lacking money. Say that the money is bú gòu.

cards.mean: dumbstruck, staring in shock
cards.lit: eyes staring wide, mouth gone slack

use.how: Predicate, or after 得 with 看/惊/吓: 孩子们看得目瞪口呆. About a sudden shock or amazement that leaves someone speechless.

near.diff: 瞠目结舌 is more written and also covers being left tongue-tied; 目瞪口呆 is the everyday word for being stunned.
呆若木鸡 'stiff as a wooden chicken' stresses being frozen and unable to react; 目瞪口呆 stresses the staring, open-mouthed amazement.

cards.cue: A street performer pulls a live rabbit out of a stranger's empty backpack, and the whole crowd just stands there staring, mouths open.

ctx.s: 魔术师把硬币变没了，孩子们看得{目瞪口呆}。
ctx.en: The magician made the coin vanish, and the children stared in amazement.

ctx.s: 听说他辞职去环游世界，我们都{目瞪口呆}。
ctx.en: When we heard he'd quit his job to travel the world, we were all speechless.

ctx.s: “你看到账单了吗？”“看到了，我当时就{目瞪口呆}。”
ctx.en: "Did you see the bill?" "I did. I just stood there, stunned."

ctx.s: 那个小女孩一口气背出了整篇长文，评委们惊得{目瞪口呆}。
ctx.en: The little girl recited the whole long text in one go, and the judges were dumbfounded.

ctx.s: 他推开门，看见满地的水，顿时{目瞪口呆}，不知道该怎么办。
ctx.en: He opened the door to find the floor covered in water and froze, staring, with no idea what to do.

ctx.s: 巨浪扑上岸的一瞬间，围观的游客个个{目瞪口呆}。
ctx.en: The moment the huge wave crashed onto the shore, every onlooker stood there stunned.

bad.s: 他上课时{目瞪口呆}地看着窗外，想着周末去哪儿玩。
bad.en: (meant: in class he stared blankly out of the window, daydreaming)
bad.why: It is shock or amazement, not idle daydreaming. For staring into space say fādāi.

bad.s: 她很生气，{目瞪口呆}地骂了他一顿。
bad.en: (meant: she was furious and gave him a telling-off)
bad.why: Its second half means too stunned to speak, so it cannot describe someone scolding. It is shock, not anger.

cards.mean: listless, lacking energy
cards.lit: no energy, no spark to raise: too drained to look lively

use.how: Predicate (often with 的) or adverbial with 地, about a person's state at the moment, from tiredness, boredom or illness: 他今天无精打采的.

near.diff: 垂头丧气 is dejection after a setback; 无精打采 is low energy, often just from tiredness or boredom.
愁眉苦脸 is a face showing worry; 无精打采 is a body and manner with no energy.

cards.cue: Your roommate gamed until four in the morning; now at lunch they sit slumped over the table, yawning, barely touching their food.

ctx.s: 他昨晚没睡好，今天上课一直{无精打采}的。
ctx.en: He slept badly last night and has been listless all through class today.

ctx.s: 你怎么{无精打采}的？是不是感冒了？
ctx.en: Why are you so sluggish? Have you caught a cold?

ctx.s: 周一早上，办公室里的人都{无精打采}地对着电脑。
ctx.en: On Monday morning everyone in the office sat in front of their screens with no energy at all.

ctx.s: 她一边{无精打采}地翻着书，一边不停地打哈欠。
ctx.en: She leafed half-heartedly through the book, yawning the whole time.

ctx.s: 这盆花好几天没浇水，叶子都{无精打采}地垂着。
ctx.en: This plant hasn't been watered for days, and its leaves hang limply.

ctx.s: 长期熬夜会让人白天{无精打采}，工作效率明显下降。
ctx.en: Staying up late night after night leaves people listless by day, and their efficiency drops markedly.

bad.s: 这个菜{无精打采}，一点味道也没有。
bad.en: (meant: this dish is bland, it has no flavour)
bad.why: It describes the low energy of a person, or figuratively a drooping plant, never the taste of food.

bad.s: 他天生是个{无精打采}的人，从来不努力。
bad.en: (meant: he is lazy by nature and never makes an effort)
bad.why: It is a passing state of low energy, not a character trait or laziness. Say that he is lǎn.

cards.mean: wearing a worried, miserable face
cards.lit: worried eyebrows, bitter face

use.how: Predicate (often with 的) or adverbial with 地, about someone whose face shows worry over a problem: 你别整天愁眉苦脸的. Can sound mildly reproachful.

near.diff: 闷闷不乐 is quiet unhappiness kept inside; 愁眉苦脸 is worry that shows on the face.
无精打采 is lack of energy from tiredness or boredom; 愁眉苦脸 is a worried face over a problem.

cards.cue: Your neighbour runs a small café. All week no customers come, and he sits behind the counter, brow knotted, sighing over the rent.

ctx.s: 你别整天{愁眉苦脸}的，事情总会解决的。
ctx.en: Don't go around with that worried face all day; things will work out.

ctx.s: 儿子拿着不及格的试卷回家，{愁眉苦脸}地站在门口。
ctx.en: Our son came home with a failed test and stood at the door looking miserable.

ctx.s: “你怎么{愁眉苦脸}的？”“房东又要涨房租了。”
ctx.en: "Why the long face?" "The landlord is putting the rent up again."

ctx.s: 一想到下个月要还的贷款，他就{愁眉苦脸}的。
ctx.en: Whenever he thinks about next month's loan repayment, his face clouds with worry.

ctx.s: 店里一整天都没有客人，老板坐在柜台后面{愁眉苦脸}地叹气。
ctx.en: Not a single customer came all day, and the owner sat behind the counter sighing, his face full of worry.

ctx.s: 与其{愁眉苦脸}地抱怨，不如想想办法改变现状。
ctx.en: Rather than complaining with a long face, it's better to find a way to change things.

bad.s: 他睡了一整天还是很困，{愁眉苦脸}地打着哈欠。
bad.en: (meant: even after sleeping all day he was still drowsy and yawning)
bad.why: It shows worry over a problem, not sleepiness. For someone drowsy and drained use wú jīng dǎ cǎi.

bad.s: 考试得了满分，她{愁眉苦脸}地跑回家告诉妈妈。
bad.en: (meant: she got full marks and ran home happily to tell her mother)
bad.why: It is a worried, miserable face, the opposite of the joy of good news. For delight say gāo gāo xìng xìng.

cards.mean: dejected and crestfallen
cards.lit: head hanging down, spirit lost

story.text: The phrase is known from Han Yu's mock-serious essay "Sending Off Poverty". He prepares a cart and a boat to send away the spirits of poverty that have dogged him all his life, but they answer back and argue that they made him who he is. In the end the host hangs his head in dejection, thanks them, burns the cart and boat, and invites them to the seat of honour.

use.how: Describes how someone looks right after a setback; as predicate or adverbial: 他垂头丧气地走了。

near.diff: 心灰意冷 is losing hope and will inside, often after many failures; 垂头丧气 is the visible slump right after one setback.
闷闷不乐 is quiet, brooding unhappiness with any cause; 垂头丧气 is the drooping look of someone who has just failed or lost.

cards.cue: Your little brother's team lost the final, and he walks home with his head down, dragging his schoolbag. How does he look?

ctx.s: 比赛输了，队员们都{垂头丧气}的。
ctx.en: They lost the match, and all the players looked crestfallen.

ctx.s: 他考完试{垂头丧气}地走出教室，我就知道没考好。
ctx.en: He walked out of the exam room looking so dejected that I knew it had gone badly.

ctx.s: 别{垂头丧气}了，这次没成功，下次再来！
ctx.en: Don't look so down. It didn't work this time; we'll try again next time!

ctx.s: 面试回来，她一副{垂头丧气}的样子，什么也不想说。
ctx.en: She came back from the interview looking utterly downcast and didn't want to talk.

ctx.s: “怎么{垂头丧气}的？比赛输了？”
ctx.en: "Why are you hanging your head like that? Did you lose the match?"

ctx.s: 钓了一整天一条鱼也没钓到，爷爷{垂头丧气}地收起了鱼竿。
ctx.en: After a whole day without catching a single fish, Grandpa glumly packed up his rod.

bad.s: 听说自己被录取了，他{垂头丧气}地跳了起来。
bad.en: (meant: he jumped up with excitement on hearing he got in)
bad.why: It describes the slumped look of defeat, so it cannot go with good news or jumping for joy.

bad.s: 爷爷去世以后，她{垂头丧气}了好几年。
bad.en: (meant: she grieved for years after her grandfather died)
bad.why: It is the short-lived slump after a setback or loss in a contest, not deep or lasting grief over a death; say bēitòng or shāngxīn instead.

cards.mean: in low spirits, unhappy
cards.lit: pent-up and gloomy, not happy

use.how: Describes quiet, brooding unhappiness that someone keeps to themselves; predicate or adverbial: 她整天闷闷不乐。

near.diff: 垂头丧气 is the visible slump after a defeat; 闷闷不乐 is a quiet, inward low mood, often with an unspoken cause.

cards.cue: Since moving to the new city, your friend hardly talks, sits alone at lunch and never smiles, but won't say what is wrong. How is she?

ctx.s: 他今天一直{闷闷不乐}，不知道怎么了。
ctx.en: He's been in low spirits all day; I don't know what's wrong.

ctx.s: 搬家以后，孩子想念老朋友，整天{闷闷不乐}。
ctx.en: After the move the child missed his old friends and moped about all day.

ctx.s: 你最近怎么总是{闷闷不乐}的？有心事就说出来吧。
ctx.en: Why have you been so down lately? If something's on your mind, tell me.

ctx.s: 她{闷闷不乐}地吃完饭，一句话也没说就回房间了。
ctx.en: She finished her meal glumly and went back to her room without a word.

ctx.s: 妈妈看出我{闷闷不乐}，就带我出去散散心。
ctx.en: Mum could see I was feeling low, so she took me out to take my mind off things.

ctx.s: 退休后的头几个月，父亲在家无事可做，有些{闷闷不乐}。
ctx.en: For the first few months after retiring, my father had nothing to do at home and was rather out of sorts.

bad.s: 这个房间没有窗户，很{闷闷不乐}。
bad.en: (meant: the room has no windows and is very stuffy)
bad.why: Mèn here is about a person's mood, not stuffy air; for a room say hěn mèn or bù tōngfēng.

bad.s: 他{闷闷不乐}地大哭大闹，把东西摔了一地。
bad.en: (meant: he cried and threw a tantrum, smashing things)
bad.why: It is a quiet, held-in low mood; it cannot describe loud crying or a tantrum.

cards.mean: overwhelmed with grief
cards.lit: grief so sharp one is about to break

use.how: Describes a person's extreme grief, usually over a death or a great loss; predicate or adverbial: 她悲痛欲绝。

cards.cue: A woman receives the call that her only son has died in an accident. She collapses, unable to stop weeping. How is she?

ctx.s: 听到母亲去世的消息，他{悲痛欲绝}。
ctx.en: When he heard that his mother had died, he was overcome with grief.

ctx.s: 在葬礼上，她{悲痛欲绝}，几次哭得站不起来。
ctx.en: At the funeral she was so stricken with grief that several times she couldn't stand up for crying.

ctx.s: 地震中失去亲人的村民们{悲痛欲绝}。
ctx.en: The villagers who lost family in the earthquake were overwhelmed with grief.

ctx.s: 那只陪了他十几年的狗死了，老人{悲痛欲绝}，好几天吃不下饭。
ctx.en: The dog that had been with him for over ten years died; the old man was grief-stricken and couldn't eat for days.

ctx.s: 看着{悲痛欲绝}的家属，医生也说不出安慰的话。
ctx.en: Faced with the grief-stricken family, even the doctor could find no words of comfort.

ctx.s: 小说的最后，女主人公得知爱人牺牲，{悲痛欲绝}。
ctx.en: At the end of the novel, the heroine learns her beloved has died in battle and is overwhelmed with grief.

bad.s: 这部电影很{悲痛欲绝}，我看哭了。
bad.en: (meant: this film is very sad; it made me cry)
bad.why: It describes a grieving person, not a sad film or story; say the film is gǎnrén (moving) or bēishāng (sad).

bad.s: 他没被录取，我有点儿{悲痛欲绝}。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't get in, and I'm a bit sad about it)
bad.why: It names the most extreme grief, so yǒudiǎnr (a bit) contradicts it, and a rejection letter is far too small a cause.

cards.mean: to flare up in a rage
cards.lit: fire shooting up three zhang (about ten metres) high

use.how: A sudden burst of anger at something just heard or seen; often after 气得 or 一听就: 他一听就火冒三丈。

near.diff: 怒气冲冲 describes the furious manner in which someone walks or speaks; 火冒三丈 is the moment the anger explodes.
忍无可忍 says one's patience has finally run out after a long time; 火冒三丈 is a sudden flare, possibly at once.

cards.cue: Dad finds out that his son has secretly spent all the money saved for his school fees on a game. His face turns red at once and he starts shouting. What happened to Dad?

ctx.s: 看到房间这么乱，妈妈{火冒三丈}。
ctx.en: Seeing the room in such a mess, Mum hit the roof.

ctx.s: 他一听说车被人划了，立刻{火冒三丈}。
ctx.en: The moment he heard someone had scratched his car, he flew into a rage.

ctx.s: 别跟他提这件事，他一听就{火冒三丈}。
ctx.en: Don't mention it to him; he blows up as soon as he hears about it.

ctx.s: 老板看到报告里那么多错误，气得{火冒三丈}。
ctx.en: When the boss saw so many mistakes in the report, he was absolutely livid.

ctx.s: 看到电脑又被弟弟弄坏了，哥哥一下子{火冒三丈}。
ctx.en: Seeing that his little brother had broken the computer again, my brother instantly hit the roof.

ctx.s: 排了一个小时的队，却被告知没票了，谁能不{火冒三丈}？
ctx.en: After queuing for an hour you're told the tickets are gone. Who wouldn't explode?

bad.s: 他是一个{火冒三丈}的人，大家都怕他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a hot-tempered person and everyone fears him)
bad.why: It describes a single outburst, not a person's character; for temperament say píqi bàozào.

bad.s: 今天三十八度，我热得{火冒三丈}。
bad.en: (meant: it's thirty-eight degrees and I'm boiling hot)
bad.why: The fire is anger, not heat; it cannot describe hot weather.

cards.mean: to make a scene for no good reason
cards.lit: having no reason, yet picking a row

use.how: Criticises someone who makes a fuss or unreasonable demands; predicate, often in 别无理取闹 or 这是无理取闹.

cards.cue: A customer demands a refund for a shirt he has clearly worn for months, shouts at the cashier and refuses to leave. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 孩子想要玩具，就在商店里{无理取闹}。
ctx.en: The child wanted a toy, so he threw a fit in the shop for no good reason.

ctx.s: 别{无理取闹}了，这件事根本不是我的错。
ctx.en: Stop making a fuss over nothing; this wasn't my fault at all.

ctx.s: 那位顾客明明穿过了衣服还要退钱，简直是{无理取闹}。
ctx.en: That customer had clearly worn the clothes and still wanted a refund. It was a completely unreasonable scene.

ctx.s: “我只是晚回了十分钟，你就说我不爱你？你这是{无理取闹}！”
ctx.en: "I'm ten minutes late and you say I don't love you? You're being totally unreasonable!"

ctx.s: 有人在网上{无理取闹}，说作者抄袭，却拿不出任何证据。
ctx.en: Someone online stirred up trouble, accusing the author of plagiarism without any evidence.

ctx.s: 对于少数人的{无理取闹}，公司决定不予理会。
ctx.en: The company decided to ignore the baseless fuss made by a handful of people.

bad.s: 他的工资被无故扣了，就去公司{无理取闹}，要回了自己的钱。
bad.en: (meant: his pay was wrongly docked, so he went and argued until he got it back)
bad.why: It condemns the fuss as baseless; for a justified complaint say tǎo shuōfa or jù lǐ lì zhēng.

bad.s: 孩子们在公园里{无理取闹}，玩得很开心。
bad.en: (meant: the children were playing noisily in the park and having fun)
bad.why: It means making unreasonable trouble, not happy, noisy play; say dǎdǎ nàonào or wánnào.

cards.mean: calm and even-tempered
cards.lit: heart level, breath gentle

use.how: Describes a calm, unangry state, most often as an adverbial before a verb of speaking: 我们心平气和地谈一谈。

cards.cue: After a big argument, two flatmates agree to sit down the next evening, without shouting, and talk through who does the cleaning. How do they plan to talk?

ctx.s: 别吵了，我们{心平气和}地谈一谈吧。
ctx.en: Stop arguing. Let's talk this over calmly.

ctx.s: 不管客人说什么，她都能{心平气和}地回答。
ctx.en: Whatever the customers say, she can answer calmly.

ctx.s: 你先冷静一下，等你{心平气和}了我们再讨论。
ctx.en: Calm down first; we'll discuss it once you've cooled off.

ctx.s: 父亲没有打骂我，而是{心平气和}地给我讲道理。
ctx.en: My father didn't shout at me or hit me; he calmly reasoned with me.

ctx.s: 被人这样冤枉，你怎么还能这么{心平气和}？
ctx.en: How can you stay so calm after being wronged like that?

ctx.s: 每天散散步、喝喝茶，人也变得{心平气和}了。
ctx.en: With a daily walk and a cup of tea, one becomes much more even-tempered.

bad.s: 今天没有风，湖面很{心平气和}。
bad.en: (meant: there's no wind today and the lake is calm)
bad.why: It describes a person's temper, not calm water or weather; say the lake is píngjìng.

bad.s: 听音乐能{心平气和}我。
bad.en: (meant: listening to music calms me down)
bad.why: It is not a transitive verb and cannot take an object; put ràng before the person: ràng wǒ xīn píng qì hé.

cards.mean: pushed beyond what one can bear
cards.lit: enduring until nothing is left that can be endured

use.how: Says patience has finally run out after long putting up with something; often 终于忍无可忍 or 对……忍无可忍, followed by what one then does.

near.diff: 火冒三丈 is a sudden explosion of anger, possibly at once; 忍无可忍 stresses that one had put up with it for a long time first.

cards.cue: For a whole year your neighbour has played loud music past midnight. You asked politely five times. Tonight you finally call the police. Why?

ctx.s: 他天天迟到，经理终于{忍无可忍}了。
ctx.en: He was late every single day, and the manager finally ran out of patience.

ctx.s: 楼上每晚吵到半夜，我{忍无可忍}，只好报了警。
ctx.en: The people upstairs were noisy till midnight every night; I couldn't take it any more and called the police.

ctx.s: 同学们对他的态度已经{忍无可忍}了。
ctx.en: His classmates have had all they can stand of his attitude.

ctx.s: “我让了你这么多次，现在真是{忍无可忍}了！”
ctx.en: "I've given in to you so many times. Now I've really had enough!"

ctx.s: {忍无可忍}之下，她辞掉了那份工作。
ctx.en: Pushed past her limit, she quit that job.

ctx.s: 这家工厂长期污染河水，村民们{忍无可忍}，联名向政府反映。
ctx.en: The factory had polluted the river for years; the villagers could bear it no longer and jointly petitioned the authorities.

bad.s: 她很{忍无可忍}，什么委屈都能受得了。
bad.en: (meant: she is very patient and can put up with anything)
bad.why: It means the opposite: patience has run out. For someone who bears everything say hěn néng rěn.

bad.s: 我真的{忍无可忍}他了。
bad.en: (meant: I really can't stand him any more)
bad.why: It takes no object; put the person after duì before it: duì tā rěn wú kě rěn.

cards.mean: fuming, visibly furious
cards.lit: angry breath rushing out

use.how: Describes the visibly angry manner of an action, mostly as an adverbial: 他怒气冲冲地走进来。

near.diff: 火冒三丈 is the moment anger flares up; 怒气冲冲 describes how an angry person moves or speaks, e.g. storming in.

cards.cue: The door bangs open and the neighbour strides into the office, red-faced, waving a letter. How did he come in?

ctx.s: 他{怒气冲冲}地走了进来。
ctx.en: He stormed in, fuming.

ctx.s: 她{怒气冲冲}地挂了电话。
ctx.en: She hung up the phone in a fury.

ctx.s: 一个顾客{怒气冲冲}地拿着坏了的手机来找经理。
ctx.en: A customer came looking for the manager, furious, holding a broken phone.

ctx.s: 看他{怒气冲冲}的样子，大家都不敢说话。
ctx.en: Seeing how furious he looked, nobody dared to say a word.

ctx.s: “这是谁干的？”老师{怒气冲冲}地问。
ctx.en: "Who did this?" the teacher demanded angrily.

ctx.s: 会议刚开始十分钟，他就{怒气冲冲}地摔门而去。
ctx.en: Ten minutes into the meeting, he slammed the door and stormed out.

bad.s: 收到礼物，她{怒气冲冲}地向我道谢。
bad.en: (meant: she thanked me eagerly when she got the gift)
bad.why: It means fuming with anger; the eager, excited look is xìngchōngchōng, a different word.

bad.s: 我迟到了，他就{怒气冲冲}我。
bad.en: (meant: I was late, so he got furious with me)
bad.why: It describes the manner of an action and takes no object; say tā chòng wǒ fāhuǒ, or nù qì chōng chōng de chòng wǒ hǎn.

cards.mean: disheartened, having lost all hope and drive
cards.lit: heart turned to ash, will gone cold

use.how: Losing hope and the will to go on, usually after repeated failure or disappointment; predicate, often with 让人 or 感到: 他心灰意冷。

near.diff: 垂头丧气 is the visible slump right after one setback; 心灰意冷 is a deeper, inner loss of hope that makes one want to give up.

cards.cue: After three years of auditions and dozens of rejections, a young actor says he no longer believes in his dream and is thinking of giving up acting. How does he feel?

ctx.s: 连续失败了好几次，他{心灰意冷}，不想再试了。
ctx.en: After failing several times in a row, he lost heart and didn't want to try again.

ctx.s: 投了上百份简历都没有回音，她渐渐{心灰意冷}。
ctx.en: She sent out over a hundred CVs without a single reply, and gradually lost heart.

ctx.s: 别因为一次挫折就{心灰意冷}，你还年轻。
ctx.en: Don't lose all hope over one setback; you're still young.

ctx.s: 父母一次次的不理解，让他对家庭彻底{心灰意冷}。
ctx.en: His parents' repeated failure to understand him left him completely disillusioned with his family.

ctx.s: 就在他{心灰意冷}、准备放弃的时候，出版社打来了电话。
ctx.en: Just when he had lost all heart and was ready to give up, the publisher called.

ctx.s: 多年的努力换来的却是背叛，老人{心灰意冷}，从此不再过问公司的事。
ctx.en: Years of effort were repaid with betrayal; the old man lost all heart and never again concerned himself with the company.

bad.s: 外面下雪了，我{心灰意冷}，赶紧多穿了一件衣服。
bad.en: (meant: it's snowing and I feel cold, so I put on another layer)
bad.why: The coldness is loss of hope and will, not physical cold; say wǒ juéde hěn lěng.

bad.s: 我有点{心灰意冷}，所以明天还要再试十次！
bad.en: (meant: I'm a bit discouraged, but I'll try ten more times tomorrow)
bad.why: It means losing the will to carry on, so it cannot lead into renewed effort; say yǒudiǎn shīwàng (a bit let down).

cards.mean: to regret something when it is too late to undo
cards.lit: regret that can no longer reach back

use.how: Regret that comes too late to change anything; predicate without an object, often in warnings: 否则会后悔莫及。

cards.cue: You warn a friend: if he skips the visa check now, he may be turned away at the airport and lose the whole trip, and then nothing can be done. What will he feel?

ctx.s: 现在不好好学习，以后会{后悔莫及}的。
ctx.en: If you don't study properly now, you'll regret it later when it's too late.

ctx.s: 他没听医生的话，病情加重才{后悔莫及}。
ctx.en: He ignored the doctor's advice, and only when he got worse did he regret it, too late.

ctx.s: 签合同前一定要看清楚，否则{后悔莫及}。
ctx.en: Read the contract carefully before you sign, or you'll regret it when nothing can be done.

ctx.s: 等到房子卖了，他才发现价格涨了一倍，真是{后悔莫及}。
ctx.en: Only after he sold the house did he find the price had doubled. The regret came far too late.

ctx.s: “那句话我说出口就{后悔莫及}了，可是已经收不回来了。”
ctx.en: "The moment I said it I regretted it, but there was no taking it back."

ctx.s: 很多人直到失去健康才{后悔莫及}，觉得当初不该拼命加班。
ctx.en: Many people only regret it once their health is gone, wishing they hadn't worked themselves so hard.

bad.s: 我{后悔莫及}，所以马上去向他道歉，问题解决了。
bad.en: (meant: I regretted it, so I apologised at once and sorted it out)
bad.why: Mò jí means it is too late to put right; if it could still be fixed, just say wǒ hěn hòuhuǐ.

bad.s: 我{后悔莫及}昨天说的话。
bad.en: (meant: I regret what I said yesterday)
bad.why: It takes no object; put the object after duì before it, or use plain hòuhuǐ with an object.

cards.mean: panic-stricken, losing one's head
cards.lit: so alarmed and flustered that one loses all sense of what to do

use.how: Predicate, or adverbial with 地: 他惊慌失措地跑了出去。 Describes a frightened reaction to sudden danger or shocking news; often in 不要惊慌失措.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is a frantic, disorganised rush, often just from being busy; 惊慌失措 is panic caused by fear or shock.
不知所措 is being at a loss what to do, from confusion or embarrassment; 惊慌失措 adds fright and panic.

cards.cue: The ship suddenly lurches and the alarm sounds; passengers scream and run in all directions, too frightened to think. How do they react?

ctx.s: 听到火警响了，几个孩子{惊慌失措}地跑出了教室。
ctx.en: When the fire alarm went off, a few children ran out of the classroom in a panic.

ctx.s: 遇到地震时千万不要{惊慌失措}，先躲到桌子下面。
ctx.en: If there is an earthquake, whatever you do, don't panic; get under a table first.

ctx.s: 飞机突然剧烈颠簸，乘客们{惊慌失措}，空姐却很镇定。
ctx.en: The plane suddenly shook violently; the passengers panicked, but the flight attendant stayed calm.

ctx.s: “你刚才怎么那么{惊慌失措}？”“我以为钱包被偷了。”
ctx.en: "Why were you in such a panic just now?" "I thought my wallet had been stolen."

ctx.s: 突然停电了，值班经理没有{惊慌失措}，马上启动了备用电源。
ctx.en: The power suddenly went out; the duty manager didn't panic and switched on the backup supply at once.

ctx.s: 看到他{惊慌失措}的样子，我就知道出大事了。
ctx.en: When I saw how panic-stricken he looked, I knew something serious had happened.

bad.s: 明天就要考试了，我{惊慌失措}地复习了一整夜。
bad.en: (meant: I was nervous and revised all night before the exam)
bad.why: It is a sudden panic in the face of danger or a shock, not ongoing nervousness while working; say you revised nervously (jǐnzhāng) instead.

bad.s: 收到录取通知书，她高兴得{惊慌失措}。
bad.en: (meant: she was beside herself with joy at the acceptance letter)
bad.why: The panic comes from fear or alarm, never from happiness; for joy, say she jumped for joy (gāoxìng de tiào le qǐlai).

cards.mean: for no reason at all
cards.lit: without cause and without reason

use.how: Adverbial before a verb, or attributive with 的: 他无缘无故发脾气。 Often in complaints, or in 不会无缘无故… (there must be a reason).

near.diff: 莫名其妙 says something baffles the speaker and makes no sense; 无缘无故 states that an action or event had no cause.

cards.cue: Your manager cancels your approved leave, gives no cause, and nothing you did could explain it. How did he cancel it?

ctx.s: 我又没惹他，他今天却{无缘无故}冲我发了一通火。
ctx.en: I hadn't done anything to him, yet today he blew up at me for no reason at all.

ctx.s: 陌生人{无缘无故}送的礼物，我是不会收的。
ctx.en: I won't accept a gift a stranger gives me for no reason.

ctx.s: 老板不会{无缘无故}请你吃饭，肯定有事要说。
ctx.en: The boss wouldn't take you to dinner for nothing; he must have something to tell you.

ctx.s: “你为什么打他？”“我可不是{无缘无故}动手的，是他先骂人的。”
ctx.en: "Why did you hit him?" "I didn't hit him for no reason; he insulted me first."

ctx.s: 扣工资总得有个理由，公司不能{无缘无故}就扣。
ctx.en: Docking pay needs a reason; the company can't just dock it for nothing.

ctx.s: 一个好好的孩子，怎么会{无缘无故}不肯上学呢？
ctx.en: How could a perfectly normal child suddenly refuse to go to school for no reason?

bad.s: 我{无缘无故}地在街上遇到了老同学。
bad.en: (meant: I happened to run into an old classmate on the street)
bad.why: It means an action had no cause, usually a puzzling or unfair one, not a lucky coincidence; say pèngqiǎo or ǒurán.

bad.s: 这道题{无缘无故}，我完全看不懂。
bad.en: (meant: this problem makes no sense to me)
bad.why: It describes an action or event that lacks a cause, not something confusing to read; call the problem baffling (mò míng qí miào).

cards.mean: only natural; as a matter of course
cards.lit: as reason says it ought to be

use.how: Predicate with 是…的, adverbial with 地, or in 把…看作理所当然 (to take for granted). Says something is right and to be expected by reason or duty.

cards.cue: Your flatmate expects you to clean up after him every day and never says thanks, as if it were simply your job. How does he see your help?

ctx.s: 借了别人的钱，按时还是{理所当然}的事。
ctx.en: If you borrow money, paying it back on time is only natural.

ctx.s: 他是队里跑得最快的，{理所当然}地被选去参加比赛。
ctx.en: He was the fastest runner on the team, so naturally he was picked for the race.

ctx.s: 很多孩子把父母的付出看作{理所当然}。
ctx.en: Many children take everything their parents do for them for granted.

ctx.s: “你帮了我这么多，真不知道怎么谢你。”“朋友之间互相帮忙，{理所当然}嘛。”
ctx.en: "You've helped me so much, I don't know how to thank you." "Friends help each other; it goes without saying."

ctx.s: 违约就要赔偿，这是{理所当然}的，没什么好争的。
ctx.en: If you break the contract you pay compensation; that's a matter of course, nothing to argue about.

ctx.s: 他是公司的创始人，大家{理所当然}地推选他当董事长。
ctx.en: He founded the company, so naturally everyone elected him chairman.

bad.s: 我今天又{理所当然}地忘了带钥匙。
bad.en: (meant: of course I forgot my keys again today)
bad.why: It says something is right and justified by reason or duty; it cannot carry the rueful English 'of course' about a slip. Say 'yòu wàng le' alone.

bad.s: 我们不应该{理所当然}父母的照顾。
bad.en: (meant: we shouldn't take our parents' care for granted)
bad.why: It is not a verb and takes no object; use the pattern bǎ … kànzuò lǐ suǒ dāng rán (to take … for granted).

cards.mean: unbelievable, beyond imagination
cards.lit: cannot be grasped by thought or put into words

story.text: The phrase began as a Buddhist term. In the sutras it described the wisdom and powers of the Buddhas as so profound that they could not be reached by thinking (sī) or by discussion (yì). In everyday Chinese it widened to mean anything so astonishing that it seems impossible.
story.source: 佛经用语，如《维摩诘经·不思议品》

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 真是不可思议 / 不可思议的事. Expresses amazement that something seems impossible, good or bad.

near.diff: 莫名其妙 is being baffled, often annoyed, by something that makes no sense; 不可思议 is amazement at something that seems impossible.

cards.cue: A tiny ant carries a leaf many times its own weight straight up a wall, and your friend stares, amazed it is even possible. What does she say?

ctx.s: 这么小的手机能拍出这么清楚的照片，真是{不可思议}！
ctx.en: A phone this small can take such sharp photos; it's incredible!

ctx.s: 一个十岁的孩子能背下整本字典？太{不可思议}了。
ctx.en: A ten-year-old who can recite a whole dictionary? That's unbelievable.

ctx.s: 他从十楼掉下来居然只受了点轻伤，医生都觉得{不可思议}。
ctx.en: He fell from the tenth floor and was only slightly hurt; even the doctors found it hard to believe.

ctx.s: “我在纽约街头碰到了小学同学。”“真的？太{不可思议}了！”
ctx.en: "I ran into a primary-school classmate on a street in New York." "Really? That's incredible!"

ctx.s: 宇宙中还有许多{不可思议}的现象等着科学家去解释。
ctx.en: The universe still holds many astonishing phenomena waiting for scientists to explain.

ctx.s: 回想起来，我们几个人开着一辆旧车穿过了沙漠，至今仍觉得{不可思议}。
ctx.en: Looking back, a few of us crossed the desert in an old car; I still find it hard to believe.

bad.s: 他说话{不可思议}，大家都听不懂。
bad.en: (meant: he talks so confusingly that nobody understands him)
bad.why: It expresses amazement at something that seems impossible, not that someone's speech is unclear or hard to follow.

bad.s: 这个问题你先{不可思议}一下，再回答我。
bad.en: (meant: think this question over first, then answer me)
bad.why: Sīyì here is part of a fixed adjective meaning inconceivable; it is not a verb for thinking something over. Say kǎolǜ yīxià.

cards.mean: as everyone knows
cards.lit: what the multitude all knows

use.how: Sentence-initial 众所周知，… or 是众所周知的 / 众所周知的事实. Introduces a fact the public or the audience already knows, in speeches, articles and reports.

cards.cue: Opening a talk, you want to remind the audience of a fact every one of them already knows before you build your argument on it. How do you begin?

ctx.s: {众所周知}，吸烟对身体有害。
ctx.en: As everyone knows, smoking is bad for your health.

ctx.s: 长城是中国的象征，这是{众所周知}的。
ctx.en: It is common knowledge that the Great Wall is a symbol of China.

ctx.s: {众所周知}，这家公司的产品以质量好而闻名。
ctx.en: As is well known, this company's products are famous for their quality.

ctx.s: 在发布会上，经理说：“{众所周知}，今年的市场竞争非常激烈。”
ctx.en: At the press conference the manager said, "As we all know, competition in the market is very fierce this year."

ctx.s: 他常常迟到，这在公司里是{众所周知}的事。
ctx.en: His lateness is common knowledge in the company.

ctx.s: 并非所有{众所周知}的说法都经得起科学的检验。
ctx.en: Not every well-known claim stands up to scientific testing.

bad.s: {众所周知}，我昨天晚上吃了饺子。
bad.en: (meant: well, last night I had dumplings)
bad.why: It introduces a fact the public widely knows; using it for a private detail nobody could know sounds absurd.

bad.s: 他{众所周知}了这件事。
bad.en: (meant: everyone came to know about it)
bad.why: It is not a verb with a person as subject; it describes the fact itself as known to all, so the matter must be the subject.

cards.mean: clear at a glance
cards.lit: one look and everything is clear

use.how: Predicate: 图表一目了然 / 让人一目了然. Said of how something is presented or shown: a chart, sign, layout or result that needs only one look.

near.diff: 一目了然 is about something being easy to see at one look; 一清二楚 is about knowing, remembering or explaining every detail.

cards.cue: The new dashboard puts every key figure on one screen, so anyone grasps the situation the moment they look at it. How is it laid out?

ctx.s: 这张地图画得很好，路线{一目了然}。
ctx.en: This map is well drawn; the route is clear at a glance.

ctx.s: 把数据做成图表，变化趋势就{一目了然}了。
ctx.en: Put the data in a chart and the trend is obvious at a glance.

ctx.s: 新菜单把价格和配料都列了出来，让顾客{一目了然}。
ctx.en: The new menu lists the prices and ingredients so customers can see everything at a glance.

ctx.s: “这个网站好用吗？”“好用，所有功能都在首页，{一目了然}。”
ctx.en: "Is the website easy to use?" "Yes, all the features are on the home page; you see them at a glance."

ctx.s: 车站的指示牌设计得{一目了然}，第一次来的人也不会走错。
ctx.en: The station signs are so clear that even first-time visitors don't go the wrong way.

ctx.s: 报告用红绿两色标出了各部门的业绩，好坏{一目了然}。
ctx.en: The report marks each department's results in red or green, so good and bad are clear at a glance.

bad.s: 那件事过去十年了，他还记得{一目了然}。
bad.en: (meant: ten years on, he still remembers it in every detail)
bad.why: It describes something visible at one look, not a person's detailed memory or knowledge; say yī qīng èr chǔ.

bad.s: 我看了他一眼，就{一目了然}地爱上了他。
bad.en: (meant: I fell in love with him at first sight)
bad.why: It means something is clear at a glance, not at first sight; love at first sight is yī jiàn zhōng qíng.

cards.mean: knowing or seeing every detail clearly
cards.lit: clear once and clear twice

use.how: Complement after 得 (记得、看得、说得、查得一清二楚) or predicate: 我心里一清二楚. About how fully someone knows, remembers or explains a matter.

near.diff: 一目了然 is about something being easy to see at one look; 一清二楚 is about knowing or explaining a matter in full detail.

cards.cue: The detective can tell you exactly where the suspect was at every minute that night, down to the smallest detail. How well does the detective know it?

ctx.s: 那天发生的事，我到现在还记得{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: I still remember every detail of what happened that day.

ctx.s: 老师把考试要求讲得{一清二楚}，没人再问问题。
ctx.en: The teacher explained the exam requirements so clearly that nobody had any more questions.

ctx.s: 你别想骗我，你昨晚去哪儿了我{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: Don't try to fool me; I know exactly where you went last night.

ctx.s: 警察很快就把事情的经过调查得{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: The police soon found out exactly how it had all happened.

ctx.s: “合同上的条款你都看明白了吗？”“放心，每一条我都看得{一清二楚}。”
ctx.en: "Did you understand all the terms in the contract?" "Don't worry, I understood every one of them perfectly."

ctx.s: 他在这条街上住了三十年，哪家店卖什么，他心里{一清二楚}。
ctx.en: He has lived on this street for thirty years and knows exactly which shop sells what.

bad.s: 今天天空{一清二楚}，一点云都没有。
bad.en: (meant: the sky is clear today, without a cloud)
bad.why: It is about knowing or explaining a matter in detail, not about clear weather; a cloudless sky is qínglǎng.

bad.s: 他是个{一清二楚}的人，从来不撒谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is an honest, upright person who never lies)
bad.why: It describes how clearly something is known, not a person's honesty; say chéngshí (honest).

cards.mean: to suddenly see the light
cards.lit: in a flash, a great awakening of understanding

use.how: Predicate without an object, often 才恍然大悟 or 恍然大悟地说; usually followed by 原来…. Said when something that puzzled you suddenly makes sense.

near.diff: 大开眼界 is seeing new things that broaden your experience; 恍然大悟 is suddenly understanding something that had puzzled you.

cards.cue: For weeks you couldn't work out why your plants kept dying; then you notice the window faces north, and in that instant it all makes sense. What happens?

ctx.s: 听他这么一说，我{恍然大悟}，原来是我记错了时间。
ctx.en: When he said that, it suddenly dawned on me: I had got the time wrong.

ctx.s: 看到桌上的蛋糕，他{恍然大悟}：原来今天是自己的生日。
ctx.en: Seeing the cake on the table, he suddenly realised that today was his own birthday.

ctx.s: 这道题我想了一个晚上，第二天刷牙时才{恍然大悟}。
ctx.en: I puzzled over this problem all evening, and it only clicked the next morning while I was brushing my teeth.

ctx.s: 直到读到最后一页，读者才{恍然大悟}，凶手就是那个管家。
ctx.en: Only on the last page does the reader suddenly realise the butler was the murderer.

ctx.s: 她{恍然大悟}地拍了拍脑袋：“难怪钥匙找不到，我放在车里了！”
ctx.en: She slapped her forehead as it dawned on her: "No wonder I couldn't find my keys, I left them in the car!"

ctx.s: 很多年后，他才{恍然大悟}，父亲当年的严厉其实是一种爱。
ctx.en: Only many years later did he realise that his father's strictness had been a kind of love.

bad.s: 我今天在课上{恍然大悟}了很多新单词。
bad.en: (meant: I learned a lot of new words in class today)
bad.why: It is a sudden insight into something that puzzled you, not learning new material, and it takes no object.

bad.s: 他早上七点{恍然大悟}，起床去上班。
bad.en: (meant: he woke up at seven and got up for work)
bad.why: Wù is waking up to the truth in the mind, not waking from sleep; say xǐnglái.

cards.mean: an eye-opening experience
cards.lit: to greatly widen the field of one's eyes

use.how: Predicate, often 让人大开眼界 or 真是大开眼界. Said after seeing or experiencing something new and impressive that widens one's horizons.

near.diff: 恍然大悟 is suddenly understanding something that puzzled you; 大开眼界 is seeing new things you had never seen before.

cards.cue: On your first visit to a huge robot factory, you see machines doing things you had never imagined. How does the visit leave you?

ctx.s: 这次去博物馆参观，孩子们都{大开眼界}。
ctx.en: The museum visit was a real eye-opener for the children.

ctx.s: 这场科技展览让我{大开眼界}，原来机器人已经会做饭了。
ctx.en: The technology fair opened my eyes; robots can already cook!

ctx.s: 在国外交流的一年让她{大开眼界}，也更了解自己的国家了。
ctx.en: Her exchange year abroad broadened her horizons and also helped her understand her own country better.

ctx.s: “昨天的魔术表演怎么样？”“太精彩了，真让人{大开眼界}！”
ctx.en: "How was the magic show yesterday?" "Amazing, a real eye-opener!"

ctx.s: 跟着老渔民出海一天，城里来的学生们{大开眼界}。
ctx.en: After a day at sea with an old fisherman, the students from the city had seen a whole new world.

ctx.s: 这本书介绍了深海里各种奇特的生物，读来令人{大开眼界}。
ctx.en: This book describes all kinds of strange deep-sea creatures; it is an eye-opening read.

bad.s: 他终于{大开眼界}，明白了自己错在哪里。
bad.en: (meant: he finally realised where he had gone wrong)
bad.why: It means seeing new things that widen one's experience, not suddenly understanding a mistake; say huǎng rán dà wù.

bad.s: 早上醒来，我{大开眼界}，看了看手机。
bad.en: (meant: I woke up, opened my eyes and checked my phone)
bad.why: It is never about physically opening one's eyes; say zhēngkāi yǎnjing.

cards.mean: in short; all in all
cards.lit: gathering it all together and saying it

use.how: Sentence-initial connector after several points have been made: 总而言之，… Sums up what was said, in speech or writing.

cards.cue: After listing the pros and cons of three phones at length, you are about to give your final verdict in one sentence. What phrase introduces it?

ctx.s: 这家店菜好吃，价格也便宜，{总而言之}，值得一去。
ctx.en: The food here is good and the prices are low; all in all, it's worth a visit.

ctx.s: 我们讨论了一下午，{总而言之}，方案下周一前必须交。
ctx.en: We've discussed it all afternoon; in short, the plan has to be handed in by Monday.

ctx.s: “这房子离公司远，房租又贵，{总而言之}，我不想租。”
ctx.en: "This flat is far from work and the rent is high; in a word, I don't want it."

ctx.s: {总而言之}，只要大家齐心协力，就没有解决不了的问题。
ctx.en: In conclusion, as long as we all pull together, there is no problem we can't solve.

ctx.s: 有人说早起好，有人说睡够了更好，{总而言之}，适合自己最重要。
ctx.en: Some say getting up early is best, others say enough sleep matters more; in the end, what suits you is what counts.

ctx.s: 文章最后写道：{总而言之}，保护环境需要每个人的参与。
ctx.en: The article ends: in short, protecting the environment needs everyone to take part.

bad.s: {总而言之}，大家好，今天我来介绍一下我们的新产品。
bad.en: (meant: to begin, hello everyone, today I'll present our new product)
bad.why: It sums up what has already been said, so it cannot open a talk; start with shǒuxiān or just the greeting.

bad.s: 他在会上{总而言之}讲了三个小时。
bad.en: (meant: altogether he spoke for three hours at the meeting)
bad.why: It is a connector that sums up points already made, not an adverb meaning altogether or in total; say yígòng.

cards.mean: reluctant to part
cards.lit: clinging tenderly, unable to let go

use.how: Mostly an adverbial with 地 before a verb of leaving (依依不舍地告别), or a predicate. Said of people at a goodbye, or of leaving a place one loves.

near.diff: 恋恋不舍 stresses clinging attachment and can be said of things or pleasures; 依依不舍 is the tender sadness of a goodbye.
舍不得 is everyday speech and also means unwilling to spend or give something up; 依依不舍 is only about parting.

cards.cue: At the airport a grandmother keeps hugging her grandson, walks him to the gate, and waves long after he has gone through. How does she see him off?

ctx.s: 毕业那天，同学们{依依不舍}地互相告别。
ctx.en: On graduation day the classmates said goodbye to one another, none of them wanting to leave.

ctx.s: 奶奶站在门口，{依依不舍}地看着我们的车开远。
ctx.en: Grandma stood at the door, watching our car drive away, sorry to see us go.

ctx.s: 假期结束了，孩子们{依依不舍}地离开了外婆家。
ctx.en: When the holiday ended, the children left their grandmother's house with heavy hearts.

ctx.s: “你怎么还不走？”——“跟你们在一起太开心了，真有点{依依不舍}。”
ctx.en: "Why haven't you left yet?" "I've had such a good time with you all, I really don't want to go."

ctx.s: 搬家前，他在住了十年的老房子里走了一圈又一圈，{依依不舍}。
ctx.en: Before moving, he walked round and round the old flat he had lived in for ten years, unwilling to leave it.

ctx.s: 站台上，两人{依依不舍}，直到火车开动才松开手。
ctx.en: On the platform the two of them couldn't bear to part, and only let go of each other's hands when the train began to move.

bad.s: 他对钱{依依不舍}，从来不肯请客。
bad.en: (meant: he hates spending money and never treats anyone)
bad.why: It is about the sadness of parting from people or places, not about being unwilling to spend money.

bad.s: 她{依依不舍}地把垃圾扔进了垃圾桶。
bad.en: (meant: she threw the rubbish into the bin)
bad.why: It expresses fond reluctance at a parting; nobody feels that about rubbish, so the sentence sounds absurd.

cards.mean: inseparable, always together
cards.lit: like a body and its shadow, never apart

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他们俩形影不离. Said of two people, or a person and a pet, who spend nearly all their time together, as a lasting habit.

near.diff: 如胶似漆 describes intense closeness, usually of lovers; 形影不离 just says they are always seen together, friends included.
寸步不离 is not leaving someone's side even a step, often to watch or guard them; 形影不离 is habitual companionship.

cards.cue: Wherever you see Lily, her best friend Mia is right beside her: at lunch, in class, at the weekend, on holiday.

ctx.s: 她们俩从小学起就{形影不离}。
ctx.en: Those two have been inseparable since primary school.

ctx.s: 这只小狗跟主人{形影不离}，主人去哪儿它就去哪儿。
ctx.en: The puppy never leaves its owner; wherever the owner goes, it goes too.

ctx.s: 那对双胞胎上学、吃饭、写作业都在一起，真是{形影不离}。
ctx.en: The twins go to school, eat and do their homework together; they really are never apart.

ctx.s: 你们俩以前不是{形影不离}吗？怎么最近不说话了？
ctx.en: Weren't you two always together? Why aren't you speaking lately?

ctx.s: 刚结婚那几年，他们夫妻{形影不离}，连买菜都一起去。
ctx.en: In the first years of their marriage the couple did everything together, even the grocery shopping.

ctx.s: 大学四年，他和室友{形影不离}，毕业后却去了不同的城市。
ctx.en: For four years at university he and his roommate were inseparable, but after graduating they moved to different cities.

bad.s: 我们昨天开会时{形影不离}地坐了两个小时。
bad.en: (meant: we sat side by side for two hours at yesterday's meeting)
bad.why: It describes a lasting habit of always being together, not sitting next to someone on one occasion.

bad.s: 他每天都{形影不离}他的女朋友。
bad.en: (meant: he is with his girlfriend all the time)
bad.why: It takes no object: the companion must come before it, joined with a word for 'and' or 'with', as in: he and his girlfriend are inseparable.

cards.mean: to share joys and hardships together
cards.lit: to taste the sweet together and bear the bitter together

story.text: After the state of Yan was crushed by its neighbour Qi, King Zhao of Yan set out to rebuild it. He invited able men to his court, mourned the dead and cared for the bereaved, and shared the sweet and the bitter with his people for twenty-eight years, until Yan was rich and strong again.

use.how: Predicate, often with 和/跟……: 我们同甘共苦了二十年. Said with warmth of spouses, friends or teams who stood together through good and bad times.

near.diff: 患难与共 is standing together in danger or disaster; 同甘共苦 covers both the good times and the hard ones.

cards.cue: An old couple ran a tiny noodle shop through years of poverty and later success, always side by side. How would you describe their marriage?

ctx.s: 他们夫妻{同甘共苦}，一起走过了三十年。
ctx.en: The couple have been through thick and thin together for thirty years.

ctx.s: 真正的朋友是能{同甘共苦}的人，不只是一起吃喝玩乐。
ctx.en: A true friend is someone who stands by you in good times and bad, not just someone to have fun with.

ctx.s: 创业那几年最苦，我们几个人{同甘共苦}，谁也没有离开。
ctx.en: The first years of the startup were the hardest; the few of us shared everything, good and bad, and nobody left.

ctx.s: 你愿意和我{同甘共苦}吗？我现在什么都没有。
ctx.en: Will you stand by me through good and bad? Right now I have nothing.

ctx.s: 老板在年会上说：“困难的时候大家跟我{同甘共苦}，现在赚钱了，人人有奖金。”
ctx.en: At the annual party the boss said: "You all stuck with me through the hard times; now that we're making money, everyone gets a bonus."

ctx.s: 当年{同甘共苦}的战友，如今头发都白了。
ctx.en: The comrades who once shared every hardship and joy now all have white hair.

bad.s: 我和新同事昨天{同甘共苦}地吃了一顿火锅。
bad.en: (meant: my new colleague and I shared a hotpot yesterday)
bad.why: It means sticking together through a long stretch of good and hard times, not sharing one meal.

bad.s: 他一个人{同甘共苦}，熬过了最难的日子。
bad.en: (meant: he got through the hardest days on his own)
bad.why: It needs people sharing with each other through good and bad; one person cannot do it alone.

cards.mean: childhood sweethearts
cards.lit: green plums and a bamboo horse: the toys of a little girl and boy playing together

story.text: In Li Bai's poem about Changgan, a young wife thinks of her husband far away. She remembers that when her hair was still cut short across her forehead, she was picking flowers by the gate, and he came riding a bamboo stick for a horse, circling round and playing with green plums. They grew up in the same lane, two small children with no suspicion of each other, and at fourteen she became his wife.

use.how: Usually 是青梅竹马 or attributive 青梅竹马的恋人. Said of a man and a woman who played together as small children, often a couple later on.

near.diff: 两小无猜 (from the same poem) stresses the innocent trust between the two children; 青梅竹马 names the childhood bond, often of a later couple.

cards.cue: Two neighbours played house together in kindergarten, lost touch at school, and married in their late twenties. What were they to each other?

ctx.s: 他和妻子是{青梅竹马}，从小在一个院子里长大。
ctx.en: He and his wife were childhood sweethearts; they grew up in the same courtyard.

ctx.s: 你知道吗？经理和他太太是{青梅竹马}，幼儿园就认识了。
ctx.en: Did you know? The manager and his wife were childhood sweethearts; they met in kindergarten.

ctx.s: 他们俩{青梅竹马}，分开二十多年后终于结了婚。
ctx.en: The two had been sweethearts as children, and after more than twenty years apart they finally married.

ctx.s: 电视剧里，女主角最后嫁给了和她{青梅竹马}的邻居哥哥。
ctx.en: In the TV series the heroine ends up marrying the boy next door she grew up with.

ctx.s: 回到老家，他又想起了那个{青梅竹马}的女孩。
ctx.en: Back in his home town, he thought again of the girl he had grown up with as a child.

ctx.s: 很多人羡慕{青梅竹马}的感情，觉得这样的两个人最了解彼此。
ctx.en: Many people envy a love that began in childhood, feeling that such a couple know each other best.

bad.s: 我和我太太是在公司认识的，我们是{青梅竹马}。
bad.en: (meant: my wife and I are a close couple who met at work)
bad.why: It is only for two people who knew each other as small children; meeting as adults at work rules it out.

bad.s: 我和我弟弟是{青梅竹马}。
bad.en: (meant: my brother and I grew up together)
bad.why: It is said of a boy and a girl from different families, usually with romance in view; siblings simply grew up together.

cards.mean: well matched in family background for marriage
cards.lit: the gates match and the households correspond

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 两家门当户对 / 门当户对的婚姻. Said of two families or a couple, about their social and economic standing in marriage.

near.diff: 郎才女貌 praises a talented man and a beautiful woman as a fine couple; 门当户对 is about the families' standing, not the couple's qualities.

cards.cue: A banker's daughter is marrying the son of a wealthy factory owner, and both sets of parents are pleased that the two families are on the same level.

ctx.s: 两家都是做生意的，算是{门当户对}。
ctx.en: Both families are in business, so they are a fair match.

ctx.s: 老一辈人找对象，最看重的就是{门当户对}。
ctx.en: When the older generation chose a spouse, what mattered most was that the families were of equal standing.

ctx.s: 她父母反对这门亲事，觉得两家不{门当户对}。
ctx.en: Her parents opposed the marriage, feeling the two families were not of the same standing.

ctx.s: “现在还讲究{门当户对}吗？”——“很多人嘴上不说，心里还是在意的。”
ctx.en: "Do people still care about matching family backgrounds?" "Many don't say so, but deep down they still do."

ctx.s: 他们俩出身差别很大，算不上{门当户对}，可结婚多年一直很幸福。
ctx.en: Their backgrounds were very different, hardly a matched pair of families, yet they have been happily married for years.

ctx.s: 有人认为{门当户对}的婚姻更稳定，因为双方的生活习惯相近。
ctx.en: Some believe marriages between families of similar standing are more stable, because the two sides live in similar ways.

bad.s: 他们俩都喜欢运动和看书，性格非常{门当户对}。
bad.en: (meant: they both like sport and reading and get on perfectly)
bad.why: It is about family background and social standing, not about shared personality or hobbies.

bad.s: 这件衬衫和这条裤子很{门当户对}。
bad.en: (meant: this shirt goes well with these trousers)
bad.why: It is about matching families in marriage, not about clothes or things that go well together.

cards.mean: to break off a relationship completely
cards.lit: one stroke of the knife and it falls in two

use.how: Usually 跟/和……一刀两断. Ending a relationship, a partnership or a habit decisively and for good; it sounds firm and often angry.

near.diff: 藕断丝连 is the opposite: still tied by threads after a break-up; 一刀两断 leaves no ties at all.

cards.cue: After finding out her business partner had lied to her for years, she dissolved the company, blocked his number and never spoke to him again.

ctx.s: 她决定跟前男友{一刀两断}，删掉了他所有的联系方式。
ctx.en: She decided to cut off her ex completely and deleted all his contact details.

ctx.s: 既然已经分手了，就{一刀两断}吧，别再联系了。
ctx.en: Since you've broken up, make a clean break and stop contacting each other.

ctx.s: “我要和你{一刀两断}！”她气得摔门就走。
ctx.en: "I'm finished with you for good!" she shouted, slamming the door as she left.

ctx.s: 他发现合伙人骗了他，当场就和对方{一刀两断}。
ctx.en: When he found out his partner had cheated him, he broke with him on the spot.

ctx.s: 他下决心跟香烟{一刀两断}，把家里的烟全扔了。
ctx.en: He resolved to be done with cigarettes for good and threw out every pack in the house.

ctx.s: 公司宣布与那家违规的供应商{一刀两断}，不再有任何合作。
ctx.en: The company announced a complete break with the supplier that broke the rules, ending all cooperation.

bad.s: 她昨天终于{一刀两断}了男朋友。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday she finally broke up with her boyfriend)
bad.why: It takes no object: the other party must come before it, joined with a word for 'with', as in: she broke with her boyfriend.

bad.s: 我们先{一刀两断}一个月，冷静一下再说。
bad.en: (meant: let's take a month apart to cool down)
bad.why: It means a complete and final break, so it cannot describe a temporary separation.

cards.mean: one-sided wishful thinking
cards.lit: the wish of one side only

use.how: Predicate (只是一厢情愿) or adverbial (一厢情愿地认为). Says a hope or plan ignores what the other side wants or what is realistic; also unreturned love.

near.diff: 心甘情愿 is being fully willing yourself; 一厢情愿 is assuming others, or reality, will go along with your wish.
自作多情 is imagining someone has feelings for you; 一厢情愿 is any one-sided hope or plan.

cards.cue: He has already planned the wedding in his head, but she has only spoken to him twice and already has a boyfriend.

ctx.s: 他喜欢她很多年，可惜只是{一厢情愿}。
ctx.en: He has loved her for years, but sadly it is all on his side.

ctx.s: 你以为老板会主动给你加薪？那只是你的{一厢情愿}。
ctx.en: You think the boss will give you a raise without being asked? That's just your wishful thinking.

ctx.s: 别{一厢情愿}了，对方根本没打算跟我们合作。
ctx.en: Stop kidding yourself; they never had any intention of working with us.

ctx.s: 父母{一厢情愿}地给孩子报了钢琴班，孩子却根本不喜欢。
ctx.en: The parents signed their child up for piano lessons assuming it would be welcome, but the child didn't like it at all.

ctx.s: 合作要双方都愿意，光我们这边积极，那只是{一厢情愿}。
ctx.en: A partnership needs both sides to want it; if only we are keen, it is just wishful thinking on our part.

ctx.s: 婚姻不是一个人{一厢情愿}就能维持的，需要两个人一起用心。
ctx.en: A marriage can't be held together by one person's wishes; it takes both people's effort.

bad.s: 他{一厢情愿}地帮我搬了家，一分钱都不要。
bad.en: (meant: he gladly helped me move house and wouldn't take a penny)
bad.why: It means a wish the other side does not share, never doing something gladly of one's own free will.

bad.s: 我们俩商量好了，{一厢情愿}地决定下个月结婚。
bad.en: (meant: we talked it over and both happily decided to marry next month)
bad.why: It means one-sided, so it cannot describe a decision both people agreed on.

cards.mean: to put oneself in another's shoes
cards.lit: to hold one's own heart up against another's

use.how: Often a clause on its own before the point (将心比心，你也不愿意这样), or after 要/学会. Urges empathy, or explains why one treats others kindly.

near.diff: 设身处地 is picturing yourself in another's situation to understand it; 将心比心 compares with how you would feel, usually to urge fairness.

cards.cue: Your friend snaps at a delivery driver who arrives late in the pouring rain. You ask him how he would feel if he were the one getting soaked.

ctx.s: 做事要{将心比心}，别只想着自己。
ctx.en: Treat people as you'd want to be treated; don't think only of yourself.

ctx.s: {将心比心}，如果你是他，你也会生气的。
ctx.en: Put yourself in his place: if you were him, you'd be angry too.

ctx.s: 老师说：“同学们，{将心比心}，谁愿意被别人取笑呢？”
ctx.en: The teacher said: "Class, think how you'd feel. Who wants to be laughed at?"

ctx.s: 我当过服务员，所以{将心比心}，从不对服务员发脾气。
ctx.en: I used to be a waiter, so I know how it feels and never lose my temper with waiting staff.

ctx.s: 半夜敲邻居的门借东西，你{将心比心}想想，这合适吗？
ctx.en: Knocking on the neighbour's door at midnight to borrow something: imagine it were you, is that reasonable?

ctx.s: 遇到顾客投诉，客服要学会{将心比心}，先理解对方的着急。
ctx.en: When customers complain, service staff need to put themselves in the customer's shoes and first understand their worry.

bad.s: 我和她{将心比心}，很快就结婚了。
bad.en: (meant: we loved each other and soon got married)
bad.why: It is about judging another's feelings by your own, not about two hearts in love.

bad.s: 我们俩{将心比心}，看看谁的成绩更好。
bad.en: (meant: let's compare and see whose marks are better)
bad.why: The comparing is of feelings, to understand someone; it never means competing or comparing results.

cards.mean: to suffer the results of one's own doing
cards.lit: what you yourself did, you yourself receive

use.how: Predicate, often 真是自作自受 or 是自作自受. A blunt verdict that someone's trouble is their own fault; can be said of oneself ruefully.

near.diff: 咎由自取 is more formal and severe, for serious blame or punishment; 自作自受 is everyday and blunt.

cards.cue: Your roommate cheated a classmate out of money, and now nobody in the dorm will speak to him. What do you mutter about his loneliness?

ctx.s: 他酒后开车，驾照被吊销了，这是{自作自受}。
ctx.en: He drove after drinking and lost his licence; he brought it on himself.

ctx.s: 谁让你在背后说别人坏话？现在大家都不理你，{自作自受}！
ctx.en: Who told you to badmouth people behind their backs? Now nobody will talk to you, and it's your own doing!

ctx.s: 我熬夜打游戏，结果考试时睡着了，真是{自作自受}。
ctx.en: I stayed up gaming and fell asleep in the exam; I brought it on myself.

ctx.s: “他被公司开除了。”——“他天天迟到早退，{自作自受}。”
ctx.en: "He got fired." "He came in late and left early every day. He asked for it."

ctx.s: 他总是骗人，现在没有人相信他了，这叫{自作自受}。
ctx.en: He was always lying, and now nobody believes him; that's what he gets.

ctx.s: 小说里那个贪心的商人最后破产了，读者都觉得他{自作自受}。
ctx.en: The greedy merchant in the novel goes bankrupt in the end, and readers all feel he got what he deserved.

bad.s: 他好好地走在人行道上，被一辆车撞了，真是{自作自受}。
bad.en: (meant: how awful, he was walking on the pavement and got hit by a car)
bad.why: It blames the person for their trouble; said of an innocent accident victim it sounds cruel.

bad.s: 她每天努力练琴，终于拿了冠军，这是{自作自受}。
bad.en: (meant: she practised every day and finally won, as she deserved)
bad.why: It is only for bad consequences of one's own folly, never for hard work paying off.

cards.mean: selfish, thinking only of oneself
cards.lit: private for oneself, profit for oneself

use.how: An adjective, as predicate or attributive: 他很自私自利 / 自私自利的人. A strong moral criticism of someone who always puts their own interest first.

near.diff: 损人利己 is actively harming others to benefit oneself; 自私自利 is caring only about oneself, whether or not others are harmed.

cards.cue: Your housemate takes the biggest room, uses everyone's food and never cleans, but won't lift a finger when anyone else needs help.

ctx.s: 他从来不帮别人，太{自私自利}了。
ctx.en: He never helps anyone; he's far too selfish.

ctx.s: 我不喜欢跟{自私自利}的人做朋友。
ctx.en: I don't like being friends with selfish people.

ctx.s: 你只想着自己方便，怎么这么{自私自利}？
ctx.en: You only think about what's convenient for you. How can you be so selfish?

ctx.s: 地铁上他一个人占三个座位，这种{自私自利}的行为让人很反感。
ctx.en: He took up three seats on the metro by himself; that kind of selfish behaviour is really off-putting.

ctx.s: 小组作业他只做自己那部分，别人有困难也不管，大家都说他{自私自利}。
ctx.en: In group projects he only does his own part and ignores anyone who's struggling, so everyone says he's selfish.

ctx.s: 父母为孩子付出一切，孩子却只知道索取，变得越来越{自私自利}。
ctx.en: The parents gave the child everything, yet the child only ever takes and grows more and more selfish.

bad.s: 医生说你太累了，应该{自私自利}一点，多照顾自己。
bad.en: (meant: the doctor says you're exhausted and should put yourself first a bit)
bad.why: It is a harsh moral criticism, never kind advice to look after yourself.

bad.s: 他{自私自利}地把最后一块蛋糕让给了妹妹。
bad.en: (meant: he gave the last piece of cake to his sister)
bad.why: Giving the last piece away is the opposite of selfish, so the idiom contradicts the action.

cards.mean: to find joy in helping others
cards.lit: to take helping people as one's pleasure

use.how: Describes a person's character, as a predicate or before 的: 他一向助人为乐；助人为乐的精神。 It takes no object. Said of everyday, willing helpfulness.

near.diff: 见义勇为 is bravely stepping in when someone is in danger; 助人为乐 is ordinary, cheerful helpfulness with no risk involved.

cards.cue: A retired neighbour spends every weekend fixing other people's bikes for free and says it makes her day. How do you describe her?

ctx.s: 我的邻居王阿姨一向{助人为乐}，谁家有事她都去帮忙。
ctx.en: My neighbour Auntie Wang has always loved helping; whenever a family has a problem, she goes over to help.

ctx.s: 学校表扬了几位{助人为乐}的同学。
ctx.en: The school commended several students who are always glad to help others.

ctx.s: 他退休后在社区免费教孩子下棋，说{助人为乐}比什么都开心。
ctx.en: After retiring he teaches the neighbourhood kids chess for free, and says nothing makes him happier than helping.

ctx.s: 我们应该从小培养孩子{助人为乐}的品质。
ctx.en: We should nurture a love of helping others in children from an early age.

ctx.s: 这位出租车司机常常免费送老人去医院，真是{助人为乐}的好榜样。
ctx.en: This taxi driver often takes elderly people to hospital for free; he's a real example of kindness to others.

ctx.s: 网上那篇文章讲了一个快递员{助人为乐}的故事，感动了很多人。
ctx.en: That article online told the story of a courier who loves helping people, and it moved a lot of readers.

bad.s: 谢谢你昨天{助人为乐}我搬家。
bad.en: (meant: thanks for helping me move yesterday)
bad.why: It describes a person's character and takes no object. Just thank them for helping, using the plain verb bang.

bad.s: 他冲进大火救出了小孩，真是{助人为乐}。
bad.en: (meant: he rushed into the fire and saved a child; how heroic)
bad.why: Risking your own safety to save someone in danger calls for jian yi yong wei; this idiom is for everyday kindness.

cards.mean: give an inch and they take a mile
cards.lit: having gained an inch, to push on for a foot

story.text: Dictionaries trace the phrase to the strategist Fan Ju, who advised King Zhaoxiang of Qin to befriend distant states and attack nearby ones, because then every inch of land taken would be the king's inch and every foot the king's foot. There it praised steady, secure gains; the idiom later came to mean never being satisfied with what one has been given.

use.how: Predicate, often in warnings: 别得寸进尺！ Said of someone who, after a concession, keeps demanding more. It takes no object.

near.diff: 贪得无厌 is insatiable greed in general; 得寸进尺 is pushing for more right after someone has given way.

cards.cue: You let your flatmate borrow your bike for an afternoon; now they've kept it a week and are asking for your car as well. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 我借给他一百块，他又要借两百，真是{得寸进尺}。
ctx.en: I lent him a hundred yuan and now he wants to borrow two hundred more. Give him an inch and he takes a mile.

ctx.s: 你已经晚交了三天，现在还想再拖一周？别{得寸进尺}了！
ctx.en: You're already three days late and now you want another week? Don't push your luck!

ctx.s: 孩子：“再玩十分钟好不好？”妈妈：“刚才已经多给你十分钟了，不许{得寸进尺}。”
ctx.en: Child: "Can I play ten more minutes?" Mum: "I already gave you ten extra minutes. Don't push it."

ctx.s: 对方一开始只要求降价一点，我们答应后，他们却{得寸进尺}，要求免费送货。
ctx.en: At first they only asked for a small discount; once we agreed, they pushed for more and demanded free delivery too.

ctx.s: 如果你一直让着他，他只会{得寸进尺}。
ctx.en: If you keep giving in to him, he'll just keep asking for more.

ctx.s: 邻居先是把车停在我家门口，后来{得寸进尺}，干脆把杂物也堆了过来。
ctx.en: First the neighbour parked in front of my house; then, emboldened, he started piling his junk there too.

bad.s: 她学习很努力，成绩{得寸进尺}，越来越好。
bad.en: (meant: she studies hard and her grades keep improving step by step)
bad.why: It does not mean steady progress; it criticises someone who keeps demanding more after a concession.

bad.s: 他总是{得寸进尺}别人。
bad.en: (meant: he always takes advantage of other people)
bad.why: It takes no object. Say simply that he is always pushing for more (ta zongshi de cun jin chi), and name the people in a separate clause.

cards.mean: to stand by and do nothing to help
cards.lit: to tuck one's hands into one's sleeves and watch from the side

story.text: In his funeral address for his friend Liu Zongyuan, Han Yu wrote that when a clumsy man does the carving, his fingers bleed and his face runs with sweat, while the skilled craftsman stands by with his hands drawn into his sleeves. He was lamenting that a man of Liu's talent had been left on the sidelines. The image became the idiom for watching without lending a hand.

use.how: Predicate, very often negated: 我不能袖手旁观。 Said of someone who could help with a problem but chooses not to.

near.diff: 见死不救 is far stronger: leaving someone in mortal danger; 袖手旁观 is any failure to pitch in when help is needed.

cards.cue: Your teammates are racing to fix a bug before the deadline, and one colleague just leans back and watches without lifting a finger. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 朋友有困难，我怎么能{袖手旁观}呢？
ctx.en: My friend is in trouble; how could I just stand by and watch?

ctx.s: 弟弟在搬家，哥哥却坐在沙发上{袖手旁观}，一点忙都不帮。
ctx.en: The younger brother was moving house, and his older brother just sat on the sofa watching, not helping at all.

ctx.s: 公司出了问题，你作为经理却{袖手旁观}，这说不过去吧？
ctx.en: The company is in trouble and you, the manager, are just watching from the sidelines. That's hard to justify, isn't it?

ctx.s: 村里修路，每家都出了力，没有一个人{袖手旁观}。
ctx.en: When the village built the road, every family pitched in; not one person stood aside.

ctx.s: 看到有人在地铁里欺负老人，乘客们没有{袖手旁观}，纷纷上前制止。
ctx.en: When someone started harassing an old man on the subway, the passengers didn't just look on; they stepped in one after another to stop it.

ctx.s: 他说：“这件事我不能{袖手旁观}，明天我去找校长谈谈。”
ctx.en: He said, "I can't just stay out of this. Tomorrow I'll go and talk to the head teacher."

bad.s: 我昨天在公园{袖手旁观}了一场足球比赛，很精彩。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday I watched a football match in the park; it was great)
bad.why: It is not neutral watching; it blames someone for not helping when help is needed.

bad.s: 谢谢你在我最困难的时候{袖手旁观}。
bad.en: (meant: thank you for standing by me in my hardest time)
bad.why: It criticises refusing to help, the opposite of standing by someone. Thank them for their support instead.

cards.mean: to abandon those who helped once they are no longer needed
cards.lit: to tear down the bridge once one has crossed the river

use.how: Predicate or before 的: 他过河拆桥；过河拆桥的人。 It takes no object. Said of someone who drops or turns on the people who helped them succeed.

near.diff: 忘恩负义 is ingratitude in general; 过河拆桥 is discarding helpers precisely once they have served their purpose.

cards.cue: As soon as the start-up turns a profit, its founder cuts out the early investor who kept it alive in the lean years. What did the founder do?

ctx.s: 他升职以后就不理当初帮过他的同事了，真是{过河拆桥}。
ctx.en: After his promotion he ignored the colleagues who had helped him. Talk about kicking away the ladder.

ctx.s: 我帮你找到了工作，你现在却说我坏话，这不是{过河拆桥}吗？
ctx.en: I helped you find this job and now you're badmouthing me. Isn't that just using me and throwing me away?

ctx.s: 做人不能{过河拆桥}，别人帮过你，你要记在心里。
ctx.en: You mustn't turn your back on people once they've helped you; remember who helped you.

ctx.s: 项目一成功，公司就把出力最多的合作方换掉了，大家都说他们{过河拆桥}。
ctx.en: As soon as the project succeeded, the company replaced the partner who had done the most. Everyone said they'd ditched them once they were no longer needed.

ctx.s: “放心吧，我不是那种{过河拆桥}的人。”
ctx.en: "Don't worry, I'm not the kind of person who forgets you once I've got what I need."

ctx.s: 小说里的那个商人发财后{过河拆桥}，最后再也没人愿意跟他合作。
ctx.en: The merchant in the novel turned on those who had helped him once he got rich, and in the end nobody would work with him.

bad.s: 为了考上大学，他{过河拆桥}，辞掉工作专心复习。
bad.en: (meant: he burned his boats, quitting his job to focus on the exam)
bad.why: Cutting off your own retreat is po fu chen zhou; this idiom is ingratitude towards the people who helped you.
