ctx.en: Don't celebrate too soon; the data hasn't been checked, and we're still far from finished.

ctx.s: 经过三年施工，这座跨江大桥的建设终于{大功告成}。
ctx.en: After three years of work, construction of the bridge across the river is finally complete.

bad.s: 他很有才华，年纪轻轻就{大功告成}，当上了总经理。
bad.en: (meant: he is talented and became general manager while still young)
bad.why: It marks the finishing of a particular task or project, not a person's success in life or career.

bad.s: 这个项目我们才开始，已经{大功告成}了一半。
bad.en: (meant: we have only just started and are already half done)
bad.why: It means the whole job is finished; it cannot be divided into fractions to describe partial progress.

cards.mean: to rank among the top
cards.lit: one's name is placed among the front grass flags, the vanguard

story.text: In the army of the state of Chu in the Spring and Autumn period, the scouts marching at the very front carried mao, a kind of tall grass, as their signal flag, raising it to warn the troops behind of danger. So qian mao, the front grass, meant the vanguard, and the Zuo Zhuan uses it in describing how the Chu army marched. Much later the phrase came to mean having one's name near the head of a list.

use.how: Predicate, usually after 在…中 or a place: 在全班名列前茅. Said of people or things in a ranking: exams, contests, sales, league tables.

near.diff: 首屈一指 means the very best, number one; 名列前茅 means somewhere among the top few of a ranking.

cards.cue: Your cousin's exam results put her in the top three of her year group yet again. How do you describe where she stands?

ctx.s: 她学习很用功，每次考试都{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: She studies hard and is near the top in every exam.

ctx.s: 这款手机的销量在全国{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: This phone's sales are among the highest in the country.

ctx.s: 我们学校的篮球队在全市比赛中一直{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: Our school basketball team has always been one of the top teams in the city championships.

ctx.s: “你儿子成绩怎么样？”“还行，在班里算是{名列前茅}吧。”
ctx.en: "How are your son's grades?" "Not bad, he's more or less near the top of his class."

ctx.s: 这座城市的空气质量多年来在全省{名列前茅}。
ctx.en: For years this city's air quality has ranked among the best in the province.

ctx.s: 他刚转来时成绩倒数，一年后竟然{名列前茅}，老师都很惊讶。
ctx.en: When he transferred here he was near the bottom, yet a year later he was among the top, which amazed his teachers.

bad.s: 排队买票的时候，我{名列前茅}，很快就买到了。
bad.en: (meant: I was near the front of the queue, so I got a ticket quickly)
bad.why: It is about rank in results or standings, not about physical position in a line of people.

bad.s: 这次比赛他得了第一名，比第二名{名列前茅}很多。
bad.en: (meant: he won, far ahead of the runner-up)
bad.why: It states that someone is among the top; it cannot take a bǐ ... hěn duō comparison to say how far ahead they are.

cards.mean: to ruin something by adding what is not needed
cards.lit: to draw a snake and add feet

story.text: Servants in the state of Chu were given one jug of wine, too little to share, so they agreed that whoever drew a snake on the ground first would drink it. One man finished early and, showing off, started adding feet. Another finished his snake, took the jug and said: a snake has no feet, so yours is not a snake. The man who added the feet lost the wine.

use.how: Predicate or after 是, 就是, 反而: 再加一句就是画蛇添足。 Criticises an addition, done or proposed, that makes a finished thing worse.

near.diff: 多此一举 is any unnecessary extra step; 画蛇添足 says the extra addition actually spoils what was already good.
弄巧成拙 is any clever trick that backfires; 画蛇添足 is specifically adding something superfluous to a thing already complete.

cards.cue: Your summary was clear and complete, but then you tacked on a long extra paragraph that only confused the readers. What did you do?

ctx.s: 这道菜已经很好吃了，再放糖就是{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: This dish is already delicious; adding sugar would only spoil it.

ctx.s: 照片拍得很自然，加那么多滤镜反而{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The photo looks natural; piling on filters just ruins it.

ctx.s: “结尾再加一句总结怎么样？”“别，现在的结尾余味正好，再加就{画蛇添足}了。”
ctx.en: "How about adding a summary line at the end?" "Don't, the ending lingers just right as it is; adding more would spoil it."

ctx.s: 这幅山水画的留白恰到好处，他偏要在空白处题一首长诗，实在是{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The empty space in this landscape painting was just right, yet he insisted on writing a long poem across it; that really spoiled it.

ctx.s: 老街的木门本来很有味道，刷上亮漆以后，很多人觉得是{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The old street's wooden doors had real character; once they were coated in glossy paint, many people felt it had spoiled them.

ctx.s: 这部电影的结局本来很好，导演却又加了一段，有点{画蛇添足}。
ctx.en: The film's ending was good as it was, but the director tacked on an extra scene, which rather spoiled it.

bad.s: 她又帮我改正了几处错误，真是{画蛇添足}，太谢谢她了！
bad.en: (meant: she kindly corrected a few more mistakes for me, I'm so grateful)
bad.why: It criticises an addition that spoils something; it cannot be used to thank someone for useful extra work.

bad.s: 他做事总是很马虎，经常{画蛇添足}。
bad.en: (meant: he is careless and often leaves things out)
bad.why: It is about adding too much to something finished, not about carelessness or leaving things out.

cards.mean: to wait idly for luck to strike again
cards.lit: to keep watch by a tree stump, waiting for a hare

story.text: A farmer of the state of Song had a tree stump in his field. One day a running hare crashed into the stump, broke its neck and died. The farmer put down his plough and sat by the stump, hoping to get another hare. No hare ever came, and he became the laughing stock of Song. Han Feizi tells it to mock rulers who govern the present with the methods of the ancient kings.

use.how: Predicate, often with 不能, 别, or after 是: 只等客人上门是守株待兔。 Mocks waiting passively for a lucky chance, often one that happened once, instead of acting.

near.diff: 坐享其成 is enjoying the results of other people's work; 守株待兔 is waiting idly for a stroke of luck that may never come.

cards.cue: A shop once got a big order from a stranger who wandered in; now the owner does no marketing at all and just sits waiting for another one. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 找工作不能{守株待兔}，要主动投简历。
ctx.en: You can't just sit and wait for a job to come to you; you have to send out your CV.

ctx.s: 开店只等客人上门是{守株待兔}，得想办法做宣传。
ctx.en: Running a shop and just waiting for customers to show up is waiting for luck; you have to find ways to advertise.

ctx.s: “这个客户上次是自己找来的，我们再等等吧。”“别{守株待兔}了，主动去联系。”
ctx.en: "This client found us on their own last time, let's just wait." "Stop waiting for lightning to strike twice, go and contact them."

ctx.s: 他中过一次小奖，就天天买彩票，等着再来一次，简直是{守株待兔}。
ctx.en: He won a small prize once, so now he buys lottery tickets every day waiting for it to happen again; it's pure wishful waiting.

ctx.s: 机会不会从天上掉下来，{守株待兔}的人只会越等越失望。
ctx.en: Opportunities don't fall from the sky; people who sit waiting for luck only grow more disappointed.

ctx.s: 去年有人在这条河边捡到过玉石，今年就有人天天来河边{守株待兔}。
ctx.en: Last year someone found a piece of jade by this river, and now people come every day to sit by the bank waiting for the same luck.

bad.s: 他每天早起锻炼，坚持了三年，真是{守株待兔}。
bad.en: (meant: he has kept up his morning exercise for three years, how persistent)
bad.why: It mocks idle waiting for luck; it cannot praise steady effort and perseverance.

bad.s: 我在门口{守株待兔}等朋友，他十分钟后就来了。
bad.en: (meant: I waited at the door for my friend, and he arrived ten minutes later)
bad.why: Waiting for someone who is on the way is ordinary waiting; the idiom is for hoping a lucky windfall will come while doing nothing.

cards.mean: to talk to someone who can't appreciate it
cards.lit: to play the zither to an ox

story.text: Gongming Yi, a musician of old, once played a refined melody on his zither to an ox. The ox went on grazing with its head down. It was not that the ox could not hear, but that the music did not suit its ears. Then he played sounds like the buzzing of mosquitoes and the lowing of a lost calf, and the ox flicked its tail, pricked up its ears and paced about, listening.

use.how: Predicate or after 是, 像: 跟他讲道理简直是对牛弹琴。 Mocks a listener who cannot understand or appreciate, or a speaker who ignores the audience. Rude if aimed at someone's face.

cards.cue: You spent an hour explaining the beauty of a poem to a friend who only cares about football, and he just yawned the whole time. What were you doing?

ctx.s: 跟他讲古典音乐，简直是{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: Talking to him about classical music is a complete waste of breath.

ctx.s: 我跟室友讲了半天这部电影的镜头有多美，他只关心打斗场面，真是{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: I spent ages telling my roommate how beautiful the film's camerawork was, but he only cares about the fight scenes; it was completely lost on him.

ctx.s: “你又跟他讲道理了？”“别提了，{对牛弹琴}。”
ctx.en: "Did you try reasoning with him again?" "Don't ask, it went straight over his head."

ctx.s: 给小学生讲这么深的理论，不是{对牛弹琴}吗？
ctx.en: Isn't lecturing primary school kids on such advanced theory just talking over their heads?

ctx.s: 我说的话他一句也听不进去，再说下去也是{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: He doesn't take in a single word I say; going on would be pointless.

ctx.s: 讲课要看对象，不了解听众就开讲，难免{对牛弹琴}。
ctx.en: A lecture has to suit its audience; if you start without knowing your listeners, you are bound to be talking over their heads.

bad.s: 他钢琴弹得很好，在音乐会上{对牛弹琴}。
bad.en: (meant: he plays the piano well and performed at the concert)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with playing well; it means talking to people who cannot appreciate it, so here it insults the concert audience.

bad.s: 王教授，谢谢您今天给我们{对牛弹琴}，我们学到了很多。
bad.en: (meant: thank you, Professor Wang, for teaching us today)
bad.why: It calls the listeners oxen; as a thank-you it insults both the audience and the speaker.

cards.mean: a person with a narrow view of the world
cards.lit: a frog at the bottom of a well

story.text: A frog living in a shallow, broken-down well boasted to a great turtle from the Eastern Sea about how happy it was there, and invited the turtle in. Before the turtle could get its left foot in, its right knee was stuck. The turtle backed away and told the frog about the sea: so vast that floods and droughts never change its level. Hearing this, the frog was startled and at a loss.

use.how: A noun phrase, after 是, 像 or 做: 别做井底之蛙。 Criticises someone, often oneself, whose outlook is narrow and who thinks their little world is all there is.

near.diff: 一知半解 is shallow knowledge of one subject; 井底之蛙 is a person whose whole view of the world is narrow without knowing it.

cards.cue: A man who has never left his hometown insists its little river is the greatest in the world and laughs at anyone who mentions the sea. What is he?

ctx.s: 多出去走走，别做{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: Get out and see the world; don't be a frog in a well.

ctx.s: 出国留学以后，我才发现自己以前就是个{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: It was only after going abroad to study that I realised how narrow my view of the world had been.

ctx.s: 他以为自己的公司是全国最好的，真是{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: He thinks his company is the best in the country; he really has no idea what's out there.

ctx.s: “我们镇上的菜最好吃！”“你呀，就是只{井底之蛙}，去大城市看看吧。”
ctx.en: "Our town has the best food anywhere!" "You're a frog in a well, you know; go and see a big city."

ctx.s: 只看一种新闻、只听一种声音，人很容易变成{井底之蛙}。
ctx.en: If you read only one kind of news and hear only one voice, you can easily end up with a very narrow view of the world.

ctx.s: 这家企业多年不关注行业变化，像{井底之蛙}一样，不知道国外的技术早就超过了自己。
ctx.en: For years the company ignored changes in its industry; like a frog in a well, it never knew that foreign technology had long since overtaken it.

bad.s: 他对这道数学题不太懂，是个{井底之蛙}。
bad.en: (meant: he doesn't really understand this maths problem)
bad.why: It describes a narrow outlook on the whole world, not failing to understand one particular thing; for that say bú tài dǒng.

bad.s: 他很{井底之蛙}，什么都不知道。
bad.en: (meant: he is very narrow-minded and knows nothing)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase and cannot take hěn like an adjective; put shì or xiàng before it instead.

cards.mean: to contradict oneself
cards.lit: one's own spear and shield clash

story.text: A man of the state of Chu was selling shields and spears. Praising his shields, he said they were so strong that nothing could pierce them. Praising his spears, he said they were so sharp that there was nothing they could not pierce. Someone asked: what happens if you use your spear to strike your shield? The man had no answer.

use.how: Predicate, often with 前后 or after 这不是…吗: 他的说法前后自相矛盾。 Said of one person's or one text's words or actions that cannot both be true.

near.diff: 口是心非 is saying one thing while meaning the opposite; 自相矛盾 is two things someone says or does that cannot both be true.

cards.cue: A witness first says he was at home all evening, then mentions seeing the accident happen on the street that night. What is wrong with his account?

ctx.s: 你刚说没去过，现在又说去过，这不是{自相矛盾}吗？
ctx.en: You just said you'd never been, and now you say you have; aren't you contradicting yourself?

ctx.s: 这份报告前后{自相矛盾}，数据根本对不上。
ctx.en: This report contradicts itself; the figures simply don't match up.

ctx.s: 他一边说要省钱，一边天天买奶茶，真是{自相矛盾}。
ctx.en: He says he wants to save money, yet he buys bubble tea every day; it makes no sense.

ctx.s: 嫌疑人的口供{自相矛盾}，警察认为他在撒谎。
ctx.en: The suspect's statement contradicted itself, and the police believed he was lying.

ctx.s: “主角前面说自己是独生子，后面又提到他哥哥。”“作者写得{自相矛盾}了。”
ctx.en: "Early on the hero says he's an only child, then later his brother turns up." "The author has contradicted himself."

ctx.s: 这项规定既要求准时下班，又要求当天工作必须做完，本身就{自相矛盾}。
ctx.en: The rule requires leaving on time but also finishing all of the day's work; it contradicts itself.

bad.s: 我和妹妹的意见{自相矛盾}，吵了一架。
bad.en: (meant: my sister and I disagreed and had a row)
bad.why: Zì xiāng means contradicting oneself; two people disagreeing is yìjiàn bù hé or yǒu máodùn.

bad.s: 他心里很{自相矛盾}，不知道该选哪份工作。
bad.en: (meant: he feels torn about which job to choose)
bad.why: Feeling torn is xīnli hěn máodùn or zuǒ yòu wéi nán; this idiom is about statements or actions that clash.

cards.mean: to fix the problem after a loss, before it worsens
cards.lit: to mend the pen after losing sheep

story.text: Zhuang Xin warned King Xiang of Chu that his life of pleasure would ruin the state, but the king would not listen and Zhuang Xin left. Soon Qin took the Chu capital and the king fled. He sent for Zhuang Xin and asked what could still be done. Zhuang Xin replied: to call the dog after seeing the hare is not too late; to mend the pen after losing sheep is not too late either.

use.how: Predicate or after 算是, 叫: 换了新锁，也算亡羊补牢。 Often with 为时未晚. Said approvingly of fixing the cause after a loss so it does not happen again.

near.diff: 后悔莫及 is regret that comes too late to help; 亡羊补牢 is acting after a loss to stop it happening again.

cards.cue: After their flat was burgled, a family finally fits strong locks and an alarm so it can't happen again. How might a neighbour describe this, approvingly?

ctx.s: 家里被偷了一次，他马上换了新锁，也算{亡羊补牢}。
ctx.en: After his home was burgled, he changed the locks straight away; better late than never.

ctx.s: 这次考试没考好不要紧，{亡羊补牢}，为时未晚。
ctx.en: Don't worry about doing badly this time; if you fix what went wrong now, it's not too late.

ctx.s: 电脑坏了丢了很多文件，从那以后他每周都备份，这叫{亡羊补牢}。
ctx.en: His computer broke and he lost a lot of files; since then he backs up every week, which is learning from the loss.

ctx.s: “公司已经被罚款了，现在加强管理还有用吗？”“{亡羊补牢}总比什么都不做强。”
ctx.en: "The company has already been fined; is tightening management any use now?" "Fixing it after the fact is better than doing nothing."

ctx.s: 事故发生后，学校连夜检查了所有教室的电线，及时{亡羊补牢}。
ctx.en: After the accident, the school checked the wiring in every classroom overnight, fixing the problem before anything worse could happen.

ctx.s: 有些问题等出了事再{亡羊补牢}，代价就太大了，不如提前预防。
ctx.en: With some problems, waiting until something goes wrong before fixing them costs far too much; better to prevent them in advance.

bad.s: 下周要下雨，我们今天先{亡羊补牢}，把屋顶修好。
bad.en: (meant: it will rain next week, so let's fix the roof today in advance)
bad.why: It needs a loss that has already happened; preparing before any damage is wèi yǔ chóu móu.

bad.s: 他错过了最后一班车，只能{亡羊补牢}，后悔得要命。
bad.en: (meant: he missed the last bus and could only regret it bitterly)
bad.why: It is about acting to prevent further loss, not regretting what cannot be undone; that is hòu huǐ mò jí.

cards.mean: to spoil things by forcing them to grow too fast
cards.lit: to pull up seedlings to help them grow

story.text: A man of the state of Song worried that his seedlings were growing too slowly, so he went into the field and pulled each one up a little. He came home worn out and told his family: I am exhausted today, I have been helping the seedlings grow. His son ran out to look, and the seedlings had all withered. Mencius tells the story to warn against forcing what must grow naturally.

use.how: Predicate or after 是, 无异于: 这是拔苗助长。 Criticises pushing a child, a person or an undertaking to develop faster than it can, so that it is harmed. Also written 揠苗助长.

near.diff: 急于求成 is being impatient for results in general; 拔苗助长 is actively forcing something to develop and so damaging it.

cards.cue: Parents make their small son study all evening, every evening, so he will get ahead, and soon he hates books. What have they done?

ctx.s: 孩子才三岁就学四门外语，这是{拔苗助长}。
ctx.en: Making a three-year-old learn four foreign languages is forcing him far too fast.

ctx.s: 学习要一步一步来，{拔苗助长}只会适得其反。
ctx.en: Learning has to go step by step; pushing too fast only backfires.

ctx.s: “我想让他跳两级，早点上大学。”“别{拔苗助长}，他还没准备好。”
ctx.en: "I want him to skip two years and get to university early." "Don't force it, he isn't ready."

ctx.s: 新员工才来一个月就让他当经理，不是{拔苗助长}吗？
ctx.en: Making a new hire a manager after just one month, isn't that pushing him before he's ready?

ctx.s: 有些家长给孩子报了太多补习班，结果{拔苗助长}，孩子反而讨厌学习了。
ctx.en: Some parents sign their children up for too many tutoring classes, and by forcing them they make the children hate studying.

ctx.s: 专家认为，用大量补贴逼着新产业快速扩张，无异于{拔苗助长}。
ctx.en: Experts argue that using huge subsidies to force a new industry to expand quickly is no different from pulling up seedlings to make them grow.

bad.s: 他学习很努力，成绩进步得很快，真是{拔苗助长}。
bad.en: (meant: he works hard and his grades improved quickly)
bad.why: It criticises forcing growth in a way that does harm; fast progress that comes naturally is not described this way.

bad.s: 时间不多了，我们得{拔苗助长}，赶快出发。
bad.en: (meant: time is short, we must hurry and set off)
bad.why: It is not a word for hurrying; it describes damaging something by pushing its development too fast.

cards.mean: to start strong and finish weakly
cards.lit: a tiger's head and a snake's tail: a big, bold start and a thin, feeble end

use.how: Predicate, often after 做事 or 总是: 他做事虎头蛇尾。 Criticises a plan, effort or piece of work whose vigorous start is not matched by its finish.

near.diff: 半途而废 means quitting halfway; 虎头蛇尾 stresses the contrast between a grand start and a weak ending, even if something is finished.

cards.cue: A TV series has a gripping first few episodes, but the final episode is rushed and flat. How do viewers describe it?

ctx.s: 他做事总是{虎头蛇尾}，开头声势很大，结尾却草草了事。
ctx.en: He always starts things with a great fanfare and then wraps them up any old how.

ctx.s: 这次的健身计划你宣传得这么热闹，可千万别又{虎头蛇尾}啊。
ctx.en: You've made such a big announcement of this fitness plan; don't let it fizzle out again.

ctx.s: 这部电视剧前几集很精彩，结局却{虎头蛇尾}，观众很失望。
ctx.en: The first episodes of this series were brilliant, but the ending was a letdown and viewers were disappointed.

ctx.s: 老师批评他的作文{虎头蛇尾}：开头写得生动，结尾只有一句话。
ctx.en: The teacher criticised his essay for its weak finish: a vivid opening, and an ending of just one sentence.

ctx.s: 主队上半场踢得很漂亮，下半场却毫无斗志，整场比赛{虎头蛇尾}。
ctx.en: The home team played beautifully in the first half but had no fight left in the second: a strong start and a feeble finish.

ctx.s: “你的报告前面那么详细，后面怎么这么草率？”“时间不够，只好{虎头蛇尾}了。”
ctx.en: "The first part of your report is so detailed, why is the rest so sloppy?" "I ran out of time, so the ending got short-changed."

bad.s: 他从小就{虎头蛇尾}，长得又高又壮。
bad.en: (meant: since childhood he has looked big and strong)
bad.why: It describes how an effort tails off, not a person's build or appearance.

bad.s: 我们还没开始就放弃了，真是{虎头蛇尾}。
bad.en: (meant: we gave up before we even started)
bad.why: The idiom needs a strong start; giving up before beginning has no tiger's head at all.

cards.mean: to accomplish nothing at all
cards.lit: not a single thing achieved

use.how: Predicate about a person over a long stretch of life or work: 到头来一事无成。 Often self-deprecating: 我还一事无成。

near.diff: 半途而废 is about abandoning one task midway; 一事无成 sums up a person's whole record as having achieved nothing.

cards.cue: Looking back on years of drifting between jobs and hobbies, someone sighs that they have nothing to show for any of it.

ctx.s: 我都三十岁了，还{一事无成}。
ctx.en: I'm already thirty and I still haven't achieved anything.

ctx.s: 他整天玩游戏，难怪一年下来{一事无成}。
ctx.en: He plays games all day, so no wonder he has achieved nothing all year.

ctx.s: 父亲常说：做事三心二意，最后只会{一事无成}。
ctx.en: My father often says that if you never commit to anything, you end up accomplishing nothing.

ctx.s: 你已经帮了这么多人，怎么能说自己{一事无成}呢？
ctx.en: You've helped so many people; how can you say you've accomplished nothing?

ctx.s: 他换了很多工作，每份都只做几个月，到头来{一事无成}。
ctx.en: He changed jobs many times, staying only a few months in each, and in the end had nothing to show for it.

ctx.s: 回顾这十年，她不愿承认自己{一事无成}。
ctx.en: Looking back on the past ten years, she refused to admit she had achieved nothing.

bad.s: 他{一事无成}地完成了任务。
bad.en: (meant: he finished the task effortlessly)
bad.why: It means achieving nothing; it cannot describe the manner in which a task was completed.

bad.s: 这家饭店的菜{一事无成}，很难吃。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant's food is a failure)
bad.why: It judges a person's achievements over time, not the quality of things like food.

cards.mean: to fail just short of success
cards.lit: the work falls short by one basket of earth

story.text: When the western Lü people sent King Wu of Zhou a great hound as tribute, a minister warned the king that small indulgences can ruin great virtue. He compared it to building a mound nine ren high: if the work stops one basket of earth short, the mound is never finished and all the labour fails.
story.source: 《尚书·旅獒》：为山九仞，功亏一篑。

use.how: Predicate, often with 最终, 差点 or 别: 千万别功亏一篑。 Said with regret about a long effort that fails at the very last step.

near.diff: 前功尽弃 means all earlier effort is wasted, at any stage; 功亏一篑 stresses failing at the final step, when success was within reach.

cards.cue: After months of work, a team's experiment collapses because of one small slip in the very last step. How do you sum it up?

ctx.s: 只差最后一道题没做对，太可惜了，真是{功亏一篑}。
ctx.en: Only the last question was wrong. What a pity to fall at the final hurdle.

ctx.s: 都坚持到现在了，千万别{功亏一篑}。
ctx.en: You've held on this long; don't fail right at the end.

ctx.s: 他在最后十米被对手超过，{功亏一篑}，只拿了第二名。
ctx.en: He was overtaken in the last ten metres, missed victory by a whisker and came second.

ctx.s: 实验已经做到最后一步，却因为一个小失误而{功亏一篑}。
ctx.en: The experiment had reached its last step, then failed because of one small mistake.

ctx.s: 谈判眼看就要成功，对方突然改变主意，合作{功亏一篑}。
ctx.en: The talks were about to succeed when the other side suddenly changed its mind, and the deal fell through at the last moment.

ctx.s: 教练提醒队员：越到最后越要小心，别让一个月的努力{功亏一篑}。
ctx.en: The coach reminded the team to be most careful at the end, so a month of effort would not be thrown away at the last step.

bad.s: 他刚开始学钢琴就放弃了，真是{功亏一篑}。
bad.en: (meant: he gave up the piano just after starting)
bad.why: It is for failing when success was nearly reached, not for quitting at the beginning.

bad.s: 他{功亏一篑}地考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: he only just got into university)
bad.why: It means failing near the end; it cannot describe succeeding by a narrow margin.

cards.mean: the loss outweighs the gain
cards.lit: what is gained does not make up for what is lost

use.how: Predicate or after 是…的: 这样做得不偿失。 Weighs the cost of an action against its benefit and finds it not worth it.

near.diff: 因小失大 stresses losing something big for a petty gain; 得不偿失 is the general verdict that the cost exceeds the benefit.

cards.cue: Driving across town to a cheaper supermarket saves less money than the petrol costs. What is your verdict on the trip?

ctx.s: 开车去那家超市省下的钱还不够油费，{得不偿失}。
ctx.en: The money saved by driving to that supermarket doesn't even cover the petrol. It's not worth it.

ctx.s: 为了多赚一点加班费天天熬夜，你不觉得{得不偿失}吗？
ctx.en: Staying up every night for a bit of overtime pay: don't you think it costs you more than you gain?

ctx.s: “要不要为这点小事跟邻居吵一架？”“算了，吵起来{得不偿失}。”
ctx.en: "Should I have it out with the neighbours over this little thing?" "Forget it, a fight would cost you more than it's worth."

ctx.s: 他为了赢一场比赛带伤上场，结果休息了半年，实在{得不偿失}。
ctx.en: He played injured to win one match and then had to rest for six months. It really wasn't worth it.

ctx.s: 专家认为，这项工程花费巨大，带来的好处却很少，{得不偿失}。
ctx.en: Experts believe the project costs a fortune and brings few benefits, so the losses outweigh the gains.

ctx.s: 大量使用农药虽然提高了产量，却污染了土地，从长远看是{得不偿失}的。
ctx.en: Heavy pesticide use raised yields but polluted the land; in the long run the cost outweighs the benefit.

bad.s: 这次投资我们赚了很多，真是{得不偿失}。
bad.en: (meant: we made a lot, it was well worth it)
bad.why: It says the loss is greater than the gain, the opposite of a profitable result.

bad.s: 他昨天{得不偿失}了一个钱包。
bad.en: (meant: he lost a wallet yesterday)
bad.why: It is a verdict on a trade-off, not a verb meaning to lose, and it takes no object.

cards.mean: to be dropped quietly without being resolved
cards.lit: to end it by leaving it unended

use.how: Predicate about a matter, case, plan or dispute, often with 最后 or 就这样: 这件事最后不了了之。

near.diff: 虎头蛇尾 is about effort fading after a strong start; 不了了之 is about a matter left unresolved and quietly dropped.

cards.cue: You complained about a broken streetlight many times; nobody fixed it, nobody replied, and eventually everyone stopped mentioning it.

ctx.s: 他们争论了半天，最后也{不了了之}了。
ctx.en: They argued for ages, and in the end the matter was just dropped.

ctx.s: 去年说要修的那条路，后来就{不了了之}了。
ctx.en: The road they promised to repair last year was quietly forgotten.

ctx.s: 你上个月借我的钱，不会就这样{不了了之}吧？
ctx.en: The money you borrowed from me last month: you're not just going to let it quietly disappear, are you?

ctx.s: 投诉了好几次都没人管，这件事只好{不了了之}。
ctx.en: I complained several times and nobody did anything, so I had no choice but to let it drop.

ctx.s: 警方调查了几个月，因为证据不足，案子最终{不了了之}。
ctx.en: Police investigated for months, but for lack of evidence the case was eventually dropped unresolved.

ctx.s: 这类问题如果每次都{不了了之}，以后只会越来越多。
ctx.en: If problems like this are always just left hanging, there will only be more of them.

bad.s: 问题终于{不了了之}，大家都很满意。
bad.en: (meant: the problem was finally settled and everyone was satisfied)
bad.why: It means the matter was dropped without a resolution, not that it was properly solved.

bad.s: 他把作业{不了了之}地写完了。
bad.en: (meant: he finished his homework carelessly)
bad.why: It describes a matter that is left unresolved, not the careless way someone finishes a task.

cards.mean: to try to be clever and make things worse
cards.lit: playing at cleverness turns into clumsiness

use.how: Predicate, often after 结果 or 反而: 他想帮忙，结果弄巧成拙。 About a deliberate clever move, trick or scheme that backfires.

near.diff: 画蛇添足 is spoiling something by adding what is not needed; 弄巧成拙 is any clever trick or scheme that backfires.

cards.cue: To look more experienced at an interview, someone exaggerates their skills, then falls apart under the first follow-up questions.

ctx.s: 他想抄近路，结果迷了路，真是{弄巧成拙}。
ctx.en: He tried to take a shortcut and got lost. His clever idea backfired.

ctx.s: 我本来想给她一个惊喜，没想到{弄巧成拙}，把她吓哭了。
ctx.en: I wanted to surprise her, but it backfired and frightened her to tears.

ctx.s: 小心点，别为了讨好老板耍小聪明，最后{弄巧成拙}。
ctx.en: Be careful: don't play clever tricks to please the boss, or it will backfire on you.

ctx.s: 他在面试时故意夸大自己的经验，被问了几个问题就露了馅，{弄巧成拙}。
ctx.en: He deliberately exaggerated his experience at the interview, was found out after a few questions, and only made things worse.

ctx.s: 这家公司想用超低价吸引顾客，结果被怀疑质量有问题，{弄巧成拙}。
ctx.en: The company tried to attract customers with rock-bottom prices, but people began to suspect the quality, and the ploy backfired.

ctx.s: 他把护照藏在一个“最安全”的地方，后来连自己也找不到，{弄巧成拙}了。
ctx.en: He hid his passport in the 'safest' place, then couldn't find it himself. Too clever by half.

bad.s: 她的手很巧，做的蛋糕总是{弄巧成拙}。
bad.en: (meant: she is skilful and her cakes are always clever creations)
bad.why: It is criticism of a clever attempt that backfires, not praise for skill.

bad.s: 他什么也没做，事情就{弄巧成拙}了。
bad.en: (meant: things went wrong on their own)
bad.why: It needs someone's deliberate clever move; things going wrong by themselves is not this idiom.

cards.mean: to ask for trouble by needlessly making things hard for oneself
cards.lit: to go asking for bitterness to eat

use.how: Predicate, often in 这不是自讨苦吃吗 or 何必自讨苦吃. Said about someone who chooses a hardship they could easily have avoided.

near.diff: 自作自受 blames someone for suffering the results of their own wrongdoing; 自讨苦吃 mocks needlessly choosing hardship or trouble.

cards.cue: Your friend refuses the lift and insists on climbing twenty floors with heavy shopping bags. What do you tell them?

ctx.s: 天这么冷，你还穿这么少，{自讨苦吃}。
ctx.en: It's freezing and you're dressed so lightly. You're asking for trouble.

ctx.s: 明知道吃辣会肚子疼，还点最辣的，这不是{自讨苦吃}吗？
ctx.en: You know spicy food gives you a stomach ache and you still ordered the hottest dish. Aren't you asking for it?

ctx.s: 有电梯不坐，非要爬二十层楼，何必{自讨苦吃}？
ctx.en: Why make life hard for yourself by climbing twenty floors when there's a lift?

ctx.s: 别去惹那个脾气暴躁的经理了，那是{自讨苦吃}。
ctx.en: Don't provoke that hot-tempered manager; you'd only be asking for trouble.

ctx.s: 他同时接下三个项目，累得生了病，朋友都说他{自讨苦吃}。
ctx.en: He took on three projects at once and worked himself sick; his friends all said he brought it on himself.

ctx.s: 有人觉得跑马拉松是{自讨苦吃}，他却乐在其中。
ctx.en: Some people think running marathons is needless self-torture, but he loves it.

bad.s: 他家里很穷，从小就{自讨苦吃}。
bad.en: (meant: his family was poor, so he suffered hardship from childhood)
bad.why: It implies the hardship was chosen needlessly; a child born into poverty did not bring it on himself.

bad.s: 谢谢你为了我{自讨苦吃}。
bad.en: (meant: thank you for taking on hardship for my sake)
bad.why: It mocks foolishly inviting trouble, so it cannot be used to thank someone for a sacrifice.

cards.mean: an unnecessary, pointless move
cards.lit: this one move is superfluous

use.how: Predicate or after 是 / 岂不是: 你这样做是多此一举。 Dismisses an action as unneeded, without saying it does harm.

near.diff: 画蛇添足 says the extra step spoils the result; 多此一举 only says it was unnecessary.

cards.cue: Everything can be done online in two minutes, yet your colleague takes a morning off to queue at the bank in person.

ctx.s: 门已经锁好了，你再检查一遍就是{多此一举}。
ctx.en: The door is already locked; checking it again is pointless.

ctx.s: 他早就知道了，你再去告诉他岂不是{多此一举}？
ctx.en: He already knows. Wouldn't telling him again be unnecessary?

ctx.s: 网上就能办，还专门跑去银行排队，真是{多此一举}。
ctx.en: You can do it online, yet you went all the way to the bank to queue. That was completely unnecessary.

ctx.s: “要不要带把伞？”“天气预报说一整天都是晴天，带伞{多此一举}。”
ctx.en: "Should I take an umbrella?" "The forecast says sunny all day; there's no need."

ctx.s: 有人认为这条规定{多此一举}，但事实证明它很有用。
ctx.en: Some people thought the rule was unnecessary, but it has proved very useful.

ctx.s: 我本来觉得准备备用方案是{多此一举}，没想到真的用上了。
ctx.en: I thought preparing a backup plan was pointless, but in the end we actually needed it.

bad.s: 他帮了我很多忙，真是{多此一举}。
bad.en: (meant: he did a lot to help me)
bad.why: It dismisses an action as pointless, so it cannot express thanks or praise for help.

bad.s: 他{多此一举}地做了两份工作。
bad.en: (meant: he took on an additional job)
bad.why: It judges one move as pointless; it does not mean 'extra' or 'additionally', so it cannot just report that he took a second job.

cards.mean: to worry about imaginary dangers
cards.lit: a man of Qi worries that the sky will fall

story.text: A man in the small state of Qǐ (not the larger state of Qí) was so afraid that the sky would fall and the earth would give way that he could neither sleep nor eat. Someone who was worried about his worrying went to explain that the sky is only gathered air and the earth only piled-up soil, so neither can collapse. The man was relieved and happy.

use.how: Predicate or after 是: 你这是杞人忧天。 Dismisses a worry as groundless; also used modestly of oneself: 也许是我杞人忧天。

near.diff: 庸人自扰 is making trouble for oneself out of nothing, a harsher charge; 杞人忧天 is fretting about a danger that is very unlikely.

cards.cue: Your grandmother is convinced her phone's radiation is damaging her brain and keeps it in a drawer. How do the family gently tease her?

ctx.s: 飞机这么安全，你还担心它掉下来，简直是{杞人忧天}。
ctx.en: Planes are so safe, and you're still afraid it will crash. That's a groundless worry.

ctx.s: 也许是我{杞人忧天}，但我总觉得这个计划有风险。
ctx.en: Maybe I'm worrying over nothing, but I still feel this plan is risky.

ctx.s: 孩子才上幼儿园，你就担心他将来找不到工作，是不是有点{杞人忧天}？
ctx.en: Your child has only just started kindergarten and you're worried he won't find a job. Isn't that a bit of a needless worry?

ctx.s: 奶奶总怕手机辐射伤脑子，我们劝她别{杞人忧天}。
ctx.en: Grandma is always afraid phone radiation will harm her brain, and we tell her not to worry about imaginary dangers.

ctx.s: 有人认为担心人工智能取代人类是{杞人忧天}，也有人不同意。
ctx.en: Some say fearing that AI will replace humans is groundless worry; others disagree.

ctx.s: 事后证明，他当初的担心并不是{杞人忧天}。
ctx.en: Events proved that his worries at the time were not unfounded after all.

bad.s: 明天就要考试了，我还没复习，真是{杞人忧天}。
bad.en: (meant: the exam is tomorrow and I haven't revised, I'm so worried)
bad.why: It calls a worry groundless; this worry is real and justified.

bad.s: 他{杞人忧天}地抬头看着天空。
bad.en: (meant: he looked up at the sky anxiously)
bad.why: It is a judgment that a worry is groundless, not an adverb for looking anxious or a literal look at the sky.

cards.mean: still shaken by a past fright
cards.lit: the heart still holds a lingering fear

use.how: Predicate, often with 至今, 仍 or 想起来还: 想起那件事我还心有余悸。 About fear that lingers long after a dangerous experience.

near.diff: 惊魂未定 is not yet calm right after a shock; 心有余悸 is fear that lingers long afterwards when the event comes to mind.

cards.cue: Years after being trapped in a lift, a woman still feels her chest tighten whenever she steps into one.

ctx.s: 想起那次车祸，我到现在还{心有余悸}。
ctx.en: When I think of that car accident, I still feel shaken even now.

ctx.s: 他小时候被狗咬过，现在看到大狗仍然{心有余悸}。
ctx.en: He was bitten by a dog as a child, and he still feels a flash of fear when he sees a big dog.

ctx.s: 上次在山里迷路的事，你现在想起来还{心有余悸}吗？
ctx.en: That time you got lost in the mountains: does it still frighten you when you think about it?

ctx.s: 经历过那场地震的人，提起当晚的情景都{心有余悸}。
ctx.en: Those who lived through the earthquake still shudder when they talk about that night.

ctx.s: 去年投资亏了很多钱，他至今{心有余悸}，再也不敢炒股了。
ctx.en: He lost a lot of money investing last year, is still rattled by it and won't touch the stock market again.

ctx.s: 她平静地讲完了那段经历，但我看得出她仍然{心有余悸}。
ctx.en: She told the story calmly, but I could see she was still haunted by the fear.

bad.s: 明天第一次坐飞机，我有点{心有余悸}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm nervous about my first flight tomorrow)
bad.why: It is fear left over from a past experience, not nerves about something still to come.

bad.s: 见到多年不见的老朋友，他{心有余悸}，非常高兴。
bad.en: (meant: his heart was full of emotion when he saw his old friend)
bad.why: The lingering feeling is fear after danger, never joy or emotion at a happy reunion.

cards.mean: to have a wildly unrealistic idea
cards.lit: thoughts so strange that one imagines the sky splitting open

use.how: Predicate, often after 是 or 太: 你这个想法太异想天开了。 Also adverbial with 地. Mocks a plan or hope that ignores reality.

near.diff: 杞人忧天 is needless worry about something that will not happen; 异想天开 is an unrealistic hope or plan.
痴心妄想 is harsher and stresses a foolish desire for something one can never get; 异想天开 mocks the idea itself as fantastical.

cards.cue: Your cousin has never cooked a meal, yet plans to open a restaurant next month and be a millionaire by spring. What do you call his plan?

ctx.s: 不复习就想考第一，你别{异想天开}了。
ctx.en: You want to come top without revising? Stop dreaming.

ctx.s: 他想一个月就把英语说得跟母语一样流利，真是{异想天开}。
ctx.en: He wants to speak English as fluently as a native in one month; what a fantasy.

ctx.s: “我打算辞职，靠买彩票养活自己。”“你这也太{异想天开}了吧？”
ctx.en: "I'm going to quit my job and live off lottery tickets." "Isn't that a bit far-fetched?"

ctx.s: 老板{异想天开}地要求我们三天做完一个月的工作。
ctx.en: The boss, with no sense of reality, demanded that we finish a month's work in three days.

ctx.s: 一百年前，很多人觉得人类登上月球是{异想天开}。
ctx.en: A hundred years ago, many people thought humans landing on the moon was a pipe dream.

ctx.s: 这个计划听起来有点{异想天开}，可他还是说服了投资人。
ctx.en: The plan sounded rather fanciful, but he still managed to win over the investors.

bad.s: 他总担心坐飞机会出事，真是{异想天开}。
bad.en: (meant: he always worries the plane will crash, a needless fear)
bad.why: Groundless worry is qǐ rén yōu tiān; this idiom mocks an unrealistic hope or plan, not a fear.

bad.s: 天气预报说明天{异想天开}，会放晴。
bad.en: (meant: the forecast says the sky will clear tomorrow)
bad.why: The opening sky is part of a figure for a fantastical idea; the idiom says nothing about the weather.

cards.mean: to show off one's skill in front of an expert
cards.lit: to swing an axe about at the door of Lu Ban, the master carpenter

story.text: Lu Ban, a craftsman of the state of Lu in the Spring and Autumn period, was so skilled that carpenters came to honour him as the master of their trade. To swing an axe at his door is to show off woodwork in front of the greatest carpenter of all. The Tang writer Liu Zongyuan used the image, saying that to wield an axe at the gate of Ban would take a brazen face.
story.source: 柳宗元《王氏伯仲唱和诗序》

use.how: Most often self-deprecating, before speaking or performing to experts: 我就班门弄斧了。 Also criticises someone who lectures a master.

near.diff: 自以为是 is a general belief that one is always right; 班门弄斧 is a display of skill in front of someone far better at it.

cards.cue: A medical student is asked to say a few words at a conference of senior surgeons and opens with a modest apology. What does she say?

ctx.s: 在您这位书法家面前写字，我真是{班门弄斧}了。
ctx.en: Writing calligraphy in front of a master like you, I'm really showing off before an expert.

ctx.s: 各位都是专家，那我就{班门弄斧}，谈谈自己的一点看法。
ctx.en: You are all experts, so forgive my presumption as I offer a few thoughts of my own.

ctx.s: 他在大厨面前教人怎么切菜，简直是{班门弄斧}。
ctx.en: He was teaching people how to chop vegetables in front of a head chef; talk about showing off before a master.

ctx.s: “你要给钢琴老师弹这首曲子？”“是啊，有点{班门弄斧}，不过是她让我弹的。”
ctx.en: "You're going to play this piece for your piano teacher?" "Yes, it's a bit presumptuous, but she asked me to."

ctx.s: 一个刚学了三个月的新手去纠正教授的发音，这不是{班门弄斧}吗？
ctx.en: A beginner of three months correcting a professor's pronunciation: isn't that showing off before an expert?

ctx.s: 他谦虚地说，在数学系的同事面前讲统计，无异于{班门弄斧}。
ctx.en: He said modestly that talking about statistics in front of colleagues from the maths department was like teaching a master his own trade.

bad.s: 我在一年级小学生面前讲加减法，真是{班门弄斧}。
bad.en: (meant: I was showing off, teaching addition to first-graders)
bad.why: The audience must be experts who know more than the speaker; showing off to beginners is not this idiom.

bad.s: 他是这方面的专家，{班门弄斧}地给我们上了一课。
bad.en: (meant: as an expert, he skilfully taught us a lesson)
bad.why: It never praises an expert's skill; it describes someone lesser displaying skill before a master.

cards.mean: to deceive oneself as well as others
cards.lit: to deceive oneself and deceive others

use.how: Predicate or after 是, takes no object: 这样做是自欺欺人。 Said of pretending an obvious problem is not there.

near.diff: 掩耳盗铃 is a vivid image of hiding from the obvious while doing wrong; 自欺欺人 is the plain statement and is used more widely.
口是心非 is saying one thing while thinking another, deceiving others only; 自欺欺人 means the person is fooling himself too.

cards.cue: A friend hides the unpaid bills in a drawer and tells everyone, himself included, that his shop is doing fine. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 把体重秤藏起来就不胖了吗？别{自欺欺人}了。
ctx.en: Do you think hiding the scales makes you any thinner? Stop kidding yourself.

ctx.s: 公司明明在亏钱，经理却对大家说一切正常，简直是{自欺欺人}。
ctx.en: The company is clearly losing money, yet the manager tells everyone all is well; he's fooling himself as much as us.

ctx.s: “我抄的答案，老师看不出来。”“你这是{自欺欺人}，考试的时候怎么办？”
ctx.en: "I copied the answers; the teacher can't tell." "You're only fooling yourself. What will you do in the exam?"

ctx.s: 他假装没看见那封催款信，用这种{自欺欺人}的办法躲了一个月。
ctx.en: He pretended he hadn't seen the payment reminder, and dodged it for a month by fooling himself like that.

ctx.s: 不去医院检查，就当自己没病，这不是{自欺欺人}吗？
ctx.en: Not getting checked at the hospital and acting as if you're not ill: isn't that just fooling yourself?

ctx.s: 数据造假不过是{自欺欺人}，问题迟早会暴露出来。
ctx.en: Faking the figures only fools yourself along with everyone else; the problem will come out sooner or later.

bad.s: 那个骗子{自欺欺人}，骗走了老人的积蓄。
bad.en: (meant: the swindler cheated the old man out of his savings)
bad.why: A con man who knowingly cheats others is not fooling himself; the idiom needs self-deception about an obvious truth.

bad.s: 他{自欺欺人}了我，说那辆车没出过事故。
bad.en: (meant: he deceived me, saying the car had never been in an accident)
bad.why: It takes no object and is not a verb for deceiving a person; say tā piàn le wǒ.

cards.mean: to theorise without practical experience
cards.lit: to discuss warfare on paper

story.text: Zhao Kuo, son of the Zhao general Zhao She, studied the books of war from youth and argued strategy so well that even his father could not beat him in debate, yet Zhao She did not trust him with an army, saying he spoke of war too lightly. Later, at the battle of Changping against Qin, the king of Zhao replaced the veteran general Lian Po with Zhao Kuo. He changed the existing plans, was surrounded by the Qin army and killed, and the Zhao army was lost.

use.how: Predicate or after 是 / 只是: 这些计划不过是纸上谈兵。 Criticises talk, plans or knowledge never tested in practice.

near.diff: 一知半解 is knowing only part of something; 纸上谈兵 may know the theory well but has never put it into practice.

cards.cue: A new manager has read every leadership book but has never run a team, and his detailed plan falls apart on the first day.

ctx.s: 他自己从没开过车，却总教别人怎么开，真是{纸上谈兵}。
ctx.en: He has never driven himself, yet he's always telling others how to drive; it's all theory.

ctx.s: 只读管理书、不去公司实习，学到的东西不过是{纸上谈兵}。
ctx.en: If you only read management books and never do an internship, what you learn is just theory.

ctx.s: “你的方案看起来不错，试过吗？”“还没有。”“那还只是{纸上谈兵}。”
ctx.en: "Your plan looks good; have you tried it?" "Not yet." "Then it's still just theory."

ctx.s: 计划写得再漂亮，不到现场看看，也是{纸上谈兵}。
ctx.en: However fine the plan looks, if you never visit the site it's just armchair strategy.

ctx.s: 不少球迷在网上{纸上谈兵}，好像比教练还懂战术。
ctx.en: Plenty of fans play armchair general online, as if they understood tactics better than the coach.

ctx.s: 我们不能满足于{纸上谈兵}，必须尽快把想法拿到市场上检验。
ctx.en: We can't be content with theorising; we have to test our ideas in the market as soon as possible.

bad.s: 这位老将军打了几十年仗，最会{纸上谈兵}。
bad.en: (meant: this old general fought for decades and is a master of strategy)
bad.why: It criticises theory with no experience; it cannot praise someone whose skill comes from long practice.

bad.s: 他拿出笔在纸上{纸上谈兵}，写了一篇作文。
bad.en: (meant: he took out a pen and wrote an essay on paper)
bad.why: The paper is figurative; the idiom is not a description of writing or of discussing anything on paper.

cards.mean: to pretend to understand
cards.lit: not understanding, yet pretending to understand

use.how: Predicate, often in advice or warnings: 不懂就问，别不懂装懂。 Said of hiding one's ignorance instead of asking.

near.diff: 一知半解 is honestly knowing only a little; 不懂装懂 is knowingly pretending to understand what one does not.
自以为是 is sincerely believing oneself right; 不懂装懂 knows it does not understand and hides it.

cards.cue: In a meeting full of jargon, a new intern nods at everything, then cannot do the task because he never asked what any of it meant.

ctx.s: 不明白就问老师，别{不懂装懂}。
ctx.en: If you don't understand, ask the teacher; don't pretend you do.

ctx.s: 他明明听不懂，却一直点头，{不懂装懂}。
ctx.en: He clearly couldn't follow, yet kept nodding, pretending he understood.

ctx.s: “这个词你认识吗？”“认识……其实不认识。”“不认识就说嘛，{不懂装懂}有什么用？”
ctx.en: "Do you know this word?" "Yes... actually, no." "Then say so. What's the use of pretending?"

ctx.s: 医生最怕病人{不懂装懂}，自己乱吃药。
ctx.en: What doctors dread most is patients who pretend to know and take medicine on their own.

ctx.s: 刚来公司的时候，我{不懂装懂}，结果把客户的订单弄错了。
ctx.en: When I first joined the company I pretended to understand, and ended up getting a customer's order wrong.

ctx.s: 承认自己不知道并不丢人，{不懂装懂}才让人看不起。
ctx.en: There's no shame in admitting you don't know; it's pretending to know that people look down on.

bad.s: 老师问谁打破了窗户，他{不懂装懂}，说什么都不知道。
bad.en: (meant: asked who broke the window, he played dumb and said he knew nothing)
bad.why: That is the opposite, pretending not to know (zhuāng hú tu); this idiom is pretending to understand.

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我完全{不懂装懂}。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is too hard; I don't understand it at all)
bad.why: It needs pretence; simply not understanding anything is yī qiào bù tōng.

cards.mean: to persevere without letting up
cards.lit: to hold on firmly and never slacken

use.how: Predicate, adverbial with 地, or attribute of 的努力: 坚持不懈地练习。 Praises long, steady effort toward a worthwhile goal.

near.diff: 半途而废 is the opposite: giving up halfway.
再接再厉 urges more effort after a success; 坚持不懈 is steady effort kept up over a long time, success or not.

cards.cue: For six years a woman studies every night after work, fails the bar exam three times and finally passes on the fourth try.

ctx.s: 只要{坚持不懈}，你的中文一定会进步。
ctx.en: As long as you keep at it, your Chinese will definitely improve.

ctx.s: 他每天早上跑步，{坚持不懈}，身体越来越好。
ctx.en: He runs every morning without fail, and his health keeps getting better.

ctx.s: “我已经失败好几次了。”“别灰心，{坚持不懈}才能成功。”
ctx.en: "I've already failed several times." "Don't lose heart; only steady perseverance brings success."

ctx.s: 经过十年{坚持不懈}的努力，她终于开了自己的诊所。
ctx.en: After ten years of unrelenting effort, she finally opened her own clinic.

ctx.s: 科学家们{坚持不懈}地研究，终于找到了新的治疗方法。
ctx.en: The scientists kept up their research tirelessly and finally found a new treatment.

ctx.s: 这位老人几十年来{坚持不懈}地在山上种树，把荒山变成了森林。
ctx.en: For decades this old man planted trees on the hill without letting up, turning the barren slopes into forest.

bad.s: 他{坚持不懈}要我请他吃饭，我只好答应了。
bad.en: (meant: he insisted that I buy him dinner, so I agreed)
bad.why: On its own jiānchí can mean to insist on a demand; this idiom only means persevering at a long effort.

bad.s: 他{坚持不懈}地喝完了一杯水。
bad.en: (meant: he drank up a glass of water)
bad.why: It needs a long, sustained effort over time, not one short ordinary action.

cards.mean: to keep up the good work and do even better
cards.lit: to clash again and sharpen again, like a fighting cock

story.text: The phrase comes from a linked poem about cockfighting written together by the Tang poets Han Yu and Meng Jiao. Describing the birds, it says they clash, sharpen their beaks and go back in again. jiē was the clash and lì (first written with the character for a whetstone) the sharpening; the fighter that returns ever keener became a call to build on success and push on.

use.how: Encouragement after a good result, often from teachers, coaches or leaders: 希望你再接再厉。 Takes no object.

near.diff: 坚持不懈 is steady effort over a long time; 再接再厉 builds on a success just achieved.
精益求精 is refining something already good to make it finer; 再接再厉 is pushing on to the next achievement.

cards.cue: Your team has just won the regional final, and before the national round the coach tells them to keep it up and aim even higher. What does she say?

ctx.s: “老师，我这次进了前十名！”“太棒了，{再接再厉}！”
ctx.en: "Teacher, I made the top ten this time!" "Brilliant, keep it up!"

ctx.s: 你这次考得很好，希望你{再接再厉}。
ctx.en: You did very well in this exam; I hope you'll keep up the good work.

ctx.s: 比赛赢了，教练对队员说：“大家{再接再厉}，争取拿冠军！”
ctx.en: After the win the coach told the players: "Keep it up, everyone, let's go for the title!"

ctx.s: 去年的销售成绩不错，今年我们要{再接再厉}。
ctx.en: Last year's sales were good; this year we need to build on that and do even better.

ctx.s: 领导在会上表扬了我们组，并鼓励大家{再接再厉}。
ctx.en: At the meeting the boss praised our team and encouraged us to keep up the good work.

ctx.s: 首战告捷后，球队{再接再厉}，又连赢了三场。
ctx.en: After winning their opening game, the team kept the momentum going and won three more in a row.

bad.s: 你这次考试作弊被发现了，下次要{再接再厉}。
bad.en: (meant: you were caught cheating; do better next time)
bad.why: It urges someone to build on good work; said after wrongdoing it sounds like encouraging more of it.

bad.s: 他{再接再厉}了自己的工作，升了职。
bad.en: (meant: he kept improving at his job and was promoted)
bad.why: It takes no object and no le like this; say tā zài gōngzuò shang zài jiē zài lì.

cards.mean: to do one's best (without promising success)
cards.lit: to act with all the strength one has

use.how: Predicate, often 我会尽力而为 or 尽力而为就好. A modest promise or reassurance that leaves room for failure.

near.diff: 全力以赴 is an all-out, determined push; 尽力而为 promises effort but quietly admits the result is uncertain.

cards.cue: A friend asks if you can get them a ticket to a sold-out concert. You'll try, but you can't promise anything. What do you reply?

ctx.s: 考试别太紧张，{尽力而为}就好。
ctx.en: Don't get too nervous about the exam; just do your best.

ctx.s: 这件事我不能保证成功，但我会{尽力而为}。
ctx.en: I can't guarantee this will work, but I'll do what I can.

ctx.s: “你能帮我找到那本书吗？”“我{尽力而为}吧，不一定找得到。”
ctx.en: "Can you find that book for me?" "I'll do my best, but I may not find it."

ctx.s: 医生对家属说：“我们会{尽力而为}，但你们也要做好心理准备。”
ctx.en: The doctor told the family: "We will do everything we can, but you should prepare yourselves."

ctx.s: 时间这么紧，老板也只要求大家{尽力而为}，不强求完美。
ctx.en: With time this tight, the boss only asked everyone to do their best, not to be perfect.

ctx.s: 比赛结果谁也说不准，每个人{尽力而为}，问心无愧就行。
ctx.en: Nobody can predict the result; if everyone does their best, we'll have nothing to regret.

bad.s: 为了拿冠军，我们要{尽力而为}，不惜一切代价！
bad.en: (meant: we'll go all out to win the title, whatever it costs)
bad.why: It is a modest hedge; an all-out, whatever-it-takes vow calls for quán lì yǐ fù.

bad.s: 他每天都{尽力而为}这份工作。
bad.en: (meant: every day he does his best at this job)
bad.why: It takes no object; say tā jìnlì zuò hǎo zhè fèn gōngzuò instead.

cards.mean: to progress step by step
cards.lit: to follow the proper order and advance gradually

use.how: Predicate, adverbial with 地, or after 是…的: 学习要循序渐进。 Said of learning, training or reform that moves in stages.

near.diff: 拔苗助长 is the opposite mistake: forcing quick progress and spoiling it.
脚踏实地 is a down-to-earth, practical attitude; 循序渐进 is the gradual order in which progress is made.

cards.cue: A beginner wants to run a marathon next month, but his coach has him start with short jogs and add a little distance each week.

ctx.s: 学外语要{循序渐进}，不能着急。
ctx.en: Learning a foreign language has to go step by step; you can't rush it.

ctx.s: 刚开始健身，运动量应该{循序渐进}地增加。
ctx.en: When you start working out, you should increase the load gradually.

ctx.s: “我能直接学最难的课吗？”“最好还是{循序渐进}，先把基础打好。”
ctx.en: "Can I go straight to the hardest course?" "Better to take it step by step and get the basics right first."

ctx.s: 这本教材从简单到复杂，编排得{循序渐进}。
ctx.en: This textbook moves from easy to hard; it is arranged in a careful progression.

ctx.s: 公司的改革是{循序渐进}的，不会一下子改变所有制度。
ctx.en: The company's reforms are gradual; they won't change every rule at once.

ctx.s: 他想一个月减十公斤，医生劝他减肥也要{循序渐进}。
ctx.en: He wanted to lose ten kilos in a month; the doctor advised him that weight loss too should be gradual.

bad.s: 他学了半年钢琴，进步飞快，真是{循序渐进}。
bad.en: (meant: after half a year of piano he has improved by leaps and bounds)
bad.why: It means slow, orderly progress; rapid leaps are tū fēi měng jìn.

bad.s: 我们在车站{循序渐进}地排队买票。
bad.en: (meant: we queued in order at the station to buy tickets)
bad.why: It is about gradual progress in learning or development, not waiting one's turn in a line (that is àn shùnxù).

cards.mean: able to endure hardship and hard work
cards.lit: to eat bitterness and bear toil

use.how: Describes a person's lasting character, as predicate or in 吃苦耐劳的精神: 他很吃苦耐劳。 Common in references and job adverts.

near.diff: 坚持不懈 is persistence toward one goal; 吃苦耐劳 is a character that bears hard conditions and heavy work without complaint.
千辛万苦 names the hardships themselves; 吃苦耐劳 describes the person able to bear them.

cards.cue: A recruiter describes a candidate who grew up on a farm, works long shifts without complaint and never shirks the dirty jobs.

ctx.s: 这个小伙子{吃苦耐劳}，老板很喜欢他。
ctx.en: This young man is hard-working and tough, and the boss likes him a lot.

ctx.s: 我爷爷年轻时很{吃苦耐劳}，什么活都干过。
ctx.en: When my grandfather was young he could take any hardship; he did every kind of work.

ctx.s: 招聘广告上写着：要求{吃苦耐劳}，能适应经常出差。
ctx.en: The job advert says: must be hard-working, able to cope with frequent travel.

ctx.s: “你觉得自己最大的优点是什么？”“我比较{吃苦耐劳}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think is your greatest strength?" "I'm quite hard-working and don't mind tough conditions."

ctx.s: 靠着{吃苦耐劳}的精神，这家人从一个小摊做成了一家大饭店。
ctx.en: Through sheer hard work and endurance, the family grew a small stall into a big restaurant.

ctx.s: 山区的农民世世代代{吃苦耐劳}，在石头缝里种出了庄稼。
ctx.en: For generations the mountain farmers have toiled through hardship, growing crops in the cracks between rocks.

bad.s: 这道菜太辣了，我{吃苦耐劳}地吃完了。
bad.en: (meant: the dish was too spicy, but I bravely finished it)
bad.why: Its bitterness is figurative hardship; the idiom is a character trait, not putting up with food or one unpleasant moment.

bad.s: 他今天{吃苦耐劳}了八个小时。
bad.en: (meant: he worked hard for eight hours today)
bad.why: It describes a lasting quality of a person and cannot take le and a length of time; say tā jīntiān xīnkǔ gàn le bā gè xiǎoshí.

cards.mean: down-to-earth and steady in one's work
cards.lit: feet treading on solid ground

use.how: Adverbial (脚踏实地地干) or predicate. Praises a practical, steady attitude to work or study, often set against 好高骛远 or 一步登天.

near.diff: 循序渐进 describes a method of going step by step in order; 脚踏实地 describes a person's attitude: practical, honest work, no empty ambitions.
吃苦耐劳 is about enduring hardship; 脚踏实地 is about doing real work instead of chasing what is out of reach.

cards.cue: A new colleague talks big about changing the whole industry but never finishes a single task. What attitude should he learn instead?

ctx.s: 年轻人要{脚踏实地}，少说空话，多干实事。
ctx.en: Young people should keep their feet on the ground: less empty talk, more real work.

ctx.s: 他从普通工人做起，{脚踏实地}干了十年，终于当上了车间主任。
ctx.en: He started as an ordinary worker, put in ten years of solid work, and finally became workshop director.

ctx.s: 老师在评语里写道：该生学习{脚踏实地}，从不好高骛远。
ctx.en: The teacher wrote in the report: this student studies steadily and never aims at things beyond reach.

ctx.s: 光有远大的理想还不够，还得{脚踏实地}地去做。
ctx.en: Having big ideals isn't enough; you also have to get down and do the work.

ctx.s: “创业最需要什么？”“{脚踏实地}，别光想着融资和上市。”
ctx.en: "What does starting a business need most?" "Steady, practical work. Don't just think about raising money and going public."

ctx.s: 这家小店从没做过广告，靠着老板{脚踏实地}的经营，慢慢有了一批老顾客。
ctx.en: The little shop never advertised; through the owner's steady, honest management it gradually built up loyal customers.

bad.s: 他第一次参加比赛就拿了冠军，真是{脚踏实地}。
bad.en: (meant: he won the first contest he entered; how impressive)
bad.why: It praises slow, steady, practical effort over time, not a quick win or natural talent.

bad.s: 我们要{脚踏实地}这份工作。
bad.en: (meant: we must do this job in a practical, steady way)
bad.why: It takes no object; use it as an adverbial or predicate instead: zuò zhè fèn gōngzuò yào jiǎo tà shí dì.

cards.mean: to keep improving what is already good
cards.lit: already refined, yet seeking still more refinement

story.text: In the Analects, Zigong quotes a line from the Book of Songs, 'as if cut, as if filed, as if carved, as if polished', and Confucius praises him. The Song scholar Zhu Xi explained the line: a craftsman working bone or horn cuts it and then files it; one working jade or stone carves it and then polishes it. The work is already fine, yet he seeks to make it finer still. The idiom comes from Zhu Xi's words.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (精益求精的精神). Praises work, craft or service that is already good and still being refined; takes no object.

near.diff: 一丝不苟 is care over every detail of a task; 精益求精 is going on to improve something that is already good.
再接再厉 urges more effort after a success; 精益求精 is about raising the quality of a skill or a piece of work.

cards.cue: A chef's signature dish already wins awards, yet she adjusts the recipe a little every week to make it better still. What attitude does she show?

ctx.s: 我们的产品已经不错了，但还要{精益求精}。
ctx.en: Our product is already good, but we still need to keep improving it.

ctx.s: 这位老师傅做的家具已经是全城最好的，可他还在不断{精益求精}。
ctx.en: The old master's furniture is already the best in town, yet he keeps on refining it.

ctx.s: “这版设计已经很好了，还要改？”“客户要求高，我们得{精益求精}。”
ctx.en: "This design is already very good; you're changing it again?" "The client's standards are high; we have to keep polishing."

ctx.s: 正是这种{精益求精}的工匠精神，让这个品牌闻名世界。
ctx.en: It is exactly this craftsman's drive to keep perfecting things that made the brand world-famous.

ctx.s: 她的演奏已经无可挑剔，可她还想{精益求精}，每天多练两个小时。
ctx.en: Her playing is already flawless, yet she wants to make it better still and practises two extra hours a day.

ctx.s: 酒店的服务一向口碑很好，今年又{精益求精}，推出了十几项改进。
ctx.en: The hotel's service has always been well regarded, and this year it raised the bar again with a dozen improvements.

bad.s: 这份报告错误百出，我们要{精益求精}。
bad.en: (meant: this report is full of errors; we must fix it)
bad.why: It means improving what is already good; a report full of errors simply needs correcting.

bad.s: 我想{精益求精}我的中文。
bad.en: (meant: I want to perfect my Chinese)
bad.why: It takes no object; name the field first instead, as in xué Zhōngwén yào jīng yì qiú jīng.

cards.mean: to handle something with skill and ease
cards.lit: what the heart conceives, the hand answers

story.text: Duke Huan of Qi was reading in his hall when Wheelwright Bian, making a wheel below, asked what he was reading. The words of the sages, said the duke. Then they are only the dregs of the ancients, said Bian. Asked to explain, he spoke of his craft: cut too slowly or too quickly and the wheel is spoiled; getting it just right is felt in the hand and answered in the heart, and he cannot put it into words or pass it even to his son. The idiom grew from this description of skill.

use.how: Predicate, often after 用起来, 做起来 or 越来越: 这把刀用起来很得心应手。 Says a tool, task or skill is handled smoothly, usually after practice; takes no object.

near.diff: 轻而易举 says a task is easy in itself; 得心应手 says the person handles it smoothly thanks to skill, practice or a well-suited tool.
熟能生巧 is the saying that practice brings skill; 得心应手 describes the smooth handling that results.

cards.cue: After two years with the same camera, a photographer changes every setting without looking. How does the camera feel in her hands?

ctx.s: 这支笔我用了很多年，写起字来特别{得心应手}。
ctx.en: I've used this pen for years; writing with it feels completely natural.

ctx.s: 刚开始做这份工作有点紧张，现在已经{得心应手}了。
ctx.en: I was a bit nervous when I started this job, but now I handle it with ease.

ctx.s: “新软件用得惯吗？”“还不太{得心应手}，再练几天就好了。”
ctx.en: "Used to the new software yet?" "Not quite at ease with it; a few more days of practice and I will be."

ctx.s: 他在销售部干了十多年，处理客户投诉早就{得心应手}。
ctx.en: He's been in sales for over ten years; dealing with customer complaints is second nature to him.

ctx.s: 换了一把合适的球拍以后，她打起球来{得心应手}多了。
ctx.en: After switching to a racket that suits her, she plays far more comfortably.

ctx.s: 他第一次当翻译时手忙脚乱，到了第三场会议，已经能{得心应手}地应对各种提问。
ctx.en: At his first interpreting job he was flustered, but by the third meeting he was handling every question with ease.

bad.s: 这道题太简单了，谁做都{得心应手}。
bad.en: (meant: this question is so easy anyone can do it)
bad.why: The ease must come from someone's skill or practice, not from the task being simple; for a simple task say qīng ér yì jǔ.

bad.s: 他很{得心应手}电脑。
bad.en: (meant: he is good with computers)
bad.why: It takes no object; say that using the computer comes easily to him: tā yòng diànnǎo hěn dé xīn yìng shǒu.

cards.mean: to do something perfunctorily to get it over with
cards.lit: to go through the motions and be done with the matter

use.how: Predicate, often after 不能, 别 or 只是: 工作不能敷衍了事。 Criticises doing a task with minimal effort just to finish it; takes no object.

near.diff: 粗心大意 is carelessness by inattention; 敷衍了事 is deliberately doing the minimum to get a task off one's hands.

cards.cue: A repairman paid to fix your heater glances at it for two minutes, tightens one screw and leaves. It breaks again that night. How did he do the job?

ctx.s: 作业要认真写，不能随便写几个字就{敷衍了事}。
ctx.en: Do your homework properly; you can't scribble a few words just to get it over with.

ctx.s: 这么重要的检查，他居然{敷衍了事}，难怪出了问题。
ctx.en: He just went through the motions on such an important inspection; no wonder things went wrong.

ctx.s: “这份总结也写得太短了吧？”“时间太紧，只好{敷衍了事}。”
ctx.en: "Isn't this summary far too short?" "Time was too tight, so I just got it done any old way."

ctx.s: 顾客投诉了三次，客服每次都{敷衍了事}，问题始终没有解决。
ctx.en: The customer complained three times; each time customer service brushed it off, and the problem was never solved.

ctx.s: 领导强调，安全检查必须一项一项做，绝不允许走过场、{敷衍了事}。
ctx.en: The manager stressed that safety checks must be done item by item; going through the motions just to finish is never allowed.

ctx.s: 那家装修公司为了赶工期{敷衍了事}，墙面没多久就开始掉皮。
ctx.en: To meet the deadline the renovation company did a slapdash job, and before long the walls began to peel.

bad.s: 他{敷衍了事}地完成了任务，受到了经理的表扬。
bad.en: (meant: he got the task done smoothly and the manager praised him)
bad.why: It is always criticism of half-hearted work, never a neutral 'got it done', so it cannot earn praise.

bad.s: 他总是{敷衍了事}他的女朋友。
bad.en: (meant: he always fobs off his girlfriend)
bad.why: The idiom takes no object and is about tasks; to fob off a person, use the plain verb fūyǎn with the person as its object.

cards.mean: to work together as one
cards.lit: hearts aligned, strength joined

use.how: Adverbial before a verb (大家齐心协力，把……) or predicate. Describes several people pulling together toward one goal.

near.diff: 一心一意 is one person's undivided devotion; 齐心协力 needs a group working together.
全力以赴 is putting all of one's own effort in; 齐心协力 is about many people joining their efforts.

cards.cue: A landslide blocked the village's only road, so every family sent someone with a shovel, and by evening the road was clear. How did they manage it?

ctx.s: 只要大家{齐心协力}，这个问题一定能解决。
ctx.en: As long as we all pull together, this problem can definitely be solved.

ctx.s: 全班同学{齐心协力}，在拔河比赛中拿了第一名。
ctx.en: The whole class pulled together and won first place in the tug-of-war.

ctx.s: “这么多箱子，今天搬得完吗？”“我们几个{齐心协力}，没问题。”
ctx.en: "So many boxes; can we move them all today?" "If the few of us work together, no problem."

ctx.s: 公司上下{齐心协力}，只用三个月就完成了全年的销售任务。
ctx.en: Everyone in the company, top to bottom, worked as one and hit the whole year's sales target in just three months.

ctx.s: 这个项目能成功，离不开团队每个成员的{齐心协力}。
ctx.en: The project's success depended on every team member working together.

ctx.s: 夫妻俩{齐心协力}，把一家小面馆经营成了连锁店。
ctx.en: Working side by side, the couple turned a small noodle shop into a chain.

bad.s: 他一个人{齐心协力}地写完了整篇论文。
bad.en: (meant: he wrote the whole thesis by himself with total dedication)
bad.why: It needs several people; for one person's dedication use yī xīn yī yì or quán lì yǐ fù.

bad.s: 我们俩{齐心协力}，都喜欢看电影。
bad.en: (meant: we are of one mind; we both love films)
bad.why: It means joining efforts on a task, not sharing tastes; for shared tastes simply say your hobbies are the same.

cards.mean: double the result with half the effort
cards.lit: half the work, double the achievement

story.text: Mencius told his disciple Gongsun Chou that their own age was the best moment for a ruler to govern by benevolence: the people were suffering under harsh rule and would welcome relief like someone freed from hanging upside down. So, he said, a ruler who did half of what the ancients did would surely achieve twice as much; only at such a time was this so.

use.how: Predicate, often after a condition with 就能 or 会: 方法对了，学习就能事半功倍。 Says a method or condition makes effort pay off far more. Its reverse is 事倍功半.

near.diff: 一举两得 is one action bringing two separate gains; 事半功倍 is one goal reached with far less effort.
事倍功半 is the exact reverse: twice the effort for half the result. Learners often swap the two.

cards.cue: A student stops memorising words at random, starts learning them in families by shared root, and remembers three times as many in the same hour. What has the new method done?

ctx.s: 学习方法对了，就能{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: With the right study method, you get far more out of less effort.

ctx.s: 用这个软件处理数据，可以说是{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: Processing the data with this software, you could say, doubles the output for half the work.

ctx.s: “怎么才能把单词背得快一点？”“先把词根弄清楚，会{事半功倍}。”
ctx.en: "How can I memorise words faster?" "Get the roots clear first; it will save you a lot of effort."

ctx.s: 好的工具能让工作{事半功倍}，所以这笔钱花得值。
ctx.en: Good tools make work far more efficient, so this money was well spent.

ctx.s: 先找准目标客户再去推销，往往{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: Pinning down your target customers before you start selling usually pays off far better.

ctx.s: 老师常说，与其熬夜苦读，不如睡足了再学，那样才能{事半功倍}。
ctx.en: The teacher always says it's better to sleep well and then study than to cram all night; that way the effort goes much further.

bad.s: 我花了一整天才做完这么一点，真是{事半功倍}。
bad.en: (meant: a whole day's work for so little result)
bad.why: That is the reverse, shì bèi gōng bàn; this idiom means less effort and a bigger result.

bad.s: 他是一个{事半功倍}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is an efficient person)
bad.why: It describes a method or condition paying off, not a person's character; to call someone efficient, talk about their xiàolǜ.

cards.mean: to have a clear plan in mind beforehand
cards.lit: to have the whole bamboo already in one's chest

story.text: The Song painter Wen Tong, also called Wen Yuke, was famous for his bamboo. His friend Su Shi wrote that to paint bamboo one must first have the complete bamboo in one's mind; then, brush in hand, gaze until the image appears and chase it at once without stopping, like a falcon swooping the instant a hare breaks cover, for if you hesitate it is gone.
story.source: 苏轼《文与可画筼筜谷偃竹记》

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (胸有成竹地说). Describes someone calm and confident because they already know how they will handle what is coming; takes no object.

near.diff: 有备无患 is a maxim that preparation prevents trouble; 胸有成竹 describes a person's confident state of mind about a plan already formed.
深思熟虑 is the process of thinking something over carefully; 胸有成竹 is the calm confidence of already knowing what to do.

cards.cue: Before a big negotiation everyone is nervous except the lead negotiator, who smiles because she already knows every step she will take. How does she look?

ctx.s: 看他{胸有成竹}的样子，这次考试肯定准备得很好。
ctx.en: From how confident he looks, he must have prepared well for this exam.

ctx.s: 面试官问了很多难题，她都{胸有成竹}地一一回答了。
ctx.en: The interviewers asked many hard questions, and she answered each one with calm assurance.

ctx.s: “明天的演讲准备好了吗？”“放心吧，我早就{胸有成竹}了。”
ctx.en: "Are you ready for tomorrow's speech?" "Don't worry, I've had it all worked out for ages."

ctx.s: 教练对下半场早有安排，一点也不着急，显得{胸有成竹}。
ctx.en: The coach had the second half planned long ago; he wasn't worried at all and looked completely sure of himself.

ctx.s: 对装修方案他早就{胸有成竹}，连每个房间的颜色都想好了。
ctx.en: He had the renovation plan clear in his head long ago, right down to the colour of every room.

ctx.s: 大家还在争论该从哪里下手，老王已经{胸有成竹}地拿出了一份完整的计划。
ctx.en: While everyone was still arguing about where to start, Lao Wang calmly produced a complete plan.

bad.s: 我对明天的考试一点准备都没有，但还是{胸有成竹}。
bad.en: (meant: I haven't prepared at all, but I feel confident anyway)
bad.why: The confidence must rest on a plan already formed; blind confidence without preparation is a contradiction.

bad.s: 我{胸有成竹}这个计划。
bad.en: (meant: I'm sure about this plan)
bad.why: It takes no object; introduce the plan with duì: wǒ duì zhège jìhuà xiōng yǒu chéng zhú.

cards.mean: to satisfy both sides at once
cards.lit: both sides made whole, both made good

use.how: Predicate or attributive, often 两全其美的办法: 这是个两全其美的办法。 Describes a solution that satisfies two needs or parties that seemed to conflict; takes no object.

near.diff: 一举两得 is one action bringing two gains; 两全其美 resolves a conflict so that neither side has to lose.
十全十美 means perfect in every way; 两全其美 only means two competing needs are both met.

cards.cue: Your parents want you home for the holidays and your boss needs you working, so you arrange to work remotely from your parents' house. What kind of solution is it?

ctx.s: 有没有{两全其美}的办法？
ctx.en: Is there a way to keep both sides happy?

ctx.s: 孩子没人照顾，工作又不能停，公司让我在家办公，真是{两全其美}。
ctx.en: No one could look after the kids and work couldn't stop, so the company let me work from home; both needs were met.

ctx.s: “我想去旅游，又不想花太多钱。”“那就去附近的小城，{两全其美}。”
ctx.en: "I want to travel, but I don't want to spend much." "Then go to a small town nearby; that covers both."

ctx.s: 公司让员工自己选上班时间，老板和员工都满意，可谓{两全其美}。
ctx.en: The company lets staff choose their own hours; bosses and staff are both satisfied, the best of both worlds.

ctx.s: 世上哪有那么多{两全其美}的事，总得放弃一样。
ctx.en: How often can you have it both ways? You always have to give something up.

ctx.s: 两家都想在自己家乡办婚礼，最后决定两地各办一场，总算{两全其美}。
ctx.en: Both families wanted the wedding in their own hometown; in the end they held one in each place, and everyone was satisfied.

bad.s: 他长得帅，学习也好，真是{两全其美}。
bad.en: (meant: he is handsome and a good student too)
bad.why: It describes a solution that meets two competing needs, not a person with two good qualities.

bad.s: 这个办法{两全其美}了我们俩。
bad.en: (meant: this plan satisfied both of us)
bad.why: It takes no object; it describes the plan itself, as in zhège bànfǎ liǎng quán qí měi.

cards.mean: to make a good thing even better
cards.lit: to add embroidered flowers to brocade

use.how: Predicate or object of 是, 算是: 这对他来说是锦上添花。 Says an extra makes something already good even better; often contrasted with 雪中送炭.

near.diff: 雪中送炭 is help for someone in trouble; 锦上添花 is an extra for someone or something already doing well.
画龙点睛 is the one key touch that brings the whole to life; 锦上添花 is a pleasant extra on top of what is already complete.

cards.cue: A company already had its best year ever, and then in December it won a big new contract as well. What did the contract do for its year?

ctx.s: 这道菜本来就很好吃，撒点香菜更是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: The dish was already delicious; a sprinkle of coriander makes it even better.

ctx.s: 他工作稳定，收入也不错，这次升职对他来说是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: He has a stable job and a good income; this promotion is just the icing on the cake.

ctx.s: “房子都装修好了，还要买画吗？”“挂几幅画，算是{锦上添花}吧。”
ctx.en: "The flat is all done up; do we still need to buy paintings?" "A few on the wall would be a nice extra."

ctx.s: 比赛已经赢定了，最后这个进球只是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: The match was already won; that last goal was just a bonus.

ctx.s: 有钱的大公司不缺赞助，捐给它们只是{锦上添花}，不如帮帮山区的小学校。
ctx.en: Rich big companies don't lack sponsors; giving to them only adds to plenty, so better to help small schools in the mountains.

ctx.s: 婚礼已经很热闹了，朋友们又准备了一场烟花表演，真是{锦上添花}。
ctx.en: The wedding was already lively, and then friends put on a fireworks show, which made it even better.

bad.s: 他失业后交不起房租，朋友借给他一笔钱，真是{锦上添花}。
bad.en: (meant: a friend's loan helped him when he lost his job)
bad.why: Help for someone in trouble is xuě zhōng sòng tàn; this idiom is an extra for something already good.

bad.s: 文章已经很好了，他又加了一段废话，结果{锦上添花}，反而变差了。
bad.en: (meant: he added a needless paragraph and spoiled it)
bad.why: It means the addition made things better; an addition that spoils the result is huà shé tiān zú.

cards.mean: to add the finishing touch that brings it to life
cards.lit: to paint a dragon and dot in its eyes

story.text: Zhang Sengyou, a painter of the Liang dynasty, painted four dragons on the walls of Anle Temple in Jinling but left out their eyes, saying that if he painted them the dragons would fly away. People thought he was boasting and pressed him to do it. He dotted in the eyes of two: at once thunder and lightning broke the wall, and the two dragons rode the clouds up into the sky. The two without eyes are still there.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (画龙点睛之笔, 起到画龙点睛的作用). Praises one key word, line or detail that brings a whole piece of writing, speech or design to life.

near.diff: 锦上添花 is a pleasant extra on top of what is already good; 画龙点睛 is the small key touch without which the whole would stay flat.
画蛇添足 is the opposite: an addition that was not needed and spoils the whole.

cards.cue: An essay is solid but flat, until the writer adds one striking closing sentence that makes the whole piece hit home. What did that sentence do?

ctx.s: 文章最后一句写得很好，起到了{画龙点睛}的作用。
ctx.en: The essay's last sentence is excellent; it is the finishing touch that brings the whole thing to life.

ctx.s: 这条红围巾是整套衣服的{画龙点睛}之笔。
ctx.en: This red scarf is the touch that makes the whole outfit come alive.

ctx.s: “标题还要改吗？”“要改，好标题能{画龙点睛}。”
ctx.en: "Do we still need to change the title?" "Yes. A good title can bring the whole piece to life."

ctx.s: 设计师只在白墙上挂了一幅小画，却有{画龙点睛}的效果，整个客厅一下子有了生气。
ctx.en: The designer hung just one small painting on the white wall, yet it made all the difference; the living room suddenly came alive.

ctx.s: 主持人最后那句总结{画龙点睛}，把整场讨论的意思都说透了。
ctx.en: The host's closing summary was the perfect final touch, bringing out the point of the whole discussion.

ctx.s: 这部电影的配乐很简单，却在几个关键镜头里{画龙点睛}。
ctx.en: The film's score is simple, but in a few key scenes it is exactly what brings them to life.

bad.s: 他的演讲本来就很长，最后又加了半小时，真是{画龙点睛}。
bad.en: (meant: his long speech dragged on another half hour)
bad.why: An addition that drags on or spoils is huà shé tiān zú; this idiom praises a small key touch that makes the whole better.

bad.s: 这家店的菜很好吃，结账时还送了一瓶饮料，真是{画龙点睛}。
bad.en: (meant: the free drink at the end was a nice bonus)
bad.why: A bonus on top is jǐn shàng tiān huā; this idiom needs one small key detail that brings a whole work to life.

cards.mean: to advance by leaps and bounds
cards.lit: to dash forward and fly, to charge ahead fiercely

use.how: Predicate or attributive, about a level, skill or field that has suddenly improved: 他的中文水平突飞猛进；取得了突飞猛进的发展。

near.diff: 日新月异 is a constant stream of new things (technology, a city); 突飞猛进 is a sudden big rise in someone's or something's level.

cards.cue: After a summer of practising every day, your friend plays the piano far better than she did in spring. How has her playing improved?

ctx.s: 他这学期中文水平{突飞猛进}，连老师都很惊讶。
ctx.en: His Chinese leapt forward this term; even his teacher was surprised.

ctx.s: 请了私人教练以后，她的网球技术{突飞猛进}。
ctx.en: After she hired a private coach, her tennis came on in leaps and bounds.

ctx.s: “你最近的成绩{突飞猛进}啊！”“我每天都在图书馆复习。”
ctx.en: "Your grades have shot up lately!" "I've been revising in the library every day."

ctx.s: 这家小公司近几年{突飞猛进}，已经成了行业里的领头羊。
ctx.en: This small company has grown by leaps and bounds in recent years and now leads its industry.

ctx.s: 近年来，新能源汽车技术取得了{突飞猛进}的发展。
ctx.en: In recent years, new-energy vehicle technology has made enormous strides.

ctx.s: 那几年，这个国家的经济{突飞猛进}，人们的收入翻了几倍。
ctx.en: In those years the country's economy surged ahead, and people's incomes multiplied several times over.

bad.s: 他最近不好好学习，成绩{突飞猛进}地下降。
bad.en: (meant: his grades have dropped sharply)
bad.why: It only describes rapid progress and improvement; it cannot describe something getting worse or falling.

bad.s: 他开车{突飞猛进}，差点撞到人。
bad.en: (meant: he drives recklessly fast)
bad.why: It is about progress, not physical speed or reckless movement.

cards.mean: being prepared means nothing to fear
cards.lit: have preparation, have no misfortune

story.text: After the state of Jin made peace with the Rong tribes and the other states rallied to it, the state of Zheng sent the Duke of Jin a gift of musicians and war chariots. Duke Dao of Jin offered half the musicians to his minister Wei Jiang, who had guided this policy. Wei Jiang declined, quoted the Book of Documents, "in safety, think of danger", and added: if you think of danger you will prepare, and if you are prepared, no disaster will come.

use.how: Usually a short clause giving the reason for a precaution: 带把伞吧，有备无患。 Also 做到有备无患, 以求有备无患.

near.diff: 有备无患 is advice to prepare for what might happen; 万无一失 claims a plan or arrangement cannot go wrong.

cards.cue: The forecast says sunny, but your mother still slips an umbrella into your bag and tells you why. What does she say?

ctx.s: 天气预报说可能下雨，带把伞吧，{有备无患}。
ctx.en: The forecast says it might rain; take an umbrella, just in case.

ctx.s: 出国旅行前多准备一些常用药，{有备无患}嘛。
ctx.en: Pack some common medicines before you travel abroad; better safe than sorry.

ctx.s: “只是爬个小山，还要带这么多水？”“{有备无患}，万一迷路呢。”
ctx.en: "It's only a small hill; why so much water?" "Better to be prepared. What if we get lost?"

ctx.s: 她每次面试前都把可能的问题过一遍，她说这叫{有备无患}。
ctx.en: Before every interview she goes over the likely questions; she calls it being prepared.

ctx.s: 家里最好准备一个应急包，放上手电筒和饮用水，以求{有备无患}。
ctx.en: It's best to keep an emergency kit at home with a torch and drinking water, so you are ready for anything.

ctx.s: 各地应提前做好防汛准备，真正做到{有备无患}。
ctx.en: All regions should prepare for floods in advance so that they are truly ready.

bad.s: 我昨天没复习，结果考试{有备无患}。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't revise, but the exam went fine)
bad.why: It means being prepared; it cannot describe an outcome, least of all one where you did not prepare.

bad.s: 这个计划{有备无患}，绝对不会失败。
bad.en: (meant: this plan is foolproof)
bad.why: It gives the reason for taking a precaution; it does not claim that a plan cannot possibly fail.

cards.mean: after careful deliberation
cards.lit: to think deeply and consider until the thought is ripe

use.how: Mostly after 经过 or as an attributive, about a serious decision reached after long thought: 经过深思熟虑，我决定……；深思熟虑的结果。

near.diff: 犹豫不决 is failing to make up one's mind; 深思熟虑 is thinking a matter through and then deciding.

cards.cue: Your friend spent two months weighing whether to leave her job, then calmly announced her choice. How did she reach it?

ctx.s: 经过{深思熟虑}，我决定辞职去读研究生。
ctx.en: After careful thought, I've decided to quit and go to graduate school.

ctx.s: 这不是一时冲动，是我{深思熟虑}后的决定。
ctx.en: This isn't a whim; it's a decision I thought through carefully.

ctx.s: “你真的想好了要搬去外地？”“放心，我是{深思熟虑}过的。”
ctx.en: "Are you really sure about moving away?" "Don't worry, I've thought it through."

ctx.s: 他说话很慢，每句话好像都经过了{深思熟虑}。
ctx.en: He speaks slowly, as if every sentence has been carefully weighed.

ctx.s: 这样重大的投资，必须{深思熟虑}，不能草率决定。
ctx.en: An investment this big needs careful deliberation; it can't be decided hastily.

ctx.s: 这份方案显然是{深思熟虑}的结果，每个细节都考虑到了。
ctx.en: This proposal is clearly the product of careful thought; every detail has been considered.

bad.s: 我{深思熟虑}了一下，觉得中午吃面条吧。
bad.en: (meant: I thought about it for a moment and chose noodles for lunch)
bad.why: It is for weighty decisions after long thought; a moment's thought about lunch makes it absurd.

bad.s: 我很想家，每天晚上都{深思熟虑}地想念妈妈。
bad.en: (meant: I miss my mother deeply every night)
bad.why: It is about weighing a decision carefully, not about longing for or thinking fondly of someone.

cards.mean: unable to make up one's mind
cards.lit: hesitating and not deciding
