use.how: Predicate or attributive, about a person stuck between choices: 他一直犹豫不决；别再犹豫不决了。 Often mildly critical.

near.diff: 优柔寡断 is an indecisive character; 犹豫不决 is being undecided about a particular choice right now.

cards.cue: In the shop, your friend keeps picking up one phone, then the other, for an hour without choosing either. What state is he in?

ctx.s: 两件衣服都很好看，她站在镜子前{犹豫不决}。
ctx.en: Both dresses looked good, and she stood in front of the mirror unable to choose.

ctx.s: 别再{犹豫不决}了，机会可不等人。
ctx.en: Stop dithering; opportunities don't wait for anyone.

ctx.s: “你到底去不去？”“我还在{犹豫不决}，明天告诉你。”
ctx.en: "Are you going or not?" "I still can't make up my mind; I'll tell you tomorrow."

ctx.s: 他对要不要接受这份工作一直{犹豫不决}，结果错过了截止日期。
ctx.en: He couldn't decide whether to accept the job and ended up missing the deadline.

ctx.s: 看着菜单上几十道菜，我{犹豫不决}，最后让朋友帮我点。
ctx.en: Faced with dozens of dishes on the menu, I couldn't decide, so I let my friend order for me.

ctx.s: 面对两所大学的录取通知，他{犹豫不决}了整整一个星期。
ctx.en: With offers from two universities, he wavered for a whole week.

bad.s: 他{犹豫不决}地答应了我们的邀请。
bad.en: (meant: he accepted our invitation hesitantly)
bad.why: It means not deciding at all, so it cannot describe how someone agreed; say he hesitated a little before agreeing.

bad.s: 这个问题很{犹豫不决}，大家讨论了很久。
bad.en: (meant: this question is hard to decide)
bad.why: It describes a person who cannot decide, not the issue; say the question is hard to decide.

cards.mean: without the slightest hesitation
cards.lit: not hesitating in the slightest

use.how: Adverbial before a verb, usually with 地: 他毫不犹豫地答应了。 Describes one quick, firm action or choice.

near.diff: 不假思索 is acting or answering without thinking at all; 毫不犹豫 is acting firmly, with no doubt about what to do.

cards.cue: When her old friend asked for help moving house, she said yes before he had even finished asking. How did she answer?

ctx.s: 看到孩子掉进水里，他{毫不犹豫}地跳了下去。
ctx.en: Seeing the child fall into the water, he jumped in without a moment's hesitation.

ctx.s: 老板给了她一个出国的机会，她{毫不犹豫}地答应了。
ctx.en: Her boss offered her a chance to work abroad, and she accepted at once.

ctx.s: “如果再选一次，你还会学医吗？”“会，我会{毫不犹豫}地再选一次。”
ctx.en: "If you could choose again, would you still study medicine?" "Yes, I'd choose it again without hesitation."

ctx.s: 医生说手术有风险，她还是{毫不犹豫}地在同意书上签了字。
ctx.en: The doctor said the operation was risky, but she signed the consent form without hesitating.

ctx.s: 另一家公司开出高薪挖他，他{毫不犹豫}地拒绝了。
ctx.en: Another company offered him a big salary to poach him, and he turned it down flat.

ctx.s: 只要朋友有需要，他总是{毫不犹豫}地伸出援手。
ctx.en: Whenever a friend needs him, he always helps without a second thought.

bad.s: 他想了三天，最后{毫不犹豫}地决定了。
bad.en: (meant: after three days of thought, he made a firm decision)
bad.why: Three days of thinking is hesitation, which contradicts the idiom; say he finally made up his mind.

bad.s: 他很{毫不犹豫}，做事从不拖泥带水。
bad.en: (meant: he is a decisive person)
bad.why: It is an adverbial for a single action and cannot be modified by a degree word like 'very' as a character trait; say he is decisive.

cards.mean: to know when to stop
cards.lit: stop when it is just enough

use.how: Predicate, usually advice or a warning: 玩笑要适可而止。 Said of drinking, joking, criticising, playing, anything that harms when overdone.

near.diff: 见好就收 is quitting while you are ahead after a gain; 适可而止 is not overdoing something.

cards.cue: Everyone laughed at your first joke about Li's haircut, but you keep making more and he is getting upset. What should you have done?

ctx.s: 酒可以喝，但要{适可而止}。
ctx.en: Drinking is fine, but know when to stop.

ctx.s: 开玩笑要{适可而止}，你看他都快生气了。
ctx.en: Don't push the joke too far; look, he's about to get angry.

ctx.s: “再玩一局吧！”“{适可而止}吧，明天还要上班呢。”
ctx.en: "One more round!" "Let's call it a night; we have work tomorrow."

ctx.s: 批评孩子要{适可而止}，说得太多反而没用。
ctx.en: When you scold a child, don't overdo it; too much talking only backfires.

ctx.s: 减肥是好事，但节食也应该{适可而止}，别把身体搞坏了。
ctx.en: Losing weight is good, but don't take dieting too far and ruin your health.

ctx.s: 双方争论了很久，主持人提醒大家{适可而止}。
ctx.en: The two sides had argued for a long time, and the host reminded everyone to leave it there.

bad.s: 我的作业做到一半就{适可而止}，明天再做。
bad.en: (meant: I stopped my homework halfway and will finish tomorrow)
bad.why: It means not overdoing something that harms in excess, not pausing an unfinished task.

bad.s: 这场雨下了一天，终于{适可而止}了。
bad.en: (meant: the rain finally stopped after a whole day)
bad.why: It implies a person's judgment and self-control; it is not used for things that simply stop.

cards.mean: completely safe, with no chance of failure
cards.lit: in ten thousand tries, not a single miss

use.how: Predicate, or after 确保/力求/为了, about a plan, arrangement or safety measure: 这样就万无一失了；为了万无一失……

near.diff: 万无一失 says a plan cannot go wrong; 有备无患 is the reason for preparing in case something does.

cards.cue: Before the product launch, the manager checks every detail three times because she wants to be absolutely sure nothing can go wrong. What does she want?

ctx.s: 我在两个地方都放了备用钥匙，这样就{万无一失}了。
ctx.en: I've left spare keys in two places, so nothing can go wrong now.

ctx.s: 婚礼的每个细节我们都检查了三遍，应该{万无一失}。
ctx.en: We've checked every detail of the wedding three times; it should be foolproof.

ctx.s: “你觉得这个计划怎么样？”“听起来不错，但不一定{万无一失}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think of the plan?" "Sounds good, but it's not necessarily foolproof."

ctx.s: 为了{万无一失}，他又把文件备份到了另一台电脑上。
ctx.en: To be completely safe, he backed the files up onto another computer as well.

ctx.s: 这次手术风险很高，医生们反复讨论，力求{万无一失}。
ctx.en: The operation was high-risk, so the doctors discussed it again and again to leave nothing to chance.

ctx.s: 世界上没有{万无一失}的投资，任何投资都有风险。
ctx.en: There's no such thing as a risk-free investment; every investment carries risk.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜{万无一失}，每道都好吃。
bad.en: (meant: every dish in this restaurant is good)
bad.why: It is about a plan or arrangement being safe from failure, not praise for quality.

bad.s: 我{万无一失}地准备了考试。
bad.en: (meant: I prepared thoroughly for the exam)
bad.why: It is not a manner adverb for how you prepared; say you prepared thoroughly so that nothing could go wrong.

cards.mean: extremely urgent, imminent
cards.lit: pressing right up against the eyebrows and eyelashes

use.how: Predicate or attributive, about a deadline, problem or task that is very close and pressing: 考试迫在眉睫；迫在眉睫的问题。

near.diff: 燃眉之急 is a noun for the urgent need itself (解燃眉之急); 迫在眉睫 describes how close and pressing something is.

cards.cue: It is Friday night, your thesis is due on Monday morning, and the conclusion is still unwritten. How close is the deadline?

ctx.s: 考试{迫在眉睫}，他却还在玩游戏。
ctx.en: The exam is just around the corner, and he's still playing games.

ctx.s: 离交论文只剩两天，截止日期已经{迫在眉睫}。
ctx.en: Only two days left before the paper is due; the deadline is right on top of us.

ctx.s: “你还不着急吗？”“当然急，比赛已经{迫在眉睫}了。”
ctx.en: "Aren't you worried yet?" "Of course I am; the match is almost here."

ctx.s: 老城区的水管已经严重老化，全面更换{迫在眉睫}。
ctx.en: The water pipes in the old town are badly worn, and replacing them all is now urgent.

ctx.s: 随着人口老龄化加剧，养老问题变得{迫在眉睫}。
ctx.en: As the population ages, the question of elderly care has become pressing.

ctx.s: 公司的资金只够维持一个月，寻找新投资人成了{迫在眉睫}的任务。
ctx.en: The company has only a month's funding left, so finding new investors has become an urgent task.

bad.s: 他是一个{迫在眉睫}的人，做什么都很急。
bad.en: (meant: he is an impatient person)
bad.why: It describes an approaching event or problem, never a person's character; say he is impatient.

bad.s: 我昨天{迫在眉睫}地赶到了机场。
bad.en: (meant: I rushed to the airport yesterday)
bad.why: It is not an adverb for hurrying; it says something urgent is close at hand. Say you rushed to the airport.

cards.mean: changing fast with each passing day
cards.lit: new every day, different every month

use.how: Predicate or attributive, about technology, a city or the times constantly renewing: 科技日新月异；日新月异的变化。 Not used of a person's skills.

near.diff: 突飞猛进 is a sudden rise in a level or skill; 日新月异 is a continuing stream of new things replacing old ones.
翻天覆地 is one total transformation compared with before; 日新月异 is change that keeps coming, day after day.

cards.cue: Every few months there is a new phone, a new app, a new gadget, and last year's model already looks old. How is technology changing?

ctx.s: 现在的手机{日新月异}，去年的新款今年就过时了。
ctx.en: Phones change so fast now that last year's new model is already out of date.

ctx.s: 这座城市{日新月异}，每次回来都能看到新的高楼。
ctx.en: This city changes constantly; every time I come back there are new tower blocks.

ctx.s: “你还在用这个老软件？”“没办法，技术{日新月异}，我跟不上。”
ctx.en: "You're still using this old software?" "I can't help it; technology changes so fast I can't keep up."

ctx.s: 在这个{日新月异}的时代，我们必须不断学习新知识。
ctx.en: In this fast-changing age, we have to keep learning new things.

ctx.s: 网上的流行语{日新月异}，父母常常听不懂孩子在说什么。
ctx.en: Internet slang changes so fast that parents often can't understand what their kids are saying.

ctx.s: 通了高铁以后，这个小镇的面貌{日新月异}。
ctx.en: Since the high-speed railway arrived, the little town has been changing with every passing day.

bad.s: 我的汉语水平{日新月异}，老师很满意。
bad.en: (meant: my Chinese is improving fast)
bad.why: It is for things that keep renewing, like technology or a city; for one person's rapidly rising level, use an idiom of leaps and bounds.

bad.s: 他今天的心情{日新月异}，一会儿高兴一会儿难过。
bad.en: (meant: his mood keeps swinging today)
bad.why: It describes renewal and progress, not fickle ups and downs; say his mood is changeable.

cards.mean: sweeping, earth-shaking (change)
cards.lit: to turn the sky over and overturn the earth

use.how: Mostly attributive in 发生了翻天覆地的变化, comparing a place, life or system with how it was before. Also a predicate: 变化翻天覆地.

near.diff: 日新月异 is change that keeps coming day after day; 翻天覆地 is a total transformation, the before and after unrecognisable.

cards.cue: When your grandmother was young her village had dirt roads and no electricity; now it has paved streets, shops and internet. How has it changed?

ctx.s: 这些年，我的家乡发生了{翻天覆地}的变化。
ctx.en: My hometown has changed beyond recognition over these years.

ctx.s: 有了孩子以后，他们的生活发生了{翻天覆地}的变化。
ctx.en: Once they had a baby, their lives were turned completely upside down.

ctx.s: “你们村现在怎么样？”“变化可大了，跟以前比真是{翻天覆地}。”
ctx.en: "How is your village these days?" "It's changed enormously; compared with before, it's a whole new world."

ctx.s: 互联网给人们的购物方式带来了{翻天覆地}的改变。
ctx.en: The internet has completely transformed the way people shop.

ctx.s: 新老板上任后进行了{翻天覆地}的改革，几乎所有部门都重组了。
ctx.en: The new boss carried out a sweeping overhaul; almost every department was reorganised.

ctx.s: 那场大病之后，他对金钱和家庭的看法发生了{翻天覆地}的转变。
ctx.en: After that serious illness, his views on money and family were completely turned around.

bad.s: 我把桌子挪了一下，房间{翻天覆地}了。
bad.en: (meant: I moved the desk and the room looks different)
bad.why: It is for sweeping, total change; a small rearrangement makes it absurd unless meant as a joke.

bad.s: 科技每天都{翻天覆地}，新产品层出不穷。
bad.en: (meant: technology changes every day)
bad.why: It is one total transformation, not continual daily novelty, which needs an idiom of constant renewal.

cards.mean: never changing; rigid
cards.lit: once formed, it does not change

story.text: The Book of Rites, discussing punishment, explains that a penalty carried out on the body is final: once it is done it cannot be changed or undone. For that reason, it says, a ruler must give his whole mind to a case before passing sentence. The phrase 'once formed, it cannot be changed' later came to describe anything fixed and never altered.

use.how: Attributive or predicate, very often negated: 计划不是一成不变的。 Said of one rule, plan or habit staying fixed over time.

near.diff: 千篇一律 says many works or things are all alike; 一成不变 says one thing stays the same over time.

cards.cue: Your manager tells the team the project schedule can be adjusted if circumstances change; it was never meant to be set in stone. What does she say about the plan?

ctx.s: 计划不是{一成不变}的，可以根据情况调整。
ctx.en: The plan isn't fixed; it can be adjusted as things develop.

ctx.s: 他每天的生活{一成不变}：上班、下班、睡觉。
ctx.en: His days never change: go to work, come home, sleep.

ctx.s: 世界上没有{一成不变}的事物。
ctx.en: Nothing in the world stays the same forever.

ctx.s: “这条规定能改吗？”“规定也不是{一成不变}的，我们可以讨论。”
ctx.en: "Can this rule be changed?" "Rules aren't set in stone either; we can discuss it."

ctx.s: 这家餐厅的菜单十年来{一成不变}，老顾客却越来越少。
ctx.en: The restaurant's menu hasn't changed in ten years, and its regulars keep dwindling.

ctx.s: 用{一成不变}的眼光看待孩子，是很多父母的误区。
ctx.en: Seeing a child through a fixed, unchanging lens is a mistake many parents make.

bad.s: 这些新房子的样子{一成不变}，看起来都一样。
bad.en: (meant: the new houses all look the same)
bad.why: It means one thing staying the same over time; many things that all look alike call for the idiom meaning 'formulaic'.

bad.s: 他把计划{一成不变}了。
bad.en: (meant: he froze the plan)
bad.why: It describes a state and cannot take an object or the ba construction; say instead that the plan stayed unchanged.

cards.mean: to keep up with the times
cards.lit: to advance together with the times

use.how: Predicate, often after 要 or 需要: 教育要与时俱进。 Said of people, institutions or ideas that update themselves to fit the present; also used playfully.

near.diff: 日新月异 describes things themselves changing fast; 与时俱进 praises someone actively adapting to change.

cards.cue: Your seventy-year-old grandmother now pays for everything by phone and sends voice messages to the family group. How do you praise her for not falling behind?

ctx.s: 奶奶现在也用手机付款了，真是{与时俱进}啊！
ctx.en: Grandma pays by phone now too. She really moves with the times!

ctx.s: 学校的教材应该{与时俱进}，不能总用老内容。
ctx.en: School textbooks should be updated, not stuck with the same old content.

ctx.s: “你怎么也开始做短视频了？”“要{与时俱进}嘛。”
ctx.en: "Since when do you make short videos?" "Got to keep up with the times."

ctx.s: 一家公司如果不能{与时俱进}，很快就会被市场淘汰。
ctx.en: A company that can't keep up with the times will soon be pushed out of the market.

ctx.s: 这家老字号在保留传统味道的同时，也在包装上{与时俱进}。
ctx.en: While keeping its traditional flavour, the old brand has modernised its packaging.

ctx.s: 法律条文需要{与时俱进}，才能应对网络时代的新问题。
ctx.en: Laws need to evolve with the times to deal with the new problems of the internet age.

bad.s: 时间{与时俱进}，转眼就到年底了。
bad.en: (meant: time flies; it's suddenly the end of the year)
bad.why: It means adapting to a new era, not time passing by; to say time flies, simply say time passes quickly.

bad.s: 他的病情{与时俱进}，越来越严重了。
bad.en: (meant: his illness got worse over time)
bad.why: It is praise for adapting to the present, not something growing worse as time goes on.

cards.mean: to see someone in a new, better light
cards.lit: to rub one's eyes and look at someone again

story.text: Lü Meng, a general of Wu, was a soldier with little learning until Sun Quan urged him to read. Later the statesman Lu Su visited him, talked with him and was astonished at how much he now knew, saying he was no longer the old Lü Meng of Wu. Lü Meng replied that when a scholar has been away for three days, you should rub your eyes and look at him anew.
story.source: 《三国志·吴书·吕蒙传》裴松之注引《江表传》

use.how: Usually 让/令人刮目相看 or 对某人刮目相看: 他的进步让大家刮目相看。 Said when someone once underrated shows real improvement.

near.diff: 另眼相看 is treating someone specially, better or worse; 刮目相看 is raising your opinion after someone has improved.

cards.cue: The quiet intern everyone overlooked gave the best presentation of the quarter, and the whole team now thinks of her differently. How do you describe their reaction?

ctx.s: 他这次考了全班第一，老师都对他{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: He came top of the class this time, and even the teachers saw him differently.

ctx.s: 半年不见，你的中文进步这么大，真让人{刮目相看}！
ctx.en: Half a year and your Chinese has improved so much. I'm impressed!

ctx.s: “你会做饭了？”“别小看我，今天就让你{刮目相看}。”
ctx.en: "You can cook now?" "Don't underestimate me. Today you'll see me in a new light."

ctx.s: 这支没人看好的球队连赢三场，令所有人{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: The team nobody rated won three in a row and made everyone think again.

ctx.s: 她暗下决心：总有一天要让那些看不起她的人{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: She quietly vowed that one day the people who looked down on her would have to think again.

ctx.s: 这家小公司凭一款新产品打开了市场，让同行{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: With one new product the small company broke into the market, and its rivals took notice.

bad.s: 他一直都是最优秀的学生，大家对他{刮目相看}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone admires him)
bad.why: It needs a change of opinion after improvement; it is not plain admiration for someone always at the top.

bad.s: 他偷了东西以后，邻居们都对他{刮目相看}。
bad.en: (meant: after the theft the neighbours saw him differently)
bad.why: It only means seeing someone in a better light, never a worse one.

cards.mean: monotonously alike, formulaic
cards.lit: a thousand pieces of writing, all to one pattern

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 这些电影千篇一律。 Criticises many works, designs or products that all follow the same dull pattern.

near.diff: 大同小异 simply says things are mostly alike; 千篇一律 complains that they are all the same and boring.
一成不变 is one thing never changing over time; 千篇一律 is many things all made to one formula.

cards.cue: You watched five new romantic comedies this month and every one had the same plot, the same jokes and the same ending. How do you complain about them?

ctx.s: 这些网红餐厅的装修{千篇一律}，没什么特色。
ctx.en: These trendy restaurants all have the same décor; none has any character.

ctx.s: 为什么现在的城市看起来都{千篇一律}？
ctx.en: Why do cities all look the same these days?

ctx.s: 学生的作文开头{千篇一律}，都是“今天天气很好”。
ctx.en: The students' essays all open the same way: "The weather was nice today."

ctx.s: 评委说：“你们的设计太{千篇一律}了，能不能有点新意？”
ctx.en: The judge said: "Your designs are all so formulaic. Can't you show something new?"

ctx.s: 很多求职信内容{千篇一律}，招聘人员看两行就放下了。
ctx.en: So many cover letters read the same that recruiters put them down after two lines.

ctx.s: 景点卖的纪念品{千篇一律}，到哪儿都是一样的钥匙扣和明信片。
ctx.en: The souvenirs at tourist spots are all alike: the same key rings and postcards everywhere.

bad.s: 我和我的双胞胎哥哥长得{千篇一律}。
bad.en: (meant: my twin brother and I look exactly alike)
bad.why: It criticises many works or products sharing one dull formula; two people who look alike are simply exactly the same.

bad.s: 我们的产品质量{千篇一律}，每一件都很好。
bad.en: (meant: our products are consistently high quality)
bad.why: It is a complaint about dull sameness, never praise for consistent quality.

cards.mean: completely different
cards.lit: as sharply apart as if cut, not the same

use.how: Predicate or attributive, often with 和/与……: 两人的性格截然不同。 Contrasts two things that differ sharply.

near.diff: 大相径庭 is more bookish and mostly said of views, results or expectations; 截然不同 fits any sharp contrast.

cards.cue: Two sisters grew up in the same house, but one is loud and adventurous and the other quiet and cautious. How do you describe their personalities?

ctx.s: 这对双胞胎的性格{截然不同}，一个外向，一个内向。
ctx.en: The twins have completely different personalities: one outgoing, one introverted.

ctx.s: 南方和北方的早餐习惯{截然不同}。
ctx.en: Breakfast habits in the south and the north are entirely different.

ctx.s: “电影和原著一样吗？”“不一样，两者的结局{截然不同}。”
ctx.en: "Is the film like the book?" "No, the two endings are completely different."

ctx.s: 同一件事，从不同角度看，可能会得出{截然不同}的结论。
ctx.en: Look at the same event from different angles and you may reach opposite conclusions.

ctx.s: 搬到乡下以后，他过上了和以前{截然不同}的生活。
ctx.en: After moving to the countryside he lived a life utterly unlike his old one.

ctx.s: 两家公司对远程办公的态度{截然不同}：一家鼓励，一家禁止。
ctx.en: The two companies take opposite views of remote work: one encourages it, the other bans it.

bad.s: 这件衣服和那件有点{截然不同}。
bad.en: (meant: this shirt is a bit different from that one)
bad.why: It already means utterly different, so it cannot be softened with 'a bit'; just say the two are a little different.

bad.s: 他{截然不同}了自己的想法。
bad.en: (meant: he completely changed his mind)
bad.why: It describes a contrast between two things and cannot take an object; say he completely changed his mind.

cards.mean: evenly matched, about equal
cards.lit: neither one above nor below the other

use.how: Predicate with two compared subjects, or 跟……不相上下: 两人的成绩不相上下。 Said of ability, level, quality or amount.

near.diff: 势均力敌 is for opposing sides in a fight or contest; 不相上下 compares the level of any two things.

cards.cue: Two job candidates have nearly identical experience and interview scores, and the manager cannot say which one is stronger. How does she describe them?

ctx.s: 他们俩的中文水平{不相上下}。
ctx.en: Their Chinese is about the same level.

ctx.s: “你和你哥谁更高？”“我们俩{不相上下}，差不多一样高。”
ctx.en: "Who's taller, you or your brother?" "We're about even, pretty much the same height."

ctx.s: 这两款手机的价格和性能都{不相上下}，很难选。
ctx.en: The two phones are about equal in price and performance, so it's hard to choose.

ctx.s: 这次期末考试，两个班的平均分{不相上下}。
ctx.en: In this term's final exams, the two classes' average scores were about the same.

ctx.s: 论做菜的手艺，她跟她妈妈已经{不相上下}了。
ctx.en: When it comes to cooking, she's now every bit as good as her mother.

ctx.s: 两位候选人的经验{不相上下}，最后是面试决定了结果。
ctx.en: The two candidates had equal experience, so in the end the interview decided it.

bad.s: 这两种颜色{不相上下}，我分不清。
bad.en: (meant: the two colours look the same and I can't tell them apart)
bad.why: It compares which of two is higher or better, not how alike they look; colours you can't tell apart simply look the same.

bad.s: 他{不相上下}地打量着我。
bad.en: (meant: he looked me up and down)
bad.why: Despite its 'up and down' characters, it is a predicate comparing two parties, never an adverb for how someone looks at you.

cards.mean: just right, to exactly the right degree
cards.lit: reaching exactly the right point

use.how: Predicate, or complement after 得: 盐放得恰到好处。 Praises an amount, degree or timing that is exactly right.

near.diff: 适可而止 advises stopping before going too far; 恰到好处 praises something that hit the right degree.

cards.cue: The chef added just enough chili to give the soup warmth without burning your mouth. How do you praise the seasoning?

ctx.s: 这道菜咸淡{恰到好处}。
ctx.en: This dish is seasoned just right.

ctx.s: “这件衣服大小怎么样？”“{恰到好处}，不松也不紧。”
ctx.en: "How's the size?" "Just right, not loose and not tight."

ctx.s: 她的妆化得{恰到好处}，自然又精神。
ctx.en: Her make-up is just right: natural and fresh.

ctx.s: 演讲中他开的那个玩笑{恰到好处}，一下子让气氛轻松了。
ctx.en: His joke in the speech was perfectly judged and instantly relaxed the room.

ctx.s: 老师的批评{恰到好处}，既指出了问题，又没伤他的自尊。
ctx.en: The teacher's criticism struck the right balance: it named the problem without hurting his pride.

ctx.s: 这部电影的配乐用得{恰到好处}，从不抢画面的风头。
ctx.en: The film's score is used just right and never upstages the pictures.

bad.s: 我昨天的考试{恰到好处}，考了满分。
bad.en: (meant: I did perfectly in yesterday's exam)
bad.why: It praises a degree that is neither too much nor too little, not an outstanding result.

bad.s: 我们{恰到好处}在车站遇见了老同学。
bad.en: (meant: we happened to run into an old classmate at the station)
bad.why: It is a predicate praising the right degree, not an adverb meaning 'by chance'; for that, use a plain word for 'happen to'.

cards.mean: very few, hardly any
cards.lit: sparse and scattered, not even a few

use.how: Predicate, said of countable people or things: 来的人寥寥无几。 Stresses how few there are, often with disappointment.

near.diff: 屈指可数 can stress rarity with respect (few true experts); 寥寥无几 simply stresses how sparse something is.
微不足道 says something is too small to matter; 寥寥无几 counts how few people or things there are.

cards.cue: On a rainy Monday morning the huge shopping mall has only a handful of shoppers wandering around. How do you describe the crowd?

ctx.s: 下大雨了，街上的行人{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: It's pouring, and there's hardly anyone on the street.

ctx.s: “报名的人多吗？”“{寥寥无几}，才三四个。”
ctx.en: "Have many signed up?" "Hardly any, just three or four."

ctx.s: 讲座开始时，台下的听众{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: When the lecture began, there were only a handful of people in the audience.

ctx.s: 新店门口冷冷清清，进去的顾客{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: The new shop is deserted; hardly any customers go in.

ctx.s: 到了深夜，还亮着灯的窗户已经{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: By late night only a few windows were still lit.

ctx.s: 这种老手艺，如今会做的人已经{寥寥无几}了。
ctx.en: Hardly anyone today still knows this old craft.

bad.s: 我杯子里的水{寥寥无几}了。
bad.en: (meant: there's hardly any water left in my cup)
bad.why: It counts people or things, not an uncountable amount like water; just say there isn't much left.

bad.s: 他的贡献{寥寥无几}，没人注意到。
bad.en: (meant: his contribution was too small to notice)
bad.why: It counts how few people or things there are; a contribution too small to matter calls for the idiom meaning 'trivial'.

cards.mean: too trivial to be worth mentioning
cards.lit: so slight it is not worth speaking of

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 一点微不足道的小事。 Said of something small or unimportant, often modestly about one's own help.

near.diff: 无关紧要 says something does not affect the outcome; 微不足道 says it is too small or slight to be worth mentioning.

cards.cue: Thanked on stage for organising the charity event, a volunteer insists that her part was tiny compared to everyone else's. How does she put it modestly?

ctx.s: 这点钱对他来说{微不足道}。
ctx.en: That bit of money means nothing to him.

ctx.s: “谢谢你帮我！”“一点{微不足道}的小忙，不用客气。”
ctx.en: "Thanks for helping me!" "It was a tiny favour, don't mention it."

ctx.s: 跟大家的努力相比，我做的事情{微不足道}。
ctx.en: Compared with everyone's effort, what I did hardly counts.

ctx.s: 在宇宙面前，人类显得多么{微不足道}啊！
ctx.en: Before the universe, how insignificant humans seem!

ctx.s: 别小看这些{微不足道}的细节，客户往往就是因为它们才选择我们。
ctx.en: Don't dismiss these tiny details; clients often choose us because of them.

ctx.s: 调查发现，一个看似{微不足道}的小错误造成了很大的损失。
ctx.en: The investigation found that a seemingly trivial mistake caused heavy losses.

bad.s: 他是公司里{微不足道}的人物，每个决定都要经过他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a key figure; every decision goes through him)
bad.why: It means trivial, the opposite of what was meant; someone every decision must pass through is an influential figure.

bad.s: 来参加聚会的人{微不足道}，只有三个。
bad.en: (meant: very few people came to the party)
bad.why: It says something is too slight to matter, not that a number is small; for very few guests use the idiom meaning 'hardly any'.

cards.mean: holding a pivotal position; very influential
cards.lit: one lift of the foot tips the weight one way or the other

story.text: In the wars that followed the fall of Wang Mang, Dou Rong held the Hexi region in the northwest, between rival powers. Liu Xiu, Emperor Guangwu of Han, wrote to him that with Gongsun Shu holding Shu and Wei Ao holding Tianshui, and Shu and Han at war, the decision lay with Dou Rong: whichever way he lifted his foot, left or right, would tip the balance. Dou Rong chose to side with Han.

use.how: Mostly 举足轻重的人物/地位/作用 or 在……中举足轻重. Said of a person, group or factor whose weight can decide an outcome.

near.diff: 至关重要 says something is crucial to get right; 举足轻重 says someone or something has the weight to sway the outcome.

cards.cue: In a tight committee vote, everyone knows the one undecided member will settle the result, so both sides are courting her. How do you describe her vote?

ctx.s: 他在公司里是个{举足轻重}的人物。
ctx.en: He's a very influential figure in the company.

ctx.s: “这个项目谁说了算？”“李经理的意见{举足轻重}，先问他吧。”
ctx.en: "Who has the final say on this project?" "Manager Li's opinion carries the most weight, so ask him first."

ctx.s: 她的一票在这次投票中{举足轻重}。
ctx.en: Her single vote could decide this ballot.

ctx.s: 父母的态度在孩子选专业时往往{举足轻重}。
ctx.en: Parents' attitudes often weigh heavily when a child chooses a major.

ctx.s: 这座港口在国际贸易中起着{举足轻重}的作用。
ctx.en: This port plays a pivotal role in international trade.

ctx.s: 作为行业里{举足轻重}的大公司，它的一举一动都受到关注。
ctx.en: As one of the industry's most influential companies, its every move is watched.

bad.s: 这件事{举足轻重}，大家不用太在意。
bad.en: (meant: this matter is trivial, don't worry about it)
bad.why: It means carrying great weight, the opposite of trivial, so it clashes with telling people not to worry about it.

bad.s: 他{举足轻重}地走进了会议室。
bad.en: (meant: he walked into the meeting room with heavy steps)
bad.why: Despite the foot in it, it describes influence, not the way someone walks, and is never used as an adverb of manner.
